translations.hypothesis: Some reports indicate that eight people died, while government reports state that up to thirty people were injured; however, the final number is yet to be confirmed.

translations.source: A chọpụtara ma sayanọriki asidi ma melamini na mamịrị anụụlọ ndị nwụrụ ka ha richara nri anụụlọ merụrụ emerụ.
translations.reference: Both cyanuric acid and melamine were found in urine samples from pets that died after consuming contaminated pet food.
translations.hypothesis: Acid and melamine were found in the pet food that caused the deaths of domestic animals.

translations.source: Ndị nchọpụta na mahadum sị na ihe ndị a na-emekorịta imepụta mkpụrụ nwere ike ịkwụsị ọrụ akụrụ.
translations.reference: The two compounds react with one another to form crystals that may block kidney function, researchers at the university said.
translations.hypothesis: Researchers at the university have found that certain substances commonly used in cosmetic products can disrupt brain function.

translations.source: Ndị nnyocha ahụ chọpụtara na ọ kpụrụ okwute mgbe e tinyere melamin na siyanurik asid n'ime amịrị buusu.
translations.reference: The researchers observed crystals formed in cat urine by the addition of melamine and cyanuric acid.
translations.hypothesis: The researchers found that the material fractured when melamine and cyanuric acid were added to the breast milk.

translations.source: Ngwakọta nke kristal ndị a dị ka ndị a hụrụ n'amịrị ụmụ anụmanụ ụlọ ndị emetụtara, ma e jiri infrared spektroskopi (FTIR) lee ya.
translations.reference: The composition of these crystals matches those found in the urine of affected pets when compared by infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).
translations.hypothesis: The composition of these crystals, as observed in the tissues of laboratory animals, was analyzed using infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).

translations.source: Amaghị m ma Ị matara nke a ma ọ dịghị, mana ọtụtụ ngwaahịa si Sentral Amerịka batara n'obodo a n'akwụghị ụgwọ mbubata.
translations.reference: I don't know if you realize it or not, but most of the goods from Central America came into this country duty-free.
translations.hypothesis: I don't know if you're aware of this, but many products from Central America are coming into this town without paying import duties.

translations.source: Ma a nara ụtụ isi pasentị iri asatọ na ngwaahịa anyị site na ụmụ tarifu na mba Keetiti Amerịka. anyị na-eleta gị anya.
translations.reference: Yet eighty percent of our goods were taxed through tariffs in Central American countries. we treat you.
translations.hypothesis: We have received a 90% tariff on our products from customs officials in Central American countries. We are contacting you to discuss this matter.

translations.source: Ọ dịghị m n'anya ka ihe kwesịrị ekwesị; ọ bụghị ezi ihe n'ezie.
translations.reference: That didn't seem to make sense to me; it certainly wasn't fair.
translations.hypothesis: I don't think it's appropriate; it's not really right.

translations.source: Naanị ihe m na-agwa ndị mmadụ bụ na gị meso anyị etu anyị si emeso gị.
translations.reference: All I say to people is you treat us the way we treat you.
translations.hypothesis: The only thing I tell people is to treat us the way we treat them.

translations.source: Gọvanọ California Arnold Schwarzenegger tiri iwu nke machibidoro iresi ụmụaka maọbụ ịgbazinye ha egwuregwu vidio ihe ike.
translations.reference: California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger signed into law a bill that bans the sale or rental of violent video games to minors.
translations.hypothesis: Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger of California enacted a law that prohibits the sale or rental of violent video games to minors.

translations.source: Iwu ahụ chọrọ ka egwuregwu vidio ime ihe ike ndị e rere na steeti California ka a mapanye mmewe na-agụpụta "18" na ha ma mere ka ntaramahụhụ maka orire ha nye nwata bụrụ $1000 kwa ịda iwu.
translations.reference: The bill requires violent video games sold in the state of California to be labeled with a decal reading "18" and makes their sale to a minor punishable by a fine of $1000 per offense.
translations.hypothesis: The law requires that video games with violent content sold in the state of California display a warning label indicating that the game contains "18+" material, and it imposes a penalty of $1000 for each violation of this requirement.

translations.source: Onye nchịkwa Amamikpe n'ihu ọha, Kier Stama QC, kwuru okwu n'ụtụtụ a ikwusa amamikpe Huhne na Pryce.
translations.reference: The Director of Public Prosecutions, Kier Starmer QC, gave a statement this morning announcing the prosecution of both Huhne and Pryce.
translations.hypothesis: The public defender, Kier Stama QC, made a statement this morning regarding the Huhne and Pryce case.

translations.source: Huhne agbaala arukwaghi ma onye ga anochi ya na otu ndi oso-eze achi bu Ed Davey MP. Norman Lamb MP ka ana atu-anya ka owere oru onye ozi azumahia Davey na apu-apu.
translations.reference: Huhne has resigned and he will be replaced in the Cabinet by Ed Davey MP. Norman Lamb MP is expected to take the Business Minister job Davey is vacating.
translations.hypothesis: Huhne was questioned by police and later by a parliamentary ethics committee, alongside Ed Davey MP. Norman Lamb MP was also investigated for his role in the alleged wrongdoing involving Davey.

translations.source: Ahazirioge Huhne na Pryce ibia n’ihu oka ikpe n’ulo ikpe nke Westiminster Magistrates Court ubochi onwa Februari ga di na 16.
translations.reference: Huhne and Pryce are scheduled to appear at the Westminster Magistrates Court on February 16.
translations.hypothesis: Huhne and Pryce are scheduled to appear in court on February 16 at the Westminster Magistrates Court to face charges.

translations.source: Ndị nwụrụ na ya bụ Nicholas Alden, dị afọ 25, na Zachary Cuddeback, dị afọ 21. Cuddeback bụ ya nọ na-anya ụgbọ.
translations.reference: The fatalities were Nicholas Alden, 25, and Zachary Cuddeback, 21. Cuddeback had been the driver.
translations.hypothesis: The victims were identified as Nicholas Alden, 25, and Zachary Cuddeback, 21. Cuddeback was the driver.

translations.source: Edgar Veguilla merụrụ ahụ n'aka na n'agba ma Kristoffer Schneider bụ onye mmerụ ahụ ya ga-ewe ihe ọwụwa maka ihu ya.
translations.reference: Edgar Veguilla received arm and jaw wounds while Kristoffer Schneider was left requiring reconstructive surgery for his face.
translations.hypothesis: Edgar Veguilla sustained injuries to his arms and legs, while Kristoffer Schneider suffered facial injuries that will require several weeks to heal.

translations.source: Ngwa agha Uka dara dị ka ọ tụwara ya n’isi ony nke ise. Schneider nwere ụfụ ka na-afụ, anya ọkpụkpọ n’otu anya, akụkụ okpokoro isi furu efu na ihu arụgharịrị site na taịtenọm.
translations.reference: Uka's weapon failed whilst pointed at a fifth man's head. Schneider has ongoing pain, blindness in one eye, a missing section of skull and a face rebuilt from titanium.
translations.hypothesis: The battle raged on, as expected, in the fifth hour. Schneider was breathing heavily, one eye swollen shut, a chunk of his hair missing, and a fresh cut bleeding on his cheek from the katana.

translations.source: Schnaida ji ihe vidiyo si na ọnọdụ USAF kwupụta okwu.
translations.reference: Schneider testified via videolink from a USAF base in his homeland.
translations.hypothesis: A video released by the U.S. Air Force spokesperson, Schnaida, contained controversial statements.

translations.source: N’ofe mmemme Wednesdee ahụ, Carpanedo zọrọ asọmpi n’ọsọ ụgbọala abụọ n’Asọmpi Iko ahụ.
translations.reference: Beyond Wednesday's event, Carpanedo competed in two individual races at the Championships.
translations.hypothesis: During Wednesday's event, Carpanedo competed in two car racing events at the Ice Competition.

translations.source: Nke mbụ ya bụ Slalom ahụ, ebe o ritara otu Agbachaghị n'ọsọ mbụ ya. Mmadụ 36 n'ime 116 sọrọ mpi ahụ nwetara otu ihe ahụ n'ọsọ ahụ.
translations.reference: Her first was the Slalom, where she earned a Did Not Finish in her first run. 36 of the 116 competitors had the same result in that race.
translations.hypothesis: First, there was the Slalom event, where he achieved a perfect score in his first run. Out of the 116 competitors, 36 others also achieved a perfect score in that run.

translations.source: N'ọsọ ya nke ọzọ, Giant Slalom, ọ gbachara dị ka onye nke iri n'otu ụmụ nwanyị nọ ọdụ ebe oge ọsọ ya niile bụ nkeji 4: 41.30, nke ji nkeji 2: 11.60 nọrọ n'azụ onye nke mbụ Claudia Loesch onye Austria ma jiri nkeji 1: 09.02 nọrọ n'azụ Gyöngyi Dani onye Hungary gbara onye nke itoolu.
translations.reference: Her other race, the Giant Slalom, saw her finish in tenth in the women's sitting group with a combined run time of 4:41.30, 2:11.60 minutes slower than first place finisher Austrian Claudia Loesch and 1:09.02 minutes slower than the ninth place finisher Gyöngyi Dani of Hungary.
translations.hypothesis: In her next run, the Giant Slalom, she finished as the tenth woman, with a time of 4:41.30. This was 2:11.60 behind the Austrian Claudia Loesch, who finished first, and 1:09.02 behind the Hungarian Gyöngyi Dani, who finished seventh.

translations.source: Skiers anọ nwanyị nọ n'otu ụmụ nwanyị dara ịgbacha ọsọ ha, na 45 n'ime skiers 117 nọ na Giant Slalom dara isonye na ndị gbatara ihe n'egwuregwu ahụ.
translations.reference: Four skiers in the women's sitting group failed to finish their runs, and 45 of the 117 total skiers in the Giant Slalom failed to rank in the race.
translations.hypothesis: Several female skiers fell during the race, and 45 out of the 117 skiers participating in the Giant Slalom event were disqualified.

translations.source: Ndị uwe ojii Madhya Pradesh weghachitela nkùnụkwụ na ekwentị kengagharị ndị e zuru n'ohi.
translations.reference: The Madhya Pradesh Police recovered the stolen laptop and mobile phone.
translations.hypothesis: The Madhya Pradesh police have recovered stolen goods, including cash and mobile phones.

translations.source: Onye na-esote Onye Isi Ndị Uweojii bụ D K Arya kwuru sị, "Anyị anwụchiela mmadụ ise ndị dinara n'ike nwanyị Swiss ahụ ma napụtakwa ekwentị na nkùnụkwụ ya".
translations.reference: Deputy Inspector General D K Arya said, "We have arrested five persons who raped the Swiss woman and recovered her mobile and laptop".
translations.hypothesis: The officer in charge of the police investigation, D.K. Arya, stated, "We have arrested five individuals who are suspected of being involved in the attack on the Swiss woman, and we have also recovered her phone and handbag."

translations.source: Ndị eboro ebubo bụ Baba Kanjar, Bhutha Kanjar, Rampro Kanjar, Gaza Kanjar na Vishnu Kanjar.
translations.reference: The accused are named as Baba Kanjar, Bhutha Kanjar, Rampro Kanjar, Gaza Kanjar and Vishnu Kanjar.
translations.hypothesis: The deities mentioned are Baba Kanjar, Bhutha Kanjar, Rampro Kanjar, Gaza Kanjar, and Vishnu Kanjar.

translations.source: Onye isi ndị uweojii Chandra Shekhar Solanki sị na ndị eboro ebubo kpuchiri ihu bịa n'ụlọ ikpe.

translations.hypothesis: The police chief, Chandra Shekhar Solanki, stated that the accused individuals, who were wearing face coverings, appeared in court.

translations.source: Obu eziokwu na mmadu ato no nime ulo ahu mgbe ugbo-ala ahu kuru ya, onweghi onye nime ha meruru ahu.
translations.reference: Although three people were inside the house when the car impacted it, none of them were hurt.
translations.hypothesis: It is true that three people were inside the building when the farmland collapsed, but none of them were injured.

translations.source: N'agbanyeghị nke a, onye ọkwọ ụgbọ merụrụ ezigbo ahụ n'isi.
translations.reference: However, the driver sustained serious injuries to the head.
translations.hypothesis: Despite this, the driver sustained a serious head injury.

translations.source: E mechiri nwa oge okporo ụzọ ahụ ebe ihe mberede mere ebe ndị ọrụ mberede tọhapụrụ onye ọkwọ ụgbọ ala ahụ site na Audi TT na-acha uhie.
translations.reference: The road where the crash happened was temporarily closed while emergency services freed the driver from the red Audi TT.
translations.hypothesis: A child was struck by a car at the intersection where an emergency occurred, and emergency responders extracted the driver from the red Audi TT.

translations.source: Ọ nọbu n'ụlọ ọgwụ Jems Pajet dị na Gret Yamawụt.
translations.reference: He was initially hospitalised in the James Paget Hospital in Great Yarmouth.
translations.hypothesis: He was at the James Paget Hospital in Great Yarmouth.

translations.source: E mechara kwagarịa ya n’Ụlọ ọgwụ Addenbrooke na Kembriji.
translations.reference: He was subsequently relocated to Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge.
translations.hypothesis: He was eventually admitted to Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge.

translations.source: Adekọya anọrọla n'Ụlọ ikpe Obodo Edịnbọg ebe eboro ya ebubo maka igbu nwa ya nwoke.
translations.reference: Adekoya has since been in Edinburgh Sheriff Court charged with murdering her son.
translations.hypothesis: The man has been arraigned in the Magistrate's Court, where he is facing charges of murdering his son.

translations.source: Atụrụ ya nga ma na-eche ikpe, mana akụkọ ọgba ama ọbụla nwere ike ịbụ nke rụrụ arụ n'ihi na ebipụtara onyonyo ya ọfụma.
translations.reference: She is in custody pending indictment and trial, but any eyewitness evidence may be tainted because her image has been widely published.
translations.hypothesis: While the trial is ongoing, the widespread dissemination of the case's details could be problematic, especially given the publication of sensitive images.

translations.source: Nke a bụ omume a na-ahụkarị ebe ndị ọzọ na UK mana íkpé íkpē Scottish na-arụ ọrụ n'ụzọ dị iche ma ụlọ ikpe eleela mbipụta nke fotò gasị dị ka ihe nwere ike ịbụ ajọ mbunobi.
translations.reference: This is common practice elsewhere in the UK but Scottish justice works differently and courts have viewed publication of photos as potentially prejudicial.
translations.hypothesis: This is a common practice in other parts of the UK, but Scottish courts operate differently, and the disclosure of photographs is not automatically considered a breach of protocol.

translations.source: Ọkachamara Pamela Ferguson nke Mahadum Dundee kwuru "ndị nta akụkọ dị ka ndị na-aga ije n'ebe dị oke egwu ma ọ bụrụ na ha ebipụta foto na ihe ndị ọzọ nke ndị a na-enyo enyo."
translations.reference: Professor Pamela Ferguson of the University of Dundee notes "journalists do seem to be walking a dangerous line if publishing photos etc of suspects."
translations.hypothesis: Pamela Ferguson, a specialist at the University of Dundee, stated, "Journalists are putting themselves in extremely dangerous situations if they publish photos and other materials related to individuals who are suspected of wrongdoing."

translations.source: Ụlọ ọrụ Krawn, nke nọ n'isi amamikpe, agwala ndị nta akụkọ na ha agaghị ekwu okwu gbasara okwu akpụ n'ọnụ ozo ruo mgbe amara mmadụ ikpe.
translations.reference: Crown Office, which is in overall charge of prosecutions, has indicated to journalists that no further comment will be made at least until indictment.
translations.hypothesis: The Crown Prosecution Service, the UK's leading prosecuting authority, has told journalists that it will not be making any further statements regarding the ongoing investigation until a person is formally charged.

translations.source: Dọkumentị ahụ, na-ndabere na ohihiahụ, ga-arụnye aka na ụmụ mgbagha oke ala ndị ahụ, nke Palestaịnụ chọrọ na-ndabere n’ụmụ oke ala tupu Agha Mideast 1967 ahụ.
translations.reference: The document, according to the leak, will refer to the borders dispute, which Palestine wants based on the borders before the 1967 Mideast War.
translations.hypothesis: The document, based on historical records, will include details about the refugees, specifically Palestinian refugees who were displaced from their homes before the 1967 Middle East war.

translations.source: Isiokwu ndị ọzọ ekpuchiri gụnyere site n'ihe akọrọ ọdịnihu Jerusalem nke dị nsọ nye mba abụọ ahụ na okwu Ndagwurugwu Jọdan.
translations.reference: Other topics covered reportedly include the future state of Jerusalem which is sacred to both nations and the Jordan Valley issue.
translations.hypothesis: Other topics discussed included the historical significance of Jerusalem to both nations and the issue of the West Bank of Jordan.

translations.source: Israel na-achọ ka ndị agha nọrọ na ndagwụrụgwụ a ruo afọ iri ozigbo abanyere na nkwekọrịta, mana PA chọrọ ka ndị agha a nọrọ ruo naanị afọ ise.
translations.reference: Israel demands an ongoing military presence in the valley for ten years once an agreement is signed while the PA agrees to leave such presence only for five years.
translations.hypothesis: Israel is seeking for the soldiers to remain in this deployment for a full ten years, but the PA (Palestinian Authority) is demanding that the soldiers only stay for five years.

translations.source: Ndị nche legidere ndị ọgbaa anya nke ọma ka ha mere nnwale njikwa ọtapịapịa nke ntụkwasị, dịka e lebara anya na nnwale ahụ ma tụlee ma ọ dị ire.
translations.reference: Shooters in the supplementary pest control trial were to be closely supervised by rangers, as the trial was monitored and its effectiveness evaluated.
translations.hypothesis: The security personnel closely monitored the suspects during the polygraph examination, paying close attention to their reactions and assessing their credibility.

translations.source: N’ime otu mmekọrịta nke NPWS na Sporting Shooters Association of Australia (NSW) Inc, e were n’ọrụ ndị ọrụ afọ ofufo tozuru oke, n’okpuru mmemme ịchụ nta nke Sporting Shooters Association ahụ.
translations.reference: In a partnership of NPWS and the Sporting Shooters Association of Australia (NSW) Inc, qualified volunteers were recruited, under the Sporting Shooters Association's hunting program.
translations.hypothesis: As part of a partnership between the National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) and the Sporting Shooters Association of Australia (NSW) Inc., qualified firearms officers are deployed, operating under the auspices of the Sporting Shooters Association's hunting program.

translations.source: Dị ka Mik O'Flynn, Onye isi ọrụ na NPWS na-ahụ maka Ndokwa Ogige na Nketa, kwuru, ndị ọgba egbe anọ a họọrọ maka mmemme ọgbụgba nke mbụ bụ ndị akuzigorola nchekwa ma nye ha ọzụzụ.
translations.reference: According to Mick O'Flynn, the Acting Director Park Conservation and Heritage with the NPWS, the four shooters selected for the first shooting operation received comprehensive safety and training instruction.
translations.hypothesis: According to Mik O'Flynn, a senior officer at the NPWS responsible for Parks and Wildlife, the four rangers selected for the initial training program have already demonstrated a commitment to conservation and have received specialized training.

translations.source: Martelly n̄ụrụ iyi n’ime otu Kansụl Ntuli aka Kenwa oge (CEP) ọhụrụ nke ndịòtù itoollu ụnyaahụ.
translations.reference: Martelly swore in a new Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) of nine members yesterday.
translations.hypothesis: Martelly was appointed to the newly formed Electoral Observation Mission (CEP) by the electoral commission.

translations.source: Ọ bụ CEP nke ise nke Marteli n'afọ anọ.
translations.reference: It is Martelly's fifth CEP in four years.
translations.hypothesis: It was Marteli's fifth CEP in four years.

translations.source: N'ọnwa gara aga ozi sitere n'onye ọchịchị kwadoro ọgbụgba arụkwaghịm CEP nọbu anọ dịka ihe so n'usoro omume ihe ibuje obodo na ntuli aka ọhụrụ
translations.reference: Last month a presidential commission recommended the prior CEP's resignation as part of a package of measures to move the country towards new elections.
translations.hypothesis: Last month, a statement was released by a government official approving the deployment of four CEP (Central Electoral Commission) teams as part of the process for preparing for the upcoming local elections.

translations.source: Ntinye ọrụ ahụ bụ azịza Martelly maka ngagharị iwe nke mgbochi ọchịchị zuru ebe niile nke bidoro na Ọktoba.
translations.reference: The commission was Martelly's response to widespread anti-regime protests that started in October.
translations.hypothesis: Martelly's appointment of a new minister was his response to the wave of protests that had been sweeping the country since October.

translations.source: Ụmụ ngagharị iwe a na-alụ ọgụ mgbe ụfọdụ na ya bụ ọdịda ime ntuli aka kpatara ya, ụfọdụ etozuola kemgbe 2011.
translations.reference: The sometimes-violent protests were triggered by failure to hold elections, some due since 2011.
translations.hypothesis: These protests sometimes erupt due to electoral irregularities, and some have been ongoing since 2011.

translations.source: E kwuputala na na e nweela nsogbu 60 sitere na iPods ndị n'anaghị arụ ọrụ nke ọma na-ekwo oke ọkụ, nke na-ebutala ọkụ ọgbụgba isii merụrụ ndị mmadụ ahụ obere.
translations.reference: Around 60 cases of malfunctioning iPods overheating have been reported, causing a total of six fires and leaving four people with minor burns.
translations.hypothesis: It was reported that there were 60 incidents involving iPods that overheated, leading to six separate cases of minor injuries to people.

translations.source: Ministri Japan nke Akụnụba, Azụmaahịa na Ụlọ ọrụ mmepụta (METI) kwuru na ọ ma ama maka ihe mberede iri abụọ na asaa metụtara njìarụ ndị ahụ.
translations.reference: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) said that it had been aware of 27 accidents related to the devices.
translations.hypothesis: The Japanese Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) stated that it is aware of the twenty-seven incidents related to the equipment.

translations.source: N'izuka gara aga, METI mara okwa sị na Apple gwara ya gbasara oke ekpomoku iri atọ na anọ merenụ, nke ụlọ ọrụ kpọrọ "ihe na-abụghị ihe."
translations.reference: Last week, METI announced that Apple had informed it of 34 additional overheating incidents, which the company called "non-serious."
translations.hypothesis: Recently, METI reported that Apple had informed them about a data breach affecting approximately 34 million users, which the company referred to as "non-critical."

translations.source: Ụlọ ozi zaghachiri sị na mbugharị oge rịpọt Apple mere dị "mwute n'ezie".
translations.reference: The ministry responded by calling Apple's postponement of the report "truly regrettable."
translations.hypothesis: The church responded, stating that the time change implemented by Apple was "truly unfortunate."

translations.source: Ala ọma jijiji ahụ mere Mariana na 07:19 elekere ụtụtụ mpaghara (09:19 p.m. GMT Friday).

translations.hypothesis: A strong earthquake struck the Mariana region at 7:19 a.m. local time (9:19 p.m. GMT on Friday).

translations.source: Ụlọ ọrụ nlekọta ihe mberede nke Nọtan Marianas sị na onweghị mmebi ihe akọpụtara n'obodo.
translations.reference: The Northern Marianas emergency management office said that there were no damages reported in the nation.
translations.hypothesis: The Marianas Trench emergency response team has reported no damage in the area.

translations.reference: Also the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center said that there was no Tsunami indication.

translations.hypothesis: A Filipino police officer has been accused of exploiting tourists in Hong Kong by extorting them, a practice that has angered many Filipinos.

translations.hypothesis: Several people were reported missing, and it was later confirmed that six of them had died.

translations.source: Ndị ejigidere ejigide isii, tinyere ụmụaka na ndị okenye, ka ahapụrụ n'oge, ma ndị Filipino n'ese foto.
translations.reference: Six hostages, including the children and elderly, were released early, as were the Filipino photographers.
translations.hypothesis: Six people, including children and adults, were rescued after being stranded at sea, thanks to the efforts of the Filipino coast guard.

translations.source: Ndị ose foto ahụ mechara nọchie otu agadi nwanyị dịka ọ gara ụlọmposi. A gbagburu Mendoza.
translations.reference: The photographers later took the place of an aged lady as she needed the lavatory. Mendoza was gunned down.
translations.hypothesis: The photographers eventually replaced an elderly woman as she entered the morgue. Mendoza was killed.

translations.source: Liggins soro n’uzoụkwụ nna ya ma banye n’ọrụ ọgwụ.
translations.reference: Liggins followed in his father’s footsteps and entered a career in medicine.
translations.hypothesis: Liggins followed in his father's footsteps and entered the medical profession.

translations.source: Ọ zụrụ ọzụzụ dị ka ọkachamara nke nne na-amụ nwa wee malite ịrụ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ọgwụ Ndị Inyom Nke ala Auckland na 1959.
translations.reference: He trained as an obstetrician and began to work at the Auckland's National Women's Hospital in 1959.
translations.hypothesis: She trained as a professional midwife and began working at Auckland Hospital in 1959.

translations.source: Mgbe ọ na-arụ ọrụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ Liggins malitere inyocha ọmụmụ nwa akaghị aka n'oge ezumike ya.
translations.reference: While he was working at the hospital Liggins began to investigate premature labor during his spare time.
translations.hypothesis: While working at Liggins Hospital, she began researching accidental pregnancies during her time off.

translations.source: Nlebaanya ya gosiri na e nye homonu, ọ ga-eme ka nkuume nwata dị n'afọ tozuo oke ọsịsọ karịa.
translations.reference: His research showed that if a hormone was administered it would speed up the baby's foetal lung maturation.
translations.hypothesis: If his prediction proves to be correct, the increased demand for breast milk will likely lead to a significant rise in its price.

translations.source: Xinhua kwuru na ndị nnyocha gọọmenti chọtara igwe 'igbe ojii' na-edokọ etu njem ụgbọelu si gaa na Wenezdee.
translations.reference: Xinhua reported that government investigators recovered two 'black box' flight recorders on Wednesday.
translations.hypothesis: Xinhua reported that government investigators found a "black box" device that contains data about how the plane crashed on Wednesday.

translations.source: Ndị mgba ibe ha mere ihe ndị gosiri nkwanye ugwu nye Luna.
translations.reference: Fellow wrestlers also paid tribute to Luna.
translations.hypothesis: Neighbors did things that showed great respect for Luna.

translations.source: Tọmi Drima sị na "Luna bụ Eze nwaanyị ihe ngabiga oke nke mbụ. Onye nlekwa ọrụ m nke mbụ. Luna nwụrụ n'abalị ọnwa abụọ. Ọ pụrụ iche dị ka ya. Nwaanyị siri ike."
translations.reference: Tommy Dreamer said "Luna was the first Queen of Extreme. My first manager. Luna passed away on the night of two moons. Pretty unique just like her. Strong woman."
translations.hypothesis: Tọmi Drima said, "Luna was the first female transit officer. She was my first supervisor. Luna passed away two months ago. She was exceptional, just like that. A strong woman."

translations.source: Dọstin "Goldọst" Runnels sị na "Luna na-eme ihe ndị ara ka m...onwere ike karịa... ahụrụ m ya n'anya aga m na atụkwa anya ya... Enwerem olileanya na ọnọ ebe ka mma."
translations.reference: Dustin "Goldust" Runnels commented that "Luna was as freaky as me...maybe even more...love her and will miss her...hopefully she's in a better place."
translations.hypothesis: Dr. "Goldust" Runnels said, "Luna is doing things that are... well, she's just better... I love her, and I expect great things from her... I have high hopes for her."

translations.source: N'ime mmadụ otu puku na iri anọ tụrụ ụtụ tupu ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị gọọmenti etiti nke afọ 2010, ndị megidere mba Ọstrelia ịbụ obodo kwuuru onwe ya ji pasentị asatọ rịa elu kemgbe afọ 2008.
translations.reference: Out of 1,400 people polled prior to the 2010 federal election, those who oppose Australia becoming a republic grew by 8 per cent since 2008.
translations.hypothesis: Prior to the implementation of the Australian government's national policy in 2010, the number of people seeking asylum in Australia increased by eight percent since 2008.

translations.source: Onye nlekota ala (Caretaker Prime Minister) Julia Gillard kwuru n’oge Kampeenu nke nhoputa ndi ochichi nke goomenti etiti na okwere na Australia kwesiri ibu repoblik ma Eze nwanyi Elizabeth nke abuo chicha.
translations.reference: Caretaker Prime Minister Julia Gillard claimed during the campaign of the 2010 federal election that she believed Australia should become a republic at the end of Queen Elizabeth II's reign.
translations.hypothesis: The caretaker Prime Minister, Julia Gillard, stated during the federal election campaign in Australia that the country should remain a republic, even if Queen Elizabeth II were to continue her reign.

translations.source: 34 nime-otu-nari-nile bu ndi tinyere aka na ntuli aka ahu n’enwe otu uche ahu, n’acho ka Eze-nwanyi Elizabeth II buru onye eze nke ikpeazu nke Australia.
translations.reference: 34 per cent of those in the poll share this view, wanting Queen Elizabeth II to be Australia's last monarch.
translations.hypothesis: Out of the one hundred and thirty-four people involved in the referendum, all shared the same view: that Queen Elizabeth II should remain the head of state of Australia.

translations.source: Ka ịtụ vootu nọ na ngwụcha, pasentị iri abụọ na itolu n'ime ndị elebaara anya kwenyere na Ọstrelia kwesịrị ịbụrụ mba nọọrọ onwe ya ngwa ngwa, ebe pasentị iri atọ na otu kwenyere na Ọstrelia ekwesịghị ịbụ obodo nọọrọ onwe ya.
translations.reference: At the extremes of the poll, 29 per cent of those surveyed believe Australia should become a republic as soon as possible, while 31 per cent believe Australia should never become a republic.
translations.hypothesis: As the election draws to a close, sixty-three percent of those surveyed believe that Australia should become an independent nation as soon as possible, while thirty-one percent believe that Australia should not become an independent nation.

translations.source: Onye nwebụrụ mgbanye ọlaedo Olympicruru igwu mmiri na nke 100m na 200m ụdị nnwere onwe na ngwụgharị ugboro atọ n'Egwuregwu Commonwealth ahụ, mana n’ihi mkpesa ya, enweela obi abụọ maka ịdị mma nke ahụike ya.
translations.reference: The Olympic gold medalist was due to swim in the 100m and 200m freestyle and in three relays at the Commonwealth Games, but due to his complaints his fitness has been in doubt.
translations.hypothesis: The swimmer, who competed in the Olympic Games and won medals in the 100m and 200m freestyle events at the Commonwealth Games, has expressed concerns about the impact of the intense training and competition on their physical well-being.

translations.source: O nwebeghị ike ịn̄ụ ọgwụ ndị ahụ o kwesịrị iji merie mgbu ya dị ka a machibidoro ha iwu site n’Egwuregwu.
translations.reference: He has been unable to take the drugs needed to overcome his pain as they are banned from the Games.
translations.hypothesis: He was unable to take the medications he needed to manage his pain because they were banned by the competition rules.

translations.source: Curtis Cooper, onye ọka mmụta mgbakọ na mwepụ na onye ọka mmụta sayensị kọmputa na Mahadum nke Etiti Missouri, achọpụtala akara praịm kachasị buo ibu ruo ta na Jenụwarị 25.
translations.reference: Curtis Cooper, a mathematician and computer science professor at the University of Central Missouri, has discovered the largest known prime number to date on January 25.
translations.hypothesis: Curtis Cooper, a professor of mathematics and a professor of computer science at Missouri State University, discovered the largest known prime number as of January 25th.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ nyochara nchọpụta ahụ n’iji ngwaike na ngwanrò dị iche iche site na mbido Februarị ma a mara ọkwa ya na Tusdee.
translations.reference: Several people verified the discovery using different hardware and software by the beginning of February and it was announced on Tuesday.
translations.hypothesis: Many people have been examining the findings of the study using various tools and methods since the beginning of February, and the results were released on Tuesday.

translations.source: Ụmụ Kọmetị nwere ike ịbụ isi mmalite nnefe mmiri nye ụwa ya na ihe dị ndụ nwere ike ịmepụta ụmụ protiin ma kwado ndụ.
translations.reference: Comets may possibly have been a source of water delivery to the earth along with organic matter that can form proteins and support life.
translations.hypothesis: Comets can be a source of water for planets, and they may also contain organic molecules that could support life.

translations.source: Ndị ọka mmụta sayensị nwere olileanya ịghọta ka uwa dị iche iche sị kpụọ, ọkachasị otu ụwa anyị siri kpụọ, kemgbe okwute igwe na ụwa anyị sukọkọ isi n'ote aka.
translations.reference: Scientists hope to understand how planets form, especially how the Earth formed, since comets collided with the Earth long ago.
translations.hypothesis: Scientists are eager to understand how different celestial bodies are formed, particularly how our own planet formed, since the Earth and other planets in our solar system began to coalesce billions of years ago.

translations.source: Kuomo, onye dị afọ iri ise na atọ, bidoro ọchịchị gọọmenti steeti na mbido afọ a ma binye aka n'ọnwa gara aga n'iwu kwadoro mmekọahụ nwoke na nwoke maọbụ nwanyị na nwanyị.
translations.reference: Cuomo, 53, began his governorship earlier this year and signed a bill last month legalizing same-sex marriage.
translations.hypothesis: Kuomo, who is fifty-three years old, began his tenure as governor of the state earlier this year and recently signed a bill legalizing same-sex marriage.

translations.source: Ọ kpọrọ asịrị ndị ahụ "mkparịta ụka ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na nzuzu".
translations.reference: He referred to the rumors as "political chatter and silliness".
translations.hypothesis: He referred to those discussions as "political and social discourse."

translations.source: A na-aka na ọ ga-azọ ọkwa onye isi ala n'afọ 2016.
translations.reference: He is speculated to make a run for president in 2016.
translations.hypothesis: He was considered a potential candidate for the presidency in 2016.

translations.source: NextGen bụ otu sistemụ FAA na-asị ga-enye ụgbọ elu òhèerè ife site n’ụzọ kara pee mpe ma chekwa ọtụtụ nde galọnụ nke mmanụ kwa afọ na mkpọfụ anwụrụ.
translations.reference: NextGen is a system the FAA claims would allow aircraft to fly shorter routes and save millions of gallons of fuel each year and cut carbon emissions.
translations.hypothesis: NextGen is a system being implemented by the FAA that will allow aircraft to fly more efficiently and save millions of gallons of fuel each year, while also reducing emissions.

translations.source: O ji teknụzụ satilaịti dị iche na teknụzụ rada nọ n'ala were enyere ndị na-ejikwa nfegharị ụgbọelu aka ịma ebe ụgbọelu nọ kpọmkwem ma nyekwa ndị ọkwọ ụgbọelu ozi ziri ezi.
translations.reference: It uses satellite-based technology as opposed to older ground-radar-based technology to allow air traffic controllers to pinpoint aircraft with greater precision and give pilots more accurate information.
translations.hypothesis: It utilizes satellite technology, which differs from ground-based radar systems, to provide air traffic controllers with precise information about the location of aircraft, and also delivers accurate data to pilots.

translations.source: Anaghị etinyekwasị ihe njem, ma ụgbọoloko elu ala agaghị akwụsị na Wembli, ma ndowe ụgbọala makwa akụrụngwa dowe ma gbakwaa adịghị ebe ahụ.
translations.reference: No extra transport is being put on and overground trains will not stop at Wembley, and car parking and park-and-ride facilities are unavailable at the ground.
translations.hypothesis: The match was not without its drama, but the away team's bus broke down near Wembley, and the players were reportedly stranded there.

translations.source: Ụjọ ụbịam ụzọ njem mere na onwere ike ndị egwuregwu ga egwu n'enweghị ndị nkwado ha.
translations.reference: Fears of lack of transportation raised the possibility that the game would be forced to play behind closed doors without the team's supporters.
translations.hypothesis: A power outage caused the sports games to be postponed, leaving the athletes without their usual support.

translations.source: Otu mmụta e bipụtara na Tọzdee n’ime jọnaalụ Sayensi kọrọ na mwube nke otu ụdị nnụnụ ọhụrụ na Agwaetiti Galápagos nke Ikuedọ.
translations.reference: A study published on Thursday in the journal Science reported on formation of a new bird species on the Ecuadorean Galápagos Islands.
translations.hypothesis: A study published on Tuesday in the journal Science reported the discovery of a new species of finch on the Galapagos Islands.

translations.source: Ndị nchọcha sitere na Mahadum Princeton dị na mba Amerịka na Mahadum Uppsala dị na mba Sweden kọwara ụdịdị ọhụrụ pụtara na naanị ọgbọ abụọ, ọ bụ ezie na ụkpụrụ a ka e chere na ọ na-ewe oge karịa, n'ihi ọmụmụ n’etiti otu ụdị nnụnụ bụ Dawin Finchi na-ebi otu ebe, Jiospiza Fọtisi, nakwa Kakụtus Finchi si esi bata, Jiospiza konirostrisi.
translations.reference: Researchers from Princeton University in the United States and Uppsala University in Sweden reported the new species evolved in just two generations, though this process had been believed to take much longer, due to breeding between an endemic Darwin finch, Geospiza fortes, and the immigrant cactus finch, Geospiza conirostris.
translations.hypothesis: Researchers from Princeton University in the United States and Uppsala University in Sweden have described a new evolutionary pattern that occurred within just two generations. This phenomenon, which challenges the traditional understanding of evolutionary timescales, involves the emergence of distinct traits within two closely related species of finches, *Darwin's finch* and *Cactus finch*, and their subsequent diversification into two new species: *Geospiza fortis* and *Geospiza conirostris*.

translations.source: E nwere ike ịrụpụta ọla edo n'ime ụdị ụdịdị niile. E nwere ike ịpịakọta ya n'ime ụdịdị ndị pere mpe.
translations.reference: Gold may be worked into all sorts of shapes. It can be rolled into tiny shapes.
translations.hypothesis: Gold can be produced in various forms. It can be refined into very pure forms.

translations.source: Enwere ike itinye ya n'ime waya girigiri, nke e nwere ike ịghịkọta ma tee ya ihe otite. Enwere ike itisa ya ma ọ bụ rọkụlọ ya n'ime mpempe akwụkwọ.
translations.reference: It can be pulled into thin wire, which can be twisted and plaited. It can be hammered or rolled into sheets.
translations.hypothesis: It can be inserted into a thin wire, which can then be easily connected and used for various purposes. It can also be melted or molded into different shapes.

translations.source: Enwere ike ime ya ọ dị oke gịrịgịrị, ma mado ya n'ahụ igwe ọzọ. Enwere ike ime ya ọ dị oke gịrịgịrị ruo na ụfọdụ oge eji ya achọ ọrụ agba ejiri aka tee n'akwụkwọ akpọrọ "akwụkwọ ihe ngosi" mma.
translations.reference: It can be made very thin, and stuck onto other metal. It can be made so thin that it was sometimes used to decorate the hand-painted pictures in books called "illuminated manuscripts".
translations.hypothesis: It can be very difficult, but I see it in another light. It can be difficult to the point where, sometimes, people use it to apply for jobs, including writing a "portfolio" showcasing their skills.

translations.source: A na-akpọ nke a PH nke kemịkal. I nwere ike ịme ihe ngosi site na iji mmiri kabeeji na-acha ọbara ọbara
translations.reference: This is called a chemical's pH. You can make an indicator using red cabbage juice.
translations.hypothesis: This is called a chemical pH indicator. You can create a demonstration by using red cabbage water.

translations.source: Ihu mmanya kabej a na-agbanwe agba dabere na otu kemikal ya si dị asidik maọbụ bezik (alkaline).
translations.reference: The cabbage juice changes color depending on how acidic or basic (alkaline) the chemical is.
translations.hypothesis: The color of a universal indicator solution changes depending on whether its chemical composition is acidic or basic (alkaline).

translations.source: Nha nke ayọn Hydrogen nọ na kemịkal ọbụla bụ ihe na-egosi ogo pH ya.
translations.reference: The pH level is indicated by the amount of Hydrogen (the H in pH) ions in the tested chemical.
translations.hypothesis: The hydrogen exponent in a chemical formula indicates the pH level of the substance.

translations.source: Ayọn Haịdrojin bụ protọn anaarala elektrọn ya (ebe atọm Haịdrojin nwere otu protọn na otu elektrọn).
translations.reference: Hydrogen ions are protons that had their electrons stripped off them (since Hydrogen atoms consist of one proton and one electron).
translations.hypothesis: Hydrogen is an element whose atom has one proton and one electron (a hydrogen atom has one proton and one electron).

translations.source: Kpaharia kota nzu abuo ahu kporo-nku onu ma mgbe-ahu, na aka di mmiri ma dikwa ocha, pikoo ha ka ha ghoo boolu.
translations.reference: Swirl the two dry powders together and then, with clean wet hands, squeeze them into a ball.
translations.hypothesis: The two elephants, covered in mud and water, but still clean, approached the pool and began to drink.

translations.source: Mpụta ya na mmiri dị gị n'aka ga-enwe mmekọrịta, nke ga-enye gị mmetụta dị aghaa ma mepụta ihe dị ka ọkpụkpụ mkpuchi.
translations.reference: The moisture on your hands will react with the outer layers, which will feel funny and form a sort of shell.
translations.hypothesis: Its water-based formula will blend seamlessly with your skin, providing a smooth finish and a natural, skin-like appearance.

translations.source: Ọ fọrọ obere ka ụlọ niile dị n'obodo Harappa na Mohenjo-daro nwee mpochi mmiri, ya na usoro mkpopu kara aka.
translations.reference: The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had a flush toilet in almost every house, attached to a sophisticated sewage system.
translations.hypothesis: It is noteworthy that all the houses in the cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had wells, along with sophisticated drainage systems.

translations.source: A chọtala sistemu nsi fọdụrụnụ n’ụlọ Minoan ndị dị n’obodo Crete na Santorini na Greece
translations.reference: Remains of sewage systems have been found in the houses of the Minoan cities of Crete and Santorini in Greece.
translations.hypothesis: A sophisticated drainage system has been discovered in Minoan settlements located on the islands of Crete and Santorini in Greece.

translations.source: Ha nwekwara ụlọ mposi n'Ijipt mgbe ochie, Peshia na Chaịna. N'okpuru ọchịchị ndị Rom, mgbe ụfọdụ ụlọ mposi na-abụkarị otu akụkụ nke ụlọ ọsịsa ahụ ọha ebe ụmụ nwoke na ụmụ nwanyị nọkọtara ọnụ.
translations.reference: There were also toilets in ancient Egypt, Persia and China. In Roman civilization, toilets were sometimes part of public bath houses where men and women were together in mixed company.
translations.hypothesis: Public toilets also existed in ancient Egypt, Persia, and China. Under Roman rule, public toilets were sometimes integrated into public bathhouses, where men and women would gather.

translations.source: Mgbe ikporo mmadu onye no otutu puku maili site n’ebe ino , ihe iji bu igwe satalaiti.
translations.reference: When you call someone who is thousands of miles away, you are using a satellite.
translations.hypothesis: When a person is located thousands of miles away, the tool used is a satellite.

translations.source: Satilaịti nọ n'ikuku na enweta oku ma zighachi ya n'ala na ntabi anya.
translations.reference: The satellite in space gets the call and then reflects it back down, almost instantly.
translations.hypothesis: The satellite is in orbit, receiving heat and radiating it back into space.

translations.source: E ji ụgbọelu rọkeetị zije satilaịti n'ikuku. Ndị ọka mmụta sayensị na eji igwe nyocha kpakpando afụ ụzọ n'ikuku mpụga ụwa n'ihi na igwe ụwa anyị na arọgharị ụfọdụ ọkụ anyị na ahụ.
translations.reference: The satellite was sent into space by a rocket. Scientists use telescopes in space because the Earth’s atmosphere distorts some of our light and view.
translations.hypothesis: A rocket-powered aircraft is used to launch satellites into space. Scientists use telescopes to observe celestial objects in the outer space, including some of the stars in our galaxy.

translations.source: O na-ewe nnukwu rọketi gafere ụkwụ otu narị n’elu itinye otu satịlaịtị na teliskop n’eluụwa.
translations.reference: It takes a giant rocket over a 100 feet high to put a satellite or telescope in space.
translations.hypothesis: It launched a large rocket that soared over a hundred kilometers above the ground to deploy a satellite and a telescope into orbit.

translations.source: Wiilu agbanweela ụwa n'ụdị enweghị atụ. Ihe kachasị ukwu nke wiilu merela anyị bụ na o nyere anyị ụzọ njem dị mfe ma dị ọsịsọ karịa.
translations.reference: The wheel has changed the world in incredible ways. The biggest thing that the wheel has done for us is given us much easier and faster transportation.
translations.hypothesis: The wheel has revolutionized the world in countless ways. Perhaps the most significant contribution of the wheel is that it has provided us with a more efficient and convenient means of transportation.

translations.source: O wetegoro anyị ụgbọoloko, ụgbọala na ọtụtụ akụrụngwa njem dị iche iche.
translations.reference: It has brought us the train, the car, and many other transportation devices.
translations.hypothesis: They provided us with bicycles, cars, and various other types of transportation.

translations.source: N'okpuru ha bụ ụmụ nwamba ha ọkara na-eri anụoriri ha ọkara nke nwere ike isi na oke bekee ruo na ele nakwa mgbada.
translations.reference: Under them are more medium sized cats that eat medium sized prey ranging from rabbits to antelopes and deer.
translations.hypothesis: They are mostly female, with approximately half being carnivorous and the other half being omnivorous, capable of consuming everything from small insects to large pieces of meat.

translations.source: N’ikpeazụ, e nwere ọtụtụ obere nwamba (gụnyere anụ ụlọ nwamba furu efu) na-eri ọtụtụ obere ụmụ anụmanụ dị ka ụmụ ahụhụ, oke, ngwere, na nnụnụ.
translations.reference: Finally, there are many small cats (including loose pet cats) that eat the far more numerous small prey like insects, rodents, lizards, and birds.
translations.hypothesis: Finally, there are many small animals (including escaped domestic animals) that prey on various small creatures such as rodents, rabbits, birds, and insects.

translations.source: Ihe nzuzo nke ọganihu ha bụ gburugburu ebe obibi, ọrụ nwamba niile ji nke na egbochi ịsọmpi ha na ndị ọzọ.
translations.reference: The secret to their success is the concept of the niche, a special job each cat holds that keeps it from competing with others.
translations.hypothesis: The key to their success lies in their environment, their strong work ethic, and the way they prevent competition from others.

translations.source: Ọdụm bụ nwamba kachasị emekọrịta n'onwe ha, na-ebi na nnukwu òtù akpọrọ nganga.
translations.reference: Lions are the most social cats, living in large groups called prides.
translations.hypothesis: Elephants are highly social animals that live in large, complex family groups.

translations.source: Mpako gasị bụ otu ruo atọ ụmụ nwoke tozuru oke metụtaranụ mejupụtara ya, yana ụmụ nwanyị na ụmụ ya dị ọtụtụ dị ka iri atọ.
translations.reference: Prides are made up of one to three related adult males, along with as many as thirty females and cubs.
translations.hypothesis: A traditional Igbo marriage ceremony typically involves a group of three to four male relatives who are closely related to the groom, along with a large number of other relatives and friends, often numbering in the dozens.

translations.source: Ndị nwanyị na-emetụtakarị nke ukwu n’onwe ha, n’ibu otu nnukwu ezinụlọ nke ụmụnne nwanyị na ụmụ nwa nwanyị.
translations.reference: The females are usually closely related to each other, being a large family of sisters and daughters.
translations.hypothesis: Women often experience significant personal growth within the context of a large family, surrounded by sisters and nieces.

translations.source: Ezinụlọ Ọdụm na-akpa agwa ka ezinụlọ oke nkịta ọhịa maọbụ nkịta ụlọ, anụ ndị nwere oyiyi dị ịtụ n'anya nye Ọdụm (mana odịghị otu a n'ebe nnukwu nwamba ndị ọzọ nọ) n'omume, ma bụrụ ihe oke iyi egwu nye ihe ọbụla ha na-achụ na nta.
translations.reference: Lion prides act much like packs of wolves or dogs, animals surprisingly similar to lions (but not other big cats) in behavior, and also very deadly to their prey.
translations.hypothesis: The Odum family, like other families of wild or domestic animals, possesses a striking appearance that is particularly appealing to the Odum (though this is not the case with other large animals). They are also incredibly agile and pose a significant threat to anything they hunt.

translations.source: Ome ihe egwuregwu zuruoke nkeoma, agu ahu ga enyili elu (obu ezie na obughi nkeoma), gwuo mmiri, maa-amaa garuo ebe di oke anya ma doo okpukpu ise dika ike mmadu di ike nwere ike ido.
translations.reference: A well rounded athlete, the tiger can climb (though not well), swim, leap great distances and pull with five times the force of a strong human.
translations.hypothesis: These incredibly strong athletes lifted heavy weights, sometimes straining their bodies, and pushed themselves to the absolute limit of human strength.

translations.source: Agụ nọ n’otu otu (Genus Panthera) dika ọdụm, owuru, na jaguar. Nwamba anọ ndị a bụ naanị ndị nwere ike ime mbigbọ.
translations.reference: The tiger is in the same group (Genus Panthera) as lions, leopards, and jaguars. These four cats are the only ones who can roar.
translations.hypothesis: Lions, tigers, and jaguars belong to the same genus (Panthera). These four animals are the only ones capable of producing a roar.

translations.source: Ụja agụ adịghị ka mgbọpụta n'uju ụja ọdụm, mana ọ dị nnọọ ka okwu e kwuputara n'iti mkpu.
translations.reference: The tiger's roar is not like the full-voiced roar of a lion, but more like a sentence of snarly, shouted words.
translations.hypothesis: The taste of the fruit is not like the sweetness of a ripe mango, but rather it is similar to a flavor that is expressed through a distinct aroma.

translations.source: Ona amasi Ocelot iri obere umu-anumanu. Ha ga anwuchi enwe, agwo, oke na nnunu ma ha nwee ike. Oka-na-onuogugu anu anumanu nile Ocelot na achu-nta di obere nnukwu karia ka odi.
translations.reference: Ocelots like to eat small animals. They will catch monkeys, snakes, rodents and birds if they can. Almost all of the animals that the ocelot hunts are far smaller than it is.
translations.hypothesis: Ocelot cats are small wild cats. They are found in forests, grasslands, and scrublands, and they are excellent climbers and hunters. The average weight of an adult Ocelot is smaller than most domestic cats.

translations.source: Ndị oke mmụta sayensị cheere na nwamba Oselọt ji isi esochi ma na-achọta anụ ha ga eri, site na ịkpọkwa imi n'ala iji site ebe ha gara.
translations.reference: Scientists think that ocelots follow and find animals to eat (prey) by smell, sniffing for where they've been on the ground.
translations.hypothesis: Scientists believe that vultures use their sense of smell to locate carcasses and find food, and they may also track the scent trails left by animals as they move.

translations.source: Ha na-ahụ ụzọ nke ọma n'abalị, ma na ejegharịkwa na nzuzo karịa. Oselọotụ na agwakọta onwe ha na gburugburu ha iji nwude anụ ha na achụ.
translations.reference: They can see very well in the dark with night vision, and move very stealthily, too. Ocelots hunt their prey by blending in with their surroundings then pouncing on their prey.
translations.hypothesis: They are most active at night and move around more discreetly. Owls blend in with their surroundings to avoid detection by prey.

translations.source: Mgbe ọbụla ụmụ obere ihe dị ndụ (obere ọnụ ọgụgụ yiri onwe ha) si na ndị otu ha pụọ (dịka ha gafee ugwu, osimiri, maọbụ gaa n'agwaetiti ọzọ ebe ọ ga-ara ahụ isi laghachi) ha ga-achọta onwe ha na gburugburu di iche ọtụtụ mgbe.
translations.reference: When a small group of living things (a small population) gets separated from the main population that they came from (like if they move over a mountain range or a river, or if they move to a new island so that they can't easily move back) they will often find themselves in a different environment than they were in before.
translations.hypothesis: Whenever small groups of animals (a small number similar to themselves) separate from their larger group (for example, by crossing a mountain, a river, or traveling to another island where they might get lost), they often find themselves in unfamiliar environments.

translations.source: Gburugburu ọhụrụ a nwere akụrụngwa dị iche ma ndị ịsọmpi dị iche, n'ihi nke a ọnụọgụgụ ọhụrụ ahụ kwesịrị inwe akụrụngwa dị iche maọbụ ihe mmegharị ọzọ ga eme ya ka ọbụrụ onye ịsọmpi dị ike karịa ka ọdịbu.
translations.reference: This new environment has different resources and different competitors, so the new population will need different features or adaptations to be a strong competitor than what they had needed before.
translations.hypothesis: This new environment features different equipment and different competitors. Therefore, the new recruit needs to have different skills or undergo additional training to become a more effective competitor than before.

translations.source: Ọnụọgụgụ nke izizi agbanwebeghị maọlị, ha ka chọrọ ihe mmegharị dịka nke mgbe mbụ.
translations.reference: The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before.
translations.hypothesis: The initial figures have not changed, and they still require the same adjustments as before.

translations.source: Ka oge na-aga, dịka gburugburu ha ọhụrụ bidoro mawa ha ahụ, oyiyi ha na ndị ha hapụrụ ebido na-ebelata.
translations.reference: Over time, as the new population begins to adapt to their new environment, they start to look less and less like the other population.
translations.hypothesis: As time passes, and as the environment around them changes, the memories they have of the people they left behind begin to fade.

translations.source: Mgbe puku afọ maọbụ rịị nde afọ ụfọdụ gasịrị, otu abụọ a ga adị nnọọ iche ruo oke ebe agaghịzị akpọ ha abụọ otu ụdị.
translations.reference: Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the two populations will look so different that they can't be called the same species.
translations.hypothesis: After a thousand years, or perhaps even a few hundred, these two things will be so different that they will no longer be considered the same type.

translations.source: Anyi na-akpọ usoro a speciation, nke pụtara nguzobe nke ụdị okike ọhụụ. Speciation bụ nsonaazụ a na-apụghị ịgbagha agbagha na akụkụ dị oke mkpa nke evolushọn.
translations.reference: We call this process speciation, which just means the formation of new species. Speciation is an unavoidable consequence and a very important part of evolution.
translations.hypothesis: We call this process speciation, which means the formation of new species. Speciation is an inevitable consequence of fundamental aspects of evolution.

translations.source: Osisi na-eme ikuku oksigin nke mmadụ na-ekuru, ma ha na e kubanye carbon-dioxide nke mmadụ na-ekufu ume (ya bụ, na-ekufu ume).
translations.reference: Plants make oxygen which humans breathe, and they take in carbon-dioxide which humans exhale (that is, breathe out).
translations.hypothesis: Trees absorb oxygen that humans breathe, while they also release carbon dioxide, which humans exhale (breathe out).

translations.source: Akụmakụ osisi na emepụta nri nke ha site n’anyanwụ site n’aka fotosintesis. Ha na-enyekwa ndo.
translations.reference: Plants make their food from the sun by photosynthesis. They also provide shade.
translations.hypothesis: Plants produce food through photosynthesis, and they also provide oxygen.

translations.source: Anyị ji osisi eme ụlọ na akwa. Ọtụtụ nri anyị na-eri bụ osisi. Ewepụ osisi, anụmanụ agaghị adị ndụ.
translations.reference: We make our houses from plants and make clothes from plants. Most foods that we eat are plants. Without plants, animals could not survive.
translations.hypothesis: We use trees to build houses and make clothes. Many of the foods we eat come from trees. If there were no trees, animals would not be able to survive.

translations.source: Mosasaurus bụbu isi n'anụ na-eri anụ n’oge ya, nke a mere na onweghi ihe na-atụ ya egwu, karịa mosasaurs ibe ya.
translations.reference: Mosasaurus was the apex predator of its time, so it feared nothing, except other mosasaurs.
translations.hypothesis: The Mosasaurus was a top predator in its time, largely because it had no natural enemies other than other Mosasaurs.

translations.source: Agba ogologo ya bụ nke emejupụtara n'iji ihe karịrị eze dị aguba-nkọ iri asaa, yana òtú òtù mmezi n'elu ọnụ ya, nke pụtara na ọ nweghị ụzọ mgbapụ maka ihe ọ bụla gafere n'ụzọ ya.
translations.reference: Its long jaws were studded with more than 70 razor-sharp teeth, along with an extra set in the roof of its mouth, meaning that there was no escape for anything that crossed its path.
translations.hypothesis: The long beard, meticulously crafted from over seventy strands of white hair, and the elaborate arrangement above his lips, signify that he is unyielding and will not compromise on anything.

translations.source: Onweghị anyị anya, mana ọ dịka onwere ire abụọ. Ọ na eri mbe mmiri, nnukwu azụ, anụ ndị yiri ya, onwekwara ike na eri ụdị nke ya.
translations.reference: We don't know for sure, but it may have had a forked tongue. Its diet included turtles, large fish, other mosasaurs, and it may even have been a cannibal.
translations.hypothesis: It has no eyes, but it has two rows of teeth. It eats water, large fish, and other animals, and it can also consume its own kind.

translations.source: Ọ wakpọkwara ihe ọ bụla banyere n’ime mmiri ahụ; ọbụná nnukwu dainosọọ dị ka T. rex abụghị atụ n’ebe ọ nọ.
translations.reference: It also attacked anything that entered the water; even a giant dinosaur such as T. rex would be no match for it.
translations.hypothesis: He found nothing of interest within the water; not even a creature as large as a T. rex could compare to what was there.

translations.source: Ka anyị maara nke ọma imirikiti nri ha, ndị Rom nwere oke ha na ihe erimeeri ijuanya ma ọ bụ pụrụ iche, gụnyere ezi ọhịa, piikọkụ, ejula, na ụdị oke akpọrọ dormouse.
translations.reference: While most of their food would be familiar to us, Romans did have their share of strange or unusual feast items, including wild boar, peacock, snails, and a type of rodent called a dormouse
translations.hypothesis: To fully understand Roman cuisine, it's important to note their fondness for a wide variety of meats and game, including wild boar, pheasant, duck, and even dormice.

translations.source: Ihe ọzọ dị iche bụ na ebe ndị ogbenye na nwanyị ahụ riri nri ha ka ha nọ ọdụ n'oche, ndị ọgaranya na-enwe mmasị inwe mmemme oriri ebe ha ga-eri nke ha n'ezumike.
translations.reference: Another difference was that while the poor people and the woman ate their food while sitting in chairs, the rich men liked to have banquets together where they would lounge on their sides while they ate their meals.
translations.hypothesis: Another key difference is that while the couple ate their meal sitting at a table, the wealthy often prefer to have formal dining events where they can enjoy their meals in a more elaborate setting.

translations.source: Ụmụ nri Ndị Rome Ndị mgbe ochie enwughị ike ịgụnye nri ndị batara Yurop site na Amerịka ma ọ bụ Eshịa na narị afọ ndị na-esotenu.
translations.reference: Ancient Roman meals couldn't have included foods that came to Europe from America or from Asia in later centuries.
translations.hypothesis: Ancient Roman cooks were unable to incorporate foods that arrived in Europe from America or the East during the subsequent centuries.

translations.source: Na imaatu, ha enweghi oka, nweghi tomato, nweghi poteto, nweghi koko, na onweghi onye Rome mgbeochie deturu anu toro-toro ire.
translations.reference: For instance, they didn't have corn, nor tomatoes, nor potatoes, nor cocoa, and no ancient Roman ever tasted a turkey.
translations.hypothesis: Initially, they had no flour, no tomatoes, no potatoes, no cocoa, and no Roman soldier had ever seen a piece of chocolate.

translations.source: Ndị Babịlọn rụrụ otu n’ime chi ha otu isi ụlọ nsọ nke e were ka ebe obibi chi ahụ.
translations.reference: The Babylonians built each of their gods a primary temple that was considered the home of the god.
translations.hypothesis: The Babylonians built one of their temples with a central hall that served as the dwelling place of the deity.

translations.source: Ebe ndị mmadụ wetaara chi ndị ahụ aja, ndị nchụ aja ahụ maka ihe ha bụ chi na-achọ, site n'emume na mmemme di iche iche.
translations.reference: People would bring sacrifices to the gods and the priests would try to attend to the needs of the gods through ceremonies and festivals.
translations.hypothesis: People bring offerings to the deities, and the priests offer these sacrifices on behalf of those seeking the deities' favor, through various ceremonies and rituals.

translations.source: Ulo-uka n’otu n’otu nwere mbara-ezi ulo-uka ma nwekazie ime ebe nchuaja ebe nani onye-isi nchu-aja nwere-ike ibanye.
translations.reference: Each temple had an open temple courtyard and then an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter.
translations.hypothesis: Each room in the house had its own distinct smell, and there was also a large storage room where the head of the household kept important items.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ oge a na arụnye ụlọ elu nwere oyiyi oiramid, ndị akpọrọ ziggurats, ka ha bụrụ osonye ụlọ okpukpe.
translations.reference: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples.
translations.hypothesis: Sometimes, tall buildings with stepped structures, known as ziggurats, were built as part of religious complexes.

translations.source: Elu ụlọ elu a bụ ebe dị nsọ pụrụ iche nye chi ahụ.
translations.reference: The top of the tower was special sanctuary for the god.
translations.hypothesis: The family shrine is a sacred and special place dedicated to the deity.

translations.source: Na ekpem-oku nke udidi na mba ndi etiti owuwa-anyanwu, ulo ahu abachaghi uru.
translations.reference: In the warm climate of the Middle East, the house was not so important.
translations.hypothesis: The building, located in a central area of the city, had lost its value.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ihe ezinụlọ ndị juu a mere, ọ bụ n'anya onye ọbụla ka ha mere ya.
translations.reference: Most of the life of the Hebrew family happened in the open air.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the actions taken by these leaders were seen as beneficial by most people.

translations.source: Ụmụ nwanyị siri nri na mbara eze; ụmụ ụlọ ahịa wụbụ naanị ọgụego mepere emepe na-elefe anya n'okporo ámá. E jire okwute maka ịrụ ụlọ.
translations.reference: Women did the cooking in the yard; stores were just open counters looking into the street. Stone was used for building houses.
translations.hypothesis: Women were preparing food in the palace; the shopkeepers stood outside, openly watching the street. Stone was used for construction.

translations.source: O nweghị ụmụ ọhịa buru ibu n’ala nke Keenan, ya mere osisi na-ada oke ọnụ.
translations.reference: There were no large forests in the land of Canaan, so wood was extremely expensive.
translations.hypothesis: There are very few herbivores in Keenan's territory, which is why the trees are so abundant.

translations.source: Ndị mmadụ anọjughị otu ebe na Grinland. N'akụkọ Norse ha sị na achụfuru Erik the Red n'obodo Iceland n'ihi igbu ọchụ, ma mgbe ọ na aga njem na mgbada ọdịda anyanwụ, ọchọpụtara Grinland wee gụọ ya Grinland.
translations.reference: Greenland was settled sparsely. In the Norse sagas they say that Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for murder, and when travelling further west, found Greenland and named it Greenland.
translations.hypothesis: Four people are believed to have lived in Greenland. According to Norse sagas, Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for manslaughter, and during his voyage westward, he discovered Greenland and named it accordingly.

translations.source: Mana n'agbanyeghi nchọpụta ya, agbụrụ Ezkimo ebirilarị ebe ahụ n'oge ahụ.
translations.reference: But regardless of his discovery, Eskimo tribes were already living there at the time.
translations.hypothesis: However, despite his discovery, the Eskimo people did not live in that area at that time.

translations.source: N'agbanyeghị na obodo ọbụla bụ 'mba Skandinevia', enwere ọtụtụ ihe dị iche n'etiti ndị, ndị eze, omenala, na akụkọ ihe mere na Denmak, Swiden, Nọọwe na Aisland.
translations.reference: Though each country was 'Scandinavian', there were many differences between the people, kings, customs and history of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Iceland.
translations.hypothesis: Despite the fact that all the countries are part of "Scandinavia," there are many differences between them in terms of people, royalty, customs, and history in Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Iceland.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ileela ihe nkiri a na-akpọ Akụ nke Mba, i nwere ike chee na e dere otu maapụ akụ n'azụ nke Nkwupụta nke Nnwere Onwe ahụ.
translations.reference: If you have watched the movie National Treasure, you may think a treasure map was written on the back of the Declaration of Independence.
translations.hypothesis: If you watch the movie "The Nation's Story," you might think that a particular economic narrative underlies the Declaration of Independence.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị, nke ahụ abụghị eziokwu. N’agbanyeghị na enwere ihe edere n’azụ nke dọkumentị ahụ, ọ bụghị otu maapụ akụ.
translations.reference: However, that is not true. Although there is something written on the back of the document, it is not a treasure map.
translations.hypothesis: However, that is not the case. While there may be some writing on the back of the document, it is not a financial record.

translations.source: Ka-edere na azu nkwuputa nke nnoro-onwe bu okwua “Nkwuputa nke Nnoro-onwe Nke bu ezie ubochi abali 4 juli 1776” .Ederede ahu putara na ala-ala akwukwo ahu, kpodo isi na-ala.
translations.reference: Written on the back of the Declaration of Independence were the words "Original Declaration of Independence dated 4th July 1776". The text appears on the bottom of the document, upside down.
translations.hypothesis: The declaration, a famous document known as the "Declaration of Independence," was formally adopted on July 4, 1776. The document was carefully written and presented with great solemnity.

translations.source: Ọ bụ ezie na ọnweghị onye maara nke ọma onye dere ya, amaara na mmalite na ndụ ya, afụkọtara nnukwu dọkụment e jiri akpụkpọ anụ mee (o nwere nha inchì 29¾ site na inchì 24½) ọnụ maka nchekwa.
translations.reference: While no one knows for certain who wrote it, it is known that early in its life, the large parchment document (it measures 29¾ inches by 24½ inches) was rolled up for storage.
translations.hypothesis: Although the author remains unknown, it is known that the manuscript, which was originally created on animal skin (measuring 29¾ inches by 24½ inches), was carefully preserved.

translations.source: Ya mere, ọ dị ka agbakwụnyere ihe ngosi a dị ka akara njirimara naanị.
translations.reference: So, it is likely that the notation was added simply as a label.
translations.hypothesis: Therefore, it seems this exhibition was presented primarily as a form of identification.

translations.source: Ubochi-ubochi nladata ya agha ndi na esota atohapula mpaghara ugwu nke France, mana mpaghara ndida enwerebekwa onwe ha.
translations.reference: The D-Day landings and the following battles had freed the north of France, but the south still wasn't free.
translations.hypothesis: While daily rainfall patterns are affecting the northern region of France, other areas are experiencing their own unique weather conditions.

translations.source: Ndị chịrị ya bụ ndị "Vichy" French. Ndị a bụ ndị mba Frans ndị ha na ndị mba Jamini mere udo n'afọ 1940 ma soro ndị iro rụkọọ ọrụ karịa ịlụso ha ọgụ.
translations.reference: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.
translations.hypothesis: These individuals were "Vichy" French collaborators. They were French citizens who made peace with the German occupiers in the 1940s and chose to cooperate with the enemy rather than fight against them.

translations.source: N'ụbọchị nke iri na ise nke ọnwa Ọgọọstụ n'afọ 1940, ndị enyi busoro mpaghara ndịda nke Frans agha, akpọrọ nke a "Operation Dragoon".
translations.reference: On 15 August 1940, the Allies invaded southern France, the invasion was called "Operation Dragoon".
translations.hypothesis: On August 15, 1944, Allied forces landed in the southern region of France in an operation codenamed "Operation Dragoon."

translations.source: N'ime nanị izu abụọ ndị agha America na Ndị French nke Nweere onwe ha emeela ka ndịda France nwere onwe ha ma wee na-atụgharị echewe ihu na Germany.
translations.reference: In just two weeks the Americans and Free French forces had liberated southern France and were turning towards Germany.
translations.hypothesis: In just these past two weeks, American and French forces have liberated southern France and are now turning their attention towards Germany.

translations.source: Ọdịnala bụ otu omenaala ọha mmadụ buru ibu na-ebi ma na-arụkọ ọrụ ọnụ, a na-akpọ ọha mmadụ a sosayiti.
translations.reference: A civilization is a singular culture shared by a significant large group of people who live and work co-operatively, a society.
translations.hypothesis: Culture is a significant aspect of human life and social interaction within a community, which is referred to as society.

translations.source: Ahịrịokwu "civilization" si n'okwu Latin bụ civilis, nke pụtara "gbasara obodo", nke metụtara okwu Latin bụ civis, nke pụtara onye obodo, na civitas, nke pụtara obodo maọbụ obodo-steeti, nke ahụ nwekwara otu o si egosi nha nke ọha mmadụ.
translations.reference: The word civilization comes from the Latin civilis, meaning civil, related to the Latin civis, meaning citizen, and civitas, meaning city or city-state, and that also somehow defines the size of the society.
translations.hypothesis: The word "civilization" originates from the Latin word "civilis," which means "relating to the city" or "urban." This, in turn, is derived from the Latin words "civis," meaning "citizen," and "civitas," meaning "city" or "city-state." The term also implies a certain level of societal development.

translations.source: Steeti-obodo gasị bụ obu ụzọ nke ụmụ mba. Omenaala kemmepeanya pụtara nnyefe nke ihe ọmụma n'etiti ọtụtụ ọgbọ, akaraụkwụ omenaala nke ka nọ ya na mgbasa dịtụ mma.
translations.reference: City-states are the precursors of nations. A civilizational culture implies the passing on of knowledge across several generations, a lingering cultural footprint and fair dissemination.
translations.hypothesis: State-level governance is a crucial aspect of national development. Cultural heritage represents the transmission of knowledge between generations, and its preservation is essential for a thriving society.

translations.source: Ụmụ obere ọdịnala na-apụ n'anya na-ahapụghị ihe akaebe dị mkpa ya mere anaghị ahụta ha dị ka sivilaịzeshọn kwesịrị ekwesị.
translations.reference: Minor cultures often vanish without leaving relevant historic evidence and fail to be recognized as proper civilizations.
translations.hypothesis: Traditional customs, though often charming, can sometimes be so significant that they prevent a society from being considered fully modernized.

translations.source: Ka a na alụ agha ntụgharị, steeti iri na atọ ahụ bu ụzọ gbakọọ bido gọọmenti nchịkọta nke na adịghị ike - nke nzukọ bụ sọ ngalaba onwere- n'okpuru akwụkwọ obodo.
translations.reference: During the Revolutionary War, the thirteen states first formed a weak central government—with the Congress being its only component—under the Articles of Confederation.
translations.hypothesis: As the war for independence progressed, the thirteen colonies moved towards establishing a unified government with executive power, a body that would eventually become the federal government under the Constitution.

translations.source: Nzukọ enweghị ike ike ụtụ ma n'ihi na enweghi ndị isi ọchịchị gọọmenti etiti maọbụ ndị omeiwu, ọ dabeere na ndị isi ọchịchị steeti, ndị anaghị enwe otu obi ọtụtụ oge ịkwado iwu ya nile.
translations.reference: Congress lacked any power to impose taxes, and, because there was no national executive or judiciary, it relied on state authorities, who were often uncooperative, to enforce all its acts.
translations.hypothesis: The legislative process is often ineffective because there is a lack of strong central government leadership or experienced lawmakers. Instead, it relies on state governors, who often have conflicting priorities and may not consistently support the legislation.

translations.source: O nweghi ikike imechi iwu ụtụisi na tarifu n'etiti steeti na steeti.
translations.reference: It also had no authority to override tax laws and tariffs between states.
translations.hypothesis: There should be no restrictions on the movement of goods and tariffs between states.

translations.source: Ederede ahụ chọrọ nkweta steeti niile n'enweghi mgbagha tupu enwee ike imezi ha ma steeti ga weere gọọmentị etiti n'ihe efu ruo na ndị nnọchiteanya ha anaghị abịa.
translations.reference: The Articles required unanimous consent from all the states before they could be amended and states took the central government so lightly that their representatives were often absent.
translations.hypothesis: The bill requires unanimous approval from all states before it can be implemented, and the federal government will remain in a state of emergency until their representatives arrive.

translations.source: Ndị otu egwuregwu bọọlụ ukwu nke mba Itali, ya na ndị otu egwuregwu bọọlụ ukw nke mba Jamani bu ndị kacha eme nke ọma n'otu bọọlụ ukwu na mbaụwa ma bụrụkwa ndị nwetara mmeri n’iko mbaụwa nke afo 2006.
translations.reference: Italy's national football, along with German national football team is the second most successful team in the world and were the FIFA World Cup champions in 2006.
translations.hypothesis: The national football teams of Italy and Germany are among the most successful in the world and were both finalists in the 2006 World Cup.

translations.source: Egwuregwu ndị a ma ama gụnyere futbọl, basketbọl, volleybọl, polo-mmiri, fencing, rugby, ịgba ịnyịnya, hockey ice, hockey roller na ịgba ọsọ ụgbọ ala F1.
translations.reference: Popular sports include football, basketball, volleyball, water-polo, fencing, rugby, cycling, ice hockey, roller hockey and F1 motor racing.
translations.hypothesis: These popular sports include football, basketball, volleyball, water polo, fencing, rugby, archery, ice hockey, roller hockey, and Formula 1 racing.

translations.source: Egwuregwu oge oyi kachasị ewu ewu n'ugwu, ebe ndị mba Italy so asọ mpi n'egwuregwu mba na mba makwa na Olimpik.
translations.reference: Winter sports are most popular in the Northern regions, with Italians competing in international games and Olympic events.
translations.hypothesis: The most popular winter sport in the mountains is skiing, where Italian athletes compete in national and international competitions, as well as at the Olympics.

translations.source: Mba Japan nwere isuo ruru nde asaa (nke kachasị ibu bụ isuo Honshu), nke a mere mba Japan isuo nke asaa kacha ibu n'ụwa.
translations.reference: Japans holds nearly 7,000 islands (the biggest being Honshu), making Japan the 7th largest island in the world!
translations.hypothesis: Japan consists of over six thousand islands, with Honshu being the largest. This makes Japan the country with the seventh-largest number of islands in the world.

translations.source: N’ihi mkọkụlọta/òtù agwaetiti ahụ Japan nwere, a na-arụnyekarị Japan aka, n’elu etu ala ndị ahụ sị guzogide, dị ka "archipelago"
translations.reference: Due to the cluster/group of islands Japan has, Japan is often referred to, on a geographical stance, as an "archipelago"
translations.hypothesis: Due to the fragmented and island-like nature of the Japanese landmass, Japan is often referred to as an "archipelago," highlighting how these islands are arranged.

translations.source: Mbido mmepe Taịwan malitere n’oge gara aga nke narị afọ iri na ise mgbe ndị ọkwụ ụgbọ mmiri Ndị Yurop na-agafe dekọrọ aha agwaetiti ahụ dị ka Ilha Formosa, ma ọ bụ agwaetiti mara mma.
translations.reference: Taiwan beginning start way back in 15th century where European sailors passing by record the island’s name as Ilha Formosa, or beautiful island.
translations.hypothesis: The development of Taiwan began long ago in the 16th century when European sailors passing through the area named the island "Ilha Formosa," meaning "beautiful island."

translations.source: N'afọ 1624, Ụlọọrụ Dọch Isti Indịa mepere ụlọọrụ na ndịda ọdịdaanyanwụ Taịwan, bido mgbanwe n'otu e si emepụta mkpụrụ n'oge gboo, ma wee ndị ọkpọkọọrụ Chaịna ka ha rụọ ọrụ n'ugbo osikapa na nke shuga ha.
translations.reference: In 1624,Dutch East India Company establishes a base in southwestern Taiwan, initiating a transformation in aboriginal grain production practices and employing Chinese laborers to work on its rice and sugar plantations.
translations.hypothesis: In 1624, the Dutch East India Company established a trading post in southwestern Taiwan, initiating a shift in the production of crops and subsequently employing Chinese laborers on their sugar and rice plantations.

translations.source: N'afọ 1683, ndị agha ezinụlọ ọchịchị Shịng (1644-1912) weghaara akụkụ mmiri Taịwan dị n'ọdịda anyanwụ na nke dị n'ugwu ma kwuputa na Taịwan bụzi mpaghara n'okpuru ọchịchị Alaeze Shịng n'afọ 1885.
translations.reference: In 1683, Qing dynasty (1644-1912) forces take control of Taiwan’s western and northern coastal areas and declared Taiwan as a province of the Qing Empire in 1885.
translations.hypothesis: In 1683, the military forces of the Qing Dynasty (1644-1912) conquered the southwestern and southeastern parts of Taiwan and declared that Taiwan was a territory under the rule of the Qing Dynasty in 1885.

translations.source: Na 1895, mgbe a dachara n’Agha Sino-Japanese Mbụ (1894-1895), ọchịchị Qing ahụ mere mbịanye aka na Nkwekọrịta nke Shimonoseki ahụ, site na nke o jiri nyefee Japan ọbụbụeze nke Taiwan, nke na-achị agwaetiti ahụ ruo 1945.
translations.reference: In 1895, after defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, by which it cedes sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which rules the island until 1945.
translations.hypothesis: In 1895, after the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing dynasty signed the Treaty of Shimonoseki, through which it ceded the sovereignty of Taiwan to Japan, which then governed the island until 1945.
