translations.source: Machu Picchu nwere ọdịdị atọ, ya bụ Intihuatana, Ụlọ Nsọ nke Anyanwu, yana Ime ụlọ nke Windo Atọ.
translations.reference: Machu Picchu consist of three main structures, namely Intihuatana, the Temple of the Sun, and the Room of the Three Windows.
translations.hypothesis: Machu Picchu has three distinct structures: Intihuatana, the Temple of the Sun, and the Complex of Three Windows.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ n'ime ụlọ ndị nọ na mpụta ogige ụlọ ahụ ka arụgharịrị ka enwee ike gosi ndị njem nleta echiche etu ha siri pụta na mbụ.
translations.reference: Most of the buildings on the edges of the complex have been rebuilt in order to give tourists a better idea of how they originally appeared.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the buildings in the historical village have been restored to showcase what they were originally like, giving visitors a sense of how the area looked in the past.

translations.source: Mgbe 1976 ruru, e mezigharịala pasent iri atọ nke Machu Pichu; mmezi a ka na-aga n'ihu ruo taa.
translations.reference: By 1976, thirty percent of Machu Picchu had been restored and restoration continues till today.
translations.hypothesis: By 1976, thirty percent of Machu Picchu had been restored; these restoration efforts continue to this day.

translations.source: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, nhàzi nka osise onyinyo nkwụ n'otu ebe a na-ahụkarị n'ụwa niile bụ 35mm, nke bụ nha fim kachasị ewu ewu na ngwụcha oge fim analọgụ.
translations.reference: For example, the most common still image photography format in the world is 35mm, which was the dominant film size at the close of the analog film era.
translations.hypothesis: For example, a standard focal length for a wide-angle lens, commonly used worldwide, is 35mm, which was the most popular film focal length at the end of the analog film era.

translations.source: A ka na-emepụta ya taa, mana ihe ka mkpa bụ na ụdịdị sensọ foto nke igwefoto dijital eketala aspekt reshiyo ya.
translations.reference: It is still produced today, but more importantly its aspect ratio has been inherited by digital camera image sensor formats.
translations.hypothesis: While it's being manufactured today, what's more important is that the type of image sensor used in digital cameras has already reached its resolution limit.

translations.source: Ọ dịtụ mgbagwoju anya na, n'ezie, ụdịdị 35mm nwere 36mm n'obosara na 24mm n'ogo.
translations.reference: The 35mm format is actually, somewhat confusingly, 36mm in width by 24mm in height.
translations.hypothesis: It's confusing, but essentially, a 35mm lens has a 36mm diameter and a 24mm focal length.

translations.source: akuku rashio nke usoro a ( iji iri na-abuo were nweta rashio onu ogugu dikasiri mfe) bu 3:2 maka nke a.
translations.reference: The aspect ratio of this format (dividing by twelve to obtain the simplest whole-number ratio) is therefore said to be 3:2.
translations.hypothesis: The ratio of this sequence (using the method of dividing by the same number to obtain a simpler ratio) is 3:2 for this case.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ usoro nkịtị (dịka usoro APS si n'otu ezinaụlọ) ga-abụ otu ihe maọbụ ruo ihe dịka nkepụta nkewa a.
translations.reference: Many common formats (APS family of formats, for example) are equal to or closely approximate this aspect ratio.
translations.hypothesis: Many standard procedures (such as the APS protocol from a particular manufacturer) will be the same or very similar up to this point.

translations.source: Iwu nke atọ ndị a na-akparị ma na-akwakarị oke emu bụ usoro dị mfe na-emepụta ịdịmgbanwò dị ka ọ na-edotekwa otu ụhara usoro ọrụ n'ime otu onyinyo.
translations.reference: The much-abused and often-ridiculed rule of thirds is a simple guideline creating dynamism while keeping a measure of order in an image.
translations.hypothesis: These three common and often misunderstood rules are simple guidelines that promote consistency and maintain a unified style throughout a piece of writing.

translations.source: O kwuru na ebe kachasị dị ire maka isi nke isiokwu bụ na mmekọta ụmụ ahịrị na-ekebi ụmụ onyinyo ahụ n’ụzọ atọ na nke eguzoro ọtọ nakwa nke a mara afọ n’ala (hụ ọmụmatụ).
translations.reference: It states that the most effective place for the main subject is at the intersection of lines dividing the image into thirds vertically and horizontally (see example).
translations.hypothesis: He stated that the most important aspect of the topic is that the combination of the three factors – the number of rows, the number of columns, and the age of the individuals – significantly affects the results (see example).

translations.source: N'oge a na Yurop, e bidoro lebawa anya n'Ụka Katọlik, nke bagoro ụba ma dị ike.
translations.reference: During this period of European history, the Catholic Church, which had become rich and powerful, came under scrutiny.
translations.hypothesis: During that time in Europe, there was a growing interest in the Catholic Church, which was expanding and gaining influence.

translations.source: Kamgbe ihe karịrị otu puku afọ, okpukpe Ndị Kraịst jikọtara obodo ndị dị na Yuropu n'agbanyeghị na asụsụ na omenala ha dịgasị iche.
translations.reference: For over a thousand years the Christian religion had bound European states together despite differences in language and customs. I
translations.hypothesis: For over a thousand years, the Christian faith has connected towns across Europe, despite their diverse languages and cultures.

translations.source: Ike ya juputara ebe niile metụtara onye ọbụla site n'eze ruo na mmadụ nkịtị.
translations.reference: Its all-pervading power affected everyone from king to commoner.
translations.hypothesis: His influence extended to every aspect of life, affecting everyone from the ruler to the common person.

translations.source: Otu n'ime isi okwu okwukwe Ndị Kristian bu na ekwesiri iji akụ belata nhụjuanya na ịda ogbenye nakwa na ego ụka nọ kpọmkwem ebe ahụ n'ihi nke ahụ.
translations.reference: One of the main Christian tenets is that wealth should be used to alleviate suffering and poverty and that the monetary funds of the church are there specifically for that reason.
translations.hypothesis: One of the central tenets of Christian faith is the idea that material possessions should be used to alleviate suffering and poverty, and that wealth should be distributed fairly.

translations.source: Ikike keetiti ahụ nke ụlọ uka anọọla n'ime Rom karịa otu puku afọ ma mkpọkọnata ike na ego a duru ọtụtụ ndị ịjụ sị ma a na-esokwa ụkpụrụ ya.
translations.reference: The central authority of the church had been in Rome for over a thousand years and this concentration of power and money led many to question whether this tenet was being met.
translations.hypothesis: The Colosseum, a landmark in Rome, is over a thousand years old, but its enduring strength and grandeur have made it a popular tourist destination and a symbol of its time.

translations.source: Ka agha dara, mba Britenị jiri ndị agha elu mmiri gbochie ndị Jamani inweta enyemaka
translations.reference: Soon after the outbreak of hostilities, Britain initiated a naval blockade of Germany.
translations.hypothesis: As the war progressed, the British navy used its superior naval power to prevent German reinforcements from reaching their troops.

translations.source: Atụmatụ ahụ rụrụ ọrụ ọfụma, na-ebepụ ụmụ ihe mbute ihe ndị agha na ndị nkiti dị oke mpka, n’agbanyeghị na mgbochi a dara iwu mba ụwa anabatara n’izugbe nke ọtụtụ nkwekọrịta n’etiti mba ụwa nke afọ narị abụọ gara aga nyere ikikere.
translations.reference: The strategy proved effective, cutting off vital military and civilian supplies, although this blockade violated generally accepted international law codified by several international agreements of the past two centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The plan worked effectively, separating combatants and civilians, despite the fact that this approach violated international law, as it contradicted several international agreements from the past century that guaranteed certain rights.

translations.source: Briten tinyere ogbunigwe na mmiri ọha mba igbochi ụgbọ mmiri ọbụla ịbata, nke a abụrụ ihe ize ndụ nye ụgbọ mmiri ndị esoghi alụ agha.
translations.reference: Britain mined international waters to prevent any ships from entering entire sections of ocean, causing danger to even neutral ships.
translations.hypothesis: Britain has deployed mines in the waters off the coast of the Igbo region, posing a danger to civilian vessels.

translations.source: Ebe nzaghachi ihe omume a pere mpe, mba Jamini lere anya na a ga emekwa otu ihe n'ebe agha okpuru mmiri nọ.
translations.reference: Since there was limited response to this tactic, Germany expected a similar response to its unrestricted submarine warfare.
translations.hypothesis: Following this incident, the government of Jammu and Kashmir is considering implementing similar measures in areas where there are frequent clashes.

translations.source: N'oge afọ ndi 1920, agwa kachasị dị ebe nile n'etiti ndị mba dị iche iche bụ nke ịchọ udo na nnọrọ onwe.
translations.reference: During the 1920s, the prevailing attitudes of most citizens and nations was that of pacifism and isolation.
translations.hypothesis: During the 1920s, the most prominent theme among different nations was the pursuit of peace and self-determination.

translations.source: Mgbe a hụchara ụmụ egwu na ajọ ọmụme nke agha n’oge Agha Ụwa I, mba gasị chọrọ izere ụdị ọnọdụ ahụ ọzọ n’ọdịnihu.
translations.reference: After seeing the horrors and atrocities of war during World War I, nations desired to avoid such a situation again in the future.
translations.hypothesis: After witnessing the devastating impact of war propaganda during World War I, many countries sought to avoid similar situations in the future.

translations.source: N'afọ 1884, Tesla kwagara na mba Amerịka ịnara ọrụ na nke Ụlọ ọrụ Edison n'Obodo Niu Yọk.
translations.reference: In 1884, Tesla moved to the United States of America to accept a job with the Edison Company in New York City.
translations.hypothesis: In 1884, Tesla emigrated to the United States to seek employment at the Edison Company in New York City.

translations.source: Ọ bịarutere na US n’inwe centị anọ n’aha ya, otu akwụkwọ nke uri, ya na otu akwụkwọ ozi nke nkwanye sitere na Charles Batchelor (onye njikwa ya n’ọrụ ya gara aga) ruo Thomas Edison.
translations.reference: He arrived in the US with 4 cents to his name, a book of poetry, and a letter of recommendation from Charles Batchelor (his manager in his previous job) to Thomas Edison.
translations.hypothesis: He arrived in the US with only four cents in his pocket, a songbook, and a letter of introduction from his former employer, Charles Batchelor, to Thomas Edison.

translations.source: Chaịna ndị mgbe ochie nwere ụzọ pụrụ iche igosi oge afọ; ogo ọbụla nke Chaịna ma ọ bụ ezinụlọ ọ bụla nọbụrụ n’ọchịchị wụbụ oge ọchịchị eze pụrụ iche.
translations.reference: Ancient China had a unique way of showing different time periods; each stage of China or each family that was in power was a distinctive dynasty.
translations.hypothesis: In ancient China, there were unique ways to mark the passage of time; the age of a person, the status of a family, or the duration of a reign under an emperor were all often measured using specific systems.

translations.source: Nakwa n’etiti usoro ndị eze ọ bụla bụ otu oge ejighị n'aka mke mpaghara ndị kewara ekewa. Oge ndị a nke a kacha mara amara bụ oge nke Alaeze Atọ nke mere ruo afọ iri na isii n'etiti Usoro Ndị Eze Han na Usoro Ndị Eze Jin ndị ahụ.
translations.reference: Also between each dynasty was an unstable age of divided provinces. The best-known of these periods was the Three Kingdoms epoch taking place for 60 years between the Han and the Jin Dynasty.
translations.hypothesis: During the various dynasties, there were periods of political fragmentation. The most well-known of these periods is the Era of the Three Kingdoms, which lasted for nearly a century between the Han and Jin dynasties.

translations.source: N'oge ndị a, a lụrụ ọtụtụ agha n'etiti ndi ukwu na-azọ oche eze.
translations.reference: During these periods fierce warfare took place between many nobles fighting for the throne.
translations.hypothesis: In recent times, there have been numerous conflicts and power struggles among those vying for the throne.

translations.source: Alaeze Atọ so n'otu n'ime ọgbọ kacha dị egwu n'akụkọ ihe mere na mba Chaịna mgbe gboo. Puku kwuru puku mmadụ nwụrụ n'agha ịnọ n'oche ọchịchị nke kachasị elu na nnukwu obi eze nke dị na Xi'an.
translations.reference: The Three Kingdoms was one of the bloodiest eras in Ancient China’s history thousands of people died fighting to sit in the highest seat in the grand palace at Xi’an.
translations.hypothesis: The Three Kingdoms period is one of the most romanticized and significant eras in Chinese history. Hundreds of thousands of people perished in wars fought for control of the highest positions of power and the vast imperial territories centered in Xi'an.

translations.source: Nke a butere ọtụtụ mmetụta na mmekọ mmadụ na ibe ya makwa na ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị dika usoro agụm ọnụ, mgbanwe site n'ọchịchị okwu otu onye gaa na nke okwu mba, nke obodo na nkwenye na obodo bụ nke ọha karịa ịbụ nke otu onye ọchịchị.
translations.reference: There are a lot of social and political effects such as the use of metric system, a shift from absolutism to republicanism, nationalism and the belief the country belongs to the people not to one sole ruler.
translations.hypothesis: This has significant implications for interpersonal relationships and for governance, including the development of legal systems, the transition from autocratic rule to systems based on dialogue, and the recognition that the community is more important than the individual ruler.

translations.source: Ọzọkwa mgbe ụmụ aka ọrụ Mgbanwe ọchịchị ahụ mepechara maka ụmụ nwoke ọchọ ọrụ niile na-ekwe ka ndị kacha nwee oké ọchịchọ na ihe ịga nke ọma ka ha gaa nke ọma.
translations.reference: Also after the Revolution occupations were open to all male applicants allowing the most ambitious and successful to succeed.
translations.hypothesis: Once again, the government's job application portal is open to all job seekers, and we encourage those who are most qualified and driven to apply.

translations.source: Ọ bụkwa otu ihe ahụ n'amị, maka na kama nhazi n'usoro nke ndị amị ga-adabere n'ogugo, ọ daberezie n'ikikere.
translations.reference: Same goes for the military because instead of army rankings being based on class they were now based on cailaber.
translations.hypothesis: It's also a matter of fairness, because instead of relying on a numerical formula to determine who gets what, it depends on what is right and just.

translations.source: Mgbanwe France melitere obi ndi oru ana emegbu emegbu no gasi na mba ndi ozo ha ewere wee ike ibido mgbanwe nke ha.
translations.reference: The French Revolution also inspired many other repressed working class people of other country's to began their own revolutions.
translations.hypothesis: The French reforms have boosted the morale of workers in other countries and inspired them to initiate similar changes.

translations.source: Muhammad nwere ezigbo mmasị n’ụmụ okwu gabigara ụwa a na-agwụ ike. Ọ dịbụ na-agakarị n’otu nnukwu ọnụala nke emechara mara dị ka “Hira‘” n’ugwu nke “Noor” (light) maka ntụgharị ụche.
translations.reference: Muhammad was deeply interested in matters beyond this mundane life. He used to frequent a cave that became known as “Hira‘” on the Mountain of “Noor” (light) for contemplation.
translations.hypothesis: Muhammad had a deep interest in the stories of prophets who came before him. He would often gather with a large group of people in a place known as "Hira'" on the mountain of "Noor" (light) for contemplation and discussion.

translations.source: ọgba ahụ n'onwe ya, nke lanarịrị oge ndị a, na-enye ezigbo ihe ngosi maka echiche gbasara ihe mmụọ nke Muhammad.
translations.reference: he cave itself, which survived the times, gives a very vivid image of Muhammad’s spiritual inclinations.
translations.hypothesis: The ongoing conflict, in its own way, provides a stark illustration of the spiritual complexities surrounding the figure of Muhammad.

translations.source: Na-ezu ike n’elu otu n’ime ugwu ndị nọ n’uwgu nke Meeka, nnukwu ọnụala dịpụrụ adịpụ n’ozuzu site n’akụkụ ụwa ndị ọzọ niile
translations.reference: Resting on the top of one of the mountains north of Mecca, the cave is completely isolated from the rest of the world.
translations.hypothesis: High up on one of the peaks of the Meeka mountains, a massive chasm stretches across the landscape, seemingly separating it from the rest of the world.

translations.source: N'ezie, ọ dịghị mfe maọlị ịchọta, ọbụrụgodi na mmadụ maara na ọ dị. Ozugbo abanyere n'ime ọgba ahụ, ọ bụ ndịpụ kpam kpam.
translations.reference: In fact, it is not easy to find at all even if one knew it existed. Once inside the cave, it is a total isolation.
translations.hypothesis: Indeed, it's not easy to find, even if someone knows it exists. Once you're inside, it's a complete transformation.

translations.source: O nweghị ihe ọzọ enwere ike ịhụ na-abụghị eluigwe dị n’elu gbachapụrụ, maa mma na ọtụtụ ugwu gbara gburugburu. Nanị obere nke ụwa ka enwere ike ịhụ ma ọ bụ nụ site n’ime nnukwu ọnụala ahụ.
translations.reference: Nothing can be seen other than the clear, beautiful sky above and the many surrounding mountains. Very little of this world can be seen or heard from inside the cave.
translations.hypothesis: There was nothing to see except the vast expanse of the sky above, framed by the surrounding mountains. Only a small portion of the world was visible or audible from within the large opening.

translations.source: Oke Piramid na Giza bụ naanị nke ka kwụ taa n'ime ihe itụnanya asaa ahụ.
translations.reference: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today.
translations.hypothesis: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World that still exists today.

translations.source: Ndị Ijipt rụrụ n’ime narị afọ atọ BCE, Oke Piramidi ahụ otu n’ime ọtụtụ nnukwu ihe ọwụwụ piramidi arụrụ ịkwanye Fero nwụrụ ugwu.
translations.reference: Built by the Egyptians in the third century BCE, the Great Pyramid is one of many large pyramid structures built to honor dead Pharaoh.
translations.hypothesis: The Egyptian pyramids, built over a period of three centuries BCE, are among the most impressive examples of ancient pyramid structures, constructed to honor the deceased pharaohs.

translations.source: Ala ugwu Giza maọbụ "Giza Nekropolis" nke dị na ndagwurugwu ọnwụ Ijipt nwere ọtụtụ piramid (nke piramid ukwu bụ nke kachasị ibu), ọtụtụ ebe olili, ọtụtụ ụlọ ofufe nakwa oke Sfinks.
translations.reference: The Giza Plateau, or "Giza Necropolis" in the Egyptian Valley of the Dead contains several pyramids (of which the great pyramid is the largest), several small tombs, several temples, and the great Sphinx.
translations.hypothesis: The Giza Plateau, also known as the "Giza Necropolis," located in the Egyptian desert, is home to numerous pyramids (the Great Pyramid being the largest), several tombs, various temples, and the Sphinx.

translations.source: Arụrụ oke piramid iji kwanyere Eze Khufu zugwu, ya na ọtụtụ piramid obere ndị ọzọ, ebe olili na ụlọ ofufe arụrụ ịkwanyere ndị inyom Khufu na ezinụlọ ya ugwu.
translations.reference: The great pyramid was created to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members.
translations.hypothesis: A large pyramid was built to honor Pharaoh Khufu, along with several smaller pyramids and other structures that served as tombs for Khufu's wives and family members.

translations.source: Akara “ụta elu” ahụ yiri otu V ma akara “ụta ala” ahụ yiri otu stepụlụ ma ọ bụ otu ǹkomgbaànoǹhà nke tufure ebe okpuru ya.
translations.reference: The "up bow" mark looks like a V and the "down bow mark" like a staple or a square missing its bottom side.
translations.hypothesis: The "upward slope" mark resembled a "V", while the "downward slope" mark resembled a step or a decline from its original position.

translations.source: Elu pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi n'ọnụnụ ya pịa ụta aka, ma ala pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi na fụrọgụ (nke bụ ebe aka gị ji ụta) were dọọ ụta aka.
translations.reference: Up means you should start at the tip and push the bow, and down means you should start at the frog (which is where your hand is holding the bow) and pull the bow.
translations.hypothesis: "Elu" means you should press with the palm of your hand, while "ala" means you should press with the side of your hand (the part of your hand where your pinky finger is).

translations.source: Otu ụta-elu na -emepụtakarị ụda kara dị nro, ebe ụta-ala ka sie ike ma kara kwupụta.
translations.reference: An up-bow usually generates a softer sound, while a down-bow is stronger and more assertive.
translations.hypothesis: The high-pitched notes are often softer, while the low-pitched notes are more powerful and resonant.

translations.source: Detuo akara nke gị na nwere onwe, mana chetakwa na akara ndị ahụ ebiri ebi nwere uru egwu ha bara, n'ihi nke a ha kwesịrị ka akwanyere ha ugwu.
translations.reference: Feel free to pencil in your own marks, but remember the printed bowing marks are there for a musical reason, so they should usually be respected.
translations.hypothesis: Express your individuality, but also remember that traditional symbols hold significant meaning and value, and therefore deserve respect.

translations.source: N'Oktoba 6, 1789, ụmụ nwanyị ahịa iwe ji yiri Eze Luwi XVI oke egwu mgbe ha si na Versailles dọrọ ya, nwunye ya Marịa Antwanet, obere ụmụ ha abụọ (Marịa Teriza dị afọ 11 na Luwi-Chals dị afọ anọ), na nwanne nwanyị Eze, Madam Elizabet, dọghachi ha na Parii.
translations.reference: The terrified King Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette their two young children (11 year old Marie Therese and four year old Louis-Charles) and the King's sister, Madam Elizabeth, on the 6th October 1789 were forced back to Paris from Versailles by a mob of market women.
translations.hypothesis: On October 6, 1789, a crowd of angry women marched from Versailles to Paris, accompanied by King Louis XVI, his wife Marie Antoinette, their two children (11-year-old Marie Thérèse and 4-year-old Louis-Charles), and the King's sister, Madame Elisabeth.

translations.source: Ha laghachiri Paris n'ime moto ịnyịnya ndị iwe na-ewe gbara gburugburu, ha na-eti mkpu na-agwa Eze na Nwunye ya ihe egwu dị iche iche.
translations.reference: In a carriage, they traveled back to Paris surrounded by a mob of people screaming and shouting threats against the King and Queen.
translations.hypothesis: They returned to Paris in a car surrounded by a motorcade of security vehicles, with sirens blaring as they announced the arrival of the King and Queen.

translations.source: Ndị iwe a manyere Eze na Queen ka ha meghee windo ụgbọ ha.
translations.reference: The mob of people forced the King And Queen to have their carriage windows wide open.
translations.hypothesis: These people demanded that the King and Queen open the windows of their car.

translations.source: N'otu mgbe otu n'ime ndị igwe mmadụ fegharịrị isi onye nche eze egburu na Versailles n'ihu eze nwanyi ụjọ ji.
translations.reference: At one point a member of the mob waved the head of a royal guard killed at Versailles in front of the terrified Queen.
translations.hypothesis: At one point, one of the human-powered machines accidentally struck and killed a royal guard in Versailles, causing the queen great distress.

translations.source: Mmefu ego n'agha nke ndị Amerịka mbịarachịwa na mmeri ndị Filipaị bụ nke ndị Filipino kwụrụ ụgwọ ya n’onwe ha.
translations.reference: The war expenditures of U.S. imperialism in the conquest of the Philippines were paid for by the Filipino people themselves.
translations.hypothesis: The financial costs of the American administration and the victory of the Philippines were ultimately borne by the Filipino people themselves.

translations.source: A manyere ha iwu ịkwụ ụtụisi nye ndị ọchịchị mbịarachịwa mba Amerịka iji wedata oke ego e mefuru n'aha gọọmenti mba Filipin site n'aka ụlọakụ Wọlụ Striti.
translations.reference: They were compelled to pay taxes to the U.S. colonial regime to defray a major part of the expenditures and the interest on bonds floated in the name of the Philippine government through the Wall Street banking houses.
translations.hypothesis: They are urging the U.S. government to impose sanctions on individuals and entities involved in the misappropriation of funds from the Philippine government, specifically those linked to the Wolli Street firm.

translations.source: N’eziokwu, nnukwu uru e nwetara na ogologo mmegbu ndị mba Filipiinụ ga-abụ ihe mejuputara isi uru omume empaya Amerịka.
translations.reference: Of course, the superprofits derived from the protracted exploitation of the Filipino people would constitute the basic gains of U.S. imperialism.
translations.hypothesis: Indeed, the significant benefits gained from the long struggle of the Filipino people will be a testament to the enduring values of American democracy.

translations.source: Ịghọta ndị Templars, aghaghi ịghọta ọnọdụ nke kpaliri okike nke otu a.
translations.reference: To understand the Templars one must understand the context that prompted the creation of the order.
translations.hypothesis: To understand the Templars, one must understand the circumstances that led to the creation of this organization.

translations.source: Ọgbọ ihe ndị a mere na ya ka a na-akpọkarị Ọgbọ Etiti dị Elu bụ oge ihe ndị mere na mba Yuropu n'afọ narị iri na otu, narị iri na abụọ na narị iri na atọ (AD 1000-1300).
translations.reference: The age where the events took place is commonly referred as the High Middle Ages the period of European history in the 11th, 12th, and 13th centuries (AD 1000–1300).
translations.hypothesis: The period commonly referred to as the High Middle Ages spans the years from approximately 1000 to 1300 AD in Europe.

translations.source: Ọgbọ etiti ndị nke mbụ butere ọgbọ etiti ndị dị elu ụzọ, nke ọgbọ etiti nke ngwụcha sotere n'azụ nke gwuru ebe 1500.
translations.reference: The High Middle Ages were preceded by the Early Middle Ages and followed by the Late Middle Ages, which by convention ends around 1500.
translations.hypothesis: The first generation of middle-class individuals paved the way for a higher echelon of the middle class, from which the upper class emerged, tracing its origins back to the 1500s.

translations.source: Mkpebi teknụụzụ bụ usoro gazuru nchịkọta nchepụta gasị etinyere n’uju, site na technụụzụ-kwàa maọbụ nye iwu siri ike nke bụ na njedebe nke onye ga-esite n’iwu metụtara sayensi na nke ngosipụta teknụụzụ.
translations.reference: Technological determinism is a term that encompasses a wide range of ideas in practice, from technology-push or the technological imperative to a strict sense that human destiny is driven by an underlying logic associated with scientific laws and their manifestation in technology.
translations.hypothesis: Technological decisions are processes that involve gathering data and applying it, using technology or adhering to strict rules, to reach a conclusion based on scientific principles and technological considerations.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ nkọwa e nyere nkwenyesiike kenkanụzụ nwere echiche izugbe abụọ: na mmepụta nkanụzụ n'onwe ya na-agbaso usoro nke gbapụrụ iche site na nkwanye nke omenala maọbụ ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị, ya na kwa na nkanụzụ n'aka nke ya nwere "mmekpaahụ" ọ na-enye ọhaobodo nke dị adị, n'abụghị nke sitere na mmekọrịta.
translations.reference: Most interpretations of technological determinism share two general ideas: that the development of technology itself follows a path largely beyond cultural or political influence, and that technology in turn has "effects" on societies that are inherent, rather than socially conditioned.
translations.hypothesis: Many interpretations of the concept of sovereignty have two core ideas: firstly, that the state exercises exclusive control over its territory and population, independent of external customs or political influence; and secondly, that the state possesses a certain "autonomy" that allows it to act in the best interests of its citizens, rather than being subject to external pressures or obligations.

translations.source: Maka ọmụmaatụ, mmadụ nwere ike ịsị na ụgbọala n'ịkwesị ekwesị na-eduga na mmepe nke ụzọ gasị.
translations.reference: For example, one might say that the motor car necessarily leads to the development of roads.
translations.hypothesis: For example, someone might argue that the increasing number of cars on the road leads to the development of more highways.

translations.source: N'agbanyeghị nke a, okporo ụzọ zuru obodo ọnụ bụ mmefu ego ma ọbụrụ na ụgbọ ala ehighị nne, ya mere emepụtara ụzọ ọhụrụ ịwedata ego o na ewe inwe ụgbọala.
translations.reference: However, a nationwide road network is not economically viable for just a handful of cars, so new methods of production are developed to reduce the cost of car ownership.
translations.hypothesis: Despite this, toll roads are an expensive undertaking, and the cost of maintaining them can be high. Therefore, new methods are being developed to reduce the financial burden of owning and operating vehicles.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ mmadụ inwe ụgbọ ala na-ebutekwa nnukwu ihe mberede n'okporo ụzọ, nke na-eweta mmepụta usoro nleta ahụike ọhụrụ maka ịrụzi ahụ mebiri emebi.
translations.reference: Mass car ownership also leads to a higher incidence of accidents on the roads, which leads to the invention of new techniques in healthcare for repairing damaged bodies.
translations.hypothesis: The increasing number of cars on the road often leads to serious traffic accidents, which in turn necessitate the development of new medical procedures for treating injuries.

translations.source: Ihunanya ya nwere otutu ihe banyere mmeme nke ọdịnala, nke sitere n'aka ndị edemede dịka Goethe, Fichte, na Schlegel.
translations.reference: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.
translations.hypothesis: Her philosophy contained many elements related to the principles of classicism, drawing inspiration from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.

translations.source: Na onodu romanticism, ala ebe onye no bu ihe na kpu omume mmadu, k’oge na aga odinala na omenala metutara ala ebe obibi amalite, nkea mere ndi mmadu jiri nabata odinala na omenala ndia maka na ha na ya bu odinala na omenala nwere nkwekorita karia iwu ana atukwasa n’isi oha.
translations.reference: In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
translations.hypothesis: In the context of romanticism, the homeland is a place of profound personal significance, and as people increasingly connect with their ancestral roots, the idea of a homeland becomes more important. This is because people see their homeland as a place where they belong, and where they can connect with their history and culture. The homeland is also a place where people can find a sense of community and belonging, which is especially important in a world that is becoming increasingly globalized.

translations.source: N'otu aka a maara Paris ka isi ejiji ịchọ mma n'ụwa nke oge a, e weere Kọnstantinopul dịka isi ejiji ịchọ mma na mba Yuropu n'oge agha.
translations.reference: In the manner that Paris is known as the fashion capital of the contemporary world, Constantinople was regarded as the fashion capital of feudal Europe.
translations.hypothesis: While Paris is known today as a global fashion capital, Constantinople was considered the fashion center of Europe during wartime.

translations.source: Ebidoro n’afo 400A.D. ruo n’afo 1100 A.D were mara ya na o bu isi mkporindu.
translations.reference: Its renown for being an epicenter of luxury began in about 400 A.D. and lasted up until about 1100 A.D.
translations.hypothesis: It flourished from the 4th century A.D. to the 11th century A.D. and was known for its agricultural productivity.

translations.source: Ọkwa na gbadara n’oge narị afọ iri na abụọ tụmadị n’ihi eziokwu bụ na Ndị agha ntute alaghachila ma bute ụmụ onyinye dị ka ụmụ akwa sịlk na ngwa nri ndị nwere mbamuru karịrị ihe ahịa Byzantine nyere.
translations.reference: Its status declined during the twelfth century mainly due to the fact that Crusaders had returned bearing gifts such as silks and spices that were valued more than what Byzantine markets offered.
translations.hypothesis: The exchange rate declined significantly during the 12th century primarily because the Crusaders returned and introduced goods such as silk textiles and foodstuffs that were more valuable than the Byzantine currency.

translations.source: Ọ bụ n'oge ahụ ka okwa isi ejiji ịchọ ma siri na Kọnstantinopul fere Paris.
translations.reference: It was at this time that the transfer of the title of Fashion Capital from Constantinople to Paris was made.
translations.hypothesis: It was during that time that the most important diplomatic missions were conducted, traveling from Constantinople to Paris.

translations.source: Usoro Gotik kasị elu n'oge dị n'etiti afọ ndị nari nke ir na narị nke iri na otu ya na narị nke iri na anọ.
translations.reference: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century.
translations.hypothesis: The peak of Gothic architecture occurred during the mid-12th to mid-13th centuries.

translations.source: Na mbido, ọ bụ usoro ejiji ndị Byzantium n'ọwụwa anyanwụ ka onye ọbụla na-eso.
translations.reference: At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east.
translations.hypothesis: Initially, Byzantine fashion trends were widely followed by people of all social classes.

translations.source: Mana, n'ihi ụkpụrụ mkparịta ụka na adịghị ọsịsọ, usoro dị na ọdịda anyanwụ nwere ike inọzụga azụ n'oteaka afọ iri abụọ na ise ruo iri atọ.
translations.reference: However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year.
translations.hypothesis: However, due to communication protocols and potential delays, the process in the southern region could take anywhere from fifteen to thirty years.

translations.source: na njedebe nke oge Mịdụl Eeji ndị ọdịda anyanwụ Europe malitere mepụtawa usoro nke ha. Otu ihe mmepụta kachasi mkpa n'oge ahụ, n'ihi ọgụ aghara, ndị mmadụ bidoro iji bọtịnụ akpọchị akwa.
translations.reference: towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
translations.hypothesis: During the Middle Ages, European societies began to develop their own distinct characteristics. One of the most significant developments of this period, driven by the onset of warfare, was the increasing use of quilted fabrics.

translations.source: Ugbo oru bu ihe oru ugbo bu nke eweputara iji meputa nri ga ezuru ndi mmadu choro ya ma obu ya na ulo ya.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is agriculture carried out for the production of enough food to meet just the needs of the agriculturalist and his/her family.
translations.hypothesis: Agriculture is the practice of cultivating plants and raising animals for food, fiber, or other products to meet human needs or for personal consumption.

translations.source: Ịkọ ọrụ ugbo bụ ihe dịcha mfe, ọtụtụ mgbe nke ndụ, sistèm n'iji nkpụrụ echekwara bụ nwa afọ na mphaghara ebe obibi ahụ ejikọtara ya na nghagharị mkpụrụ ma ọ bụ usoro ndị ọzọ dị mfe iji mee ka ọmịmị kachasị.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is a simple, often organic, system using saved seed native to the ecoregion combined with crop rotation or other relatively simple techniques to maximize yield.
translations.hypothesis: Farming is often a simple, yet vital, process. It typically involves planting seeds or seedlings in a prepared area, and then providing the necessary care and resources for growth, such as water and nutrients, to maximize yield.

translations.source: Na mgbe gboo ọtụtụ n'ime ndị na-akọ ugbo na-eme ụdị nke onwe n'enweghị nke orire ọ ka dịkwa otu a n'ọtụtụ obodo ka na etolite etolite.
translations.reference: Historically most farmers were engaged in subsistence agriculture and this is still the case in many developing nations.
translations.hypothesis: Unfortunately, many farmers are still engaging in practices that are harmful to the environment, and this problem persists in many communities.

translations.source: Obere omenaala na-ekpọkọta ọnụ ndị nwere ụdị echiche ndị nwere mmetụta na ụkpụrụ keobodo ha leghaara ha anya ma nye ha ohere ịzụlite echiche nke njirimara.
translations.reference: Subcultures bring together like-minded individuals who feel neglected by societal standards and allow them to develop a sense of identity.
translations.hypothesis: Small communities often bring together individuals with similar perspectives, allowing them to develop a strong sense of identity and shared values.

translations.source: Enwere ike imata ngalaba omenala site na afo, agburu, klaasi, ebe onye bi, ma o bu etu chukwu si kee mmadu -i bu nwoke ka ibu nwanyi.
translations.reference: Subcultures can be distinctive because of the age, ethnicity, class, location, and/or gender of the members.
translations.hypothesis: Cultural differences can be observed through traditions, customs, social norms, living environments, and, fundamentally, through the way people—both men and women—live their lives.

translations.source: Ihe nlereanya aji ama na omenala pụrụ iche bụ asụsụ, ịchọ mma, okpukpe, ọchịchị, mmekọahụ, ọnọdụ ebe, maọbu njikọ ọtụtụ ihe.
translations.reference: The qualities that determine a subculture as distinct may be linguistic, aesthetic, religious, political, sexual, geographical, or a combination of factors.
translations.hypothesis: This cultural artifact, which is a unique tradition, encompasses language, art, religion, governance, social relationships, geographical location, and often a combination of these elements.

translations.source: Ndịòtù nke otu okpuru omenala na-akpọtụrụkarị ịdị n'òtù ha site n'otu ojiji akanka pụrụ iche ma dịmara, nke gụnyere ụmụ ejiji, omume, na asụsụ ịgba izu.
translations.reference: Members of a subculture often signal their membership through a distinctive and symbolic use of style, which includes fashions, mannerisms, and argot.
translations.hypothesis: Members of a traditional cultural group often demonstrate their unity through a unique and distinctive style, which includes clothing, behavior, and specific greetings.

translations.source: Otu n’ime ukpuru akacha mara nke atuzi-aka banyere uru di mmekorita bu iweta n’uche ihe nwute banyere umu-aka ndi elefuuru-anya, na-nwuta, maobu mmeto akpachaara-anya mee, enweghi mmekorita ha ndi toro-eto mgbe ha ka na-eto eto.
translations.reference: One of the most common methods used to illustrate the importance of socialization is to draw upon the few unfortunate cases of children who were, through neglect, misfortune, or wilful abuse, not socialized by adults while they were growing up.
translations.hypothesis: One of the most significant misconceptions about the benefits of collaboration is the idea that it primarily benefits highly skilled, experienced, and innovative individuals, while those who are less experienced or less talented may not gain as much from the collaborative process, especially when they are still developing their skills.

translations.source: Ụdị ụmụaka a ka a na akpọ ndị azụghị azụ. Ọtụtụ ụmụaka an na azụghị azụ abụrụla ndị ndị mmadụ jituru ejitu (ọ na abụkarị ndị mụrụ ha); oge ụfọdụ ngharịpụ ụmụaka bụ maka ọjụjụ ntụpọ dị na ahụ nwatakịrị ahụ a na ahụ anya maọbụ ntụpọ dị n' akọ n'uche ya.
translations.reference: Such children are called "feral" or wild. Some feral children have been confined by people (usually their own parents); in some cases this child abandonment was due to the parents' rejection of a child's severe intellectual or physical impairment.
translations.hypothesis: These children are often referred to as "orphans." Many orphans have lost one or both parents (often due to death); sometimes, the separation of children occurs due to physical or mental disabilities that the child or their caregivers are unable to manage.

translations.source: Ụmụaka azụghịazụ nwere ike ha e nweela ahụmihe nke mmetọ ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ahụmihe mkpasasị uche nke ukwuu tupu agbahapụ ha ma ọ bụ ha na-agbalaga.
translations.reference: Feral children may have experienced severe child abuse or trauma before being abandoned or running away.
translations.hypothesis: Children who are adopted may have experienced abuse or significant emotional trauma before being placed with their adoptive families, or they may be struggling with the challenges of adjusting to a new environment.

translations.source: Ndị ọzọ bụ ebubo ka eboro n’ọbụ ụmụ anụmanụ kpọpụtara ha; a sịkwara n’ụfọdụ biri n’ime ọhịa na onwe ha.
translations.reference: Others are alleged to have been brought up by animals; some are said to have lived in the wild on their own.
translations.hypothesis: Some were raised by experienced keepers, while others lived in the wild, on their own.

translations.source: Mgbe anumanu na-abughi-mmadu zulitechara ya kpam-kpam, nwa-ohia ahu egosi akparama-agwa (na njedebe ebe ana ahu anya) ihe dika nani nke anumanu-nlekota ya, dika ujo ya nye maobu enweghi ujo nye umu mmadu.
translations.reference: When completely brought up by non-human animals, the feral child exhibits behaviors (within physical limits) almost entirely like those of the particular care-animal, such as its fear of or indifference to humans.
translations.hypothesis: When the artificial intelligence system was completely overwhelmed, the robot displayed a message (on its screen) that was essentially a reflection of its programming, stating its loyalty to its creators and its lack of loyalty to humans.

translations.source: Dịka ọmụmụ dabere n’arụmarụ kwesịrị ime ka ọmụmụ kara dị mfe ma na-adọkwu mmasị, ịkụ skafoldu gakwuru otu ụzọụkwụ n’ihu.
translations.reference: While project based learning should make learning easier and more interesting, scaffolding goes a step beyond.
translations.hypothesis: As a demonstration of how scaffolding can make construction easier and more appealing, the scaffolding was moved one step forward.

translations.source: Skafoldin abụghị usoro mmụta kama ọ bụ enyemaka na-akwado ndị na-amụ ihe ọhụrụ dịka iji program ọhụrụ arụ ọrụ na kọmputa maọbụ ibido ọrụ ọhụrụ
translations.reference: Scaffolding is not a method of learning but rather an aid that provides support to individuals whom are undergoing a new learning experience such as using a new computer program or beginning a new project.
translations.hypothesis: Scaffolding is not a teaching method in itself, but rather a supportive tool that helps learners acquire new skills, such as learning how to use a new software program on a computer or starting a new job.

translations.source: Ụmụ arụrụmarụ osisi nwere ike ịbụ ma kendịnuche ma ịdịrị ire, n'ụzọ ọzọ, onye nkuzi bụ ụdị arụrụmarụ osisi mana ọ dịkwa dị ka nwoke ntakịrị mkpado akwụkwọ n'ime Microsoft Office.
translations.reference: Scaffolds can be both virtual and real, in other words, a teacher is a form of scaffold but so is the little paperclip man in Microsoft Office.
translations.hypothesis: Wooden furniture can be both elegant and practical, while a teacher is a type of wooden furniture, but also resembles a small, helpful assistant within the Microsoft Office suite.

translations.source: A rụnyechara Ihe nkwado n'ime ngwanro a, ndị ga-ajụ ajụjụ, nye ozi, ma kọwaa usoro ndị gaara ara nwa akwụkwọ ahụ ịghọta n'onwe ya.
translations.reference: Virtual Scaffolds are internalized in the software and are meant to question, prompt, and explain procedures that may have been to challenging for the student to handle alone.
translations.hypothesis: Within this framework, there will be opportunities for questions, information sharing, and explanations to help the student understand the process.

translations.source: Enwere ọtụtụ ihe e ji akpọga ụmụ aka ka onye ọzọ lekọta ha, dịka nleghara anya, mmegbu, nakwa nnapụ ihe.
translations.reference: Children are placed in Foster Care for a wide variety of reasons that range from neglect, to abuse, and even to extortion.
translations.hypothesis: There are many reasons why someone might be accused of child abuse, including neglect, physical harm, or emotional abuse.

translations.source: Ọ dị mma ka nwatakịrị tolite na gburugburu ebe a na-adịghị elekọta, elekọta, na agụmakwụkwọ, mana ha na-eme ya.
translations.reference: No child should ever have to grow up in an environment that is not nurturing, caring, and educational, but they do.
translations.hypothesis: It's unfortunate that some children grow up in environments lacking care, support, and education, but they still manage to thrive.

translations.source: Anyị na-ahụta Ụkpụrụ Nlekọta anya ahụ ka ebe n’enweghi ihe iyi ndụ egwu nye ụmụaka ndị a.
translations.reference: We perceive the Foster Care System to be a safety zone for these children.
translations.hypothesis: We are seeing the principles of child protection being applied to ensure the safety and well-being of these children.

translations.source: Ụlọ nchekwa ụmụaka anyị kwesịrị inye ụlọ nwere nchekwa, ndị nledo anya nwere ịhụnanya, nkụzi akwụkwọ dị mma, na nlekọta ahụike dị ntụkwasịobi.
translations.reference: Our foster care system is supposed to provide safe homes, loving caregivers, stable education, and reliable health care.
translations.hypothesis: Our childcare facilities should provide safe environments, caring staff, engaging learning materials, and reliable healthcare services.

translations.source: Ulo nlekọta anya ndi akpotara-akpota kwesiri inyecha ihe nile di mkpa nke na adighi n’ulo ochie esi na kpota ha.
translations.reference: Foster care is supposed to provide all the necessities that were lacking in the home they were previously taken from.
translations.hypothesis: Modern eye care centers should provide all the necessary equipment and resources that were previously unavailable in traditional settings.

translations.source: Ịntanetị na-ejikọ akụkụ nke nkwukọrịta ọha na nkwukọrịta nke mmadụ abụọ.
translations.reference: The Internet combines elements of both mass and interpersonal communication.
translations.hypothesis: The internet connects different aspects of social interaction and human communication.

translations.source: Njirimara pụrụ iche nke Ịntaneetị na-eduga akụkụ agbakwụnyere n’usoro nke ojiji ya na usoro afọ ojuju.
translations.reference: The distinct characteristics of the Internet lead to additional dimensions in terms of the uses and gratifications approach.
translations.hypothesis: The unique features of the internet contribute to its widespread use and its continued relevance over time.

translations.source: Maka ọmụmaatụ, “mmụta” na “mkpakọrịta” bụ ndị atụnyere dịka mkpalite dị mkpa maka ojiji Ịntanetị (James na ndị ọzọ., 1995).
translations.reference: For example, “learning” and “socialization” are suggested as important motivations for Internet use (James et al., 1995).
translations.hypothesis: For example, "education" and "communication" are cited as essential prerequisites for effective internet usage (James et al., 1995).

translations.source: Eighmey na McCord(1998) chọpụtara na “nsonye” na “mmekọrịta ga-adịgịde” sokwa na ihe mkpali ọhụrụ mgbe ha nyochara mmeghachi omume ndị na-abịa n'ọtụtụ webụsaịtị.
translations.reference: “Personal involvement” and “continuing relationships” were also identified as new motivation aspects by Eighmey and McCord (1998) when they investigated audience reactions to websites.
translations.hypothesis: Eighmey and McCord (1998) found that "engagement" and "continued interaction" were likely to occur following positive experiences on various websites.

translations.source: Ojiji nke ndekọ vidio edugawo na ụmụ nchọpụta dị mkpa n’ime nkọwa nke nzipụta-n’ihu-kentakịrị, mmegharị ihu nke na-anọru milisekọnd ole na ole.
translations.reference: The use of video recording has led to important discoveries in the interpretation of micro-expressions, facial movements which last a few milliseconds.
translations.hypothesis: Video recordings are crucial for researchers in the analysis of micro-expressions, which are fleeting facial movements that occur in milliseconds.

translations.source: Akachasị ekwu na mmadụ nwere ike ịma mmgbe mmadụ na atụ asi ma ọbụrụ na onwere ike ịkọwapụta obere mmegharị ahụ dị iche iche ọfụma.
translations.reference: In particular, it is claimed that one can detect whether a person is lying by interpreting micro-expressions correctly.
translations.hypothesis: It is often said that people can tell when they are being lied to if they can identify subtle changes in behavior.

translations.source: Oliver Saks, n'akwụkwọ ya Okwu Onyeisi Obodo, gosiri ka ndị enweghị ike ịghọta ọnụ okwu n'ihi isi mmebi nwere ike ikwu mgbe mmadụ na-ekwu eziokwu.
translations.reference: Oliver Sacks, in his paper The President's Speech, indicated how people who are unable to understand speech because of brain damage are nevertheless able to assess sincerity accurately.
translations.hypothesis: In his book, "The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat," Oliver Sacks describes how individuals with brain damage affecting language comprehension can sometimes speak truthfully.

translations.source: Ọ na-ekwu rịị na ikekwe ụmụ anụmanụ dịka nkịta ụlọ nwekwara ụdịrị ikikere a ịghọta omume mmadụ
translations.reference: He even suggests that such abilities in interpreting human behavior may be shared by animals such as domestic dogs.
translations.hypothesis: It is said that even animals, such as domestic dogs, may possess a certain capacity to understand human behavior.

translations.source: Nnyocha na narị afọ nke iri abụọ egosipụtala na enwere ụdịrị genetik variyeshọn abụọ: nke zoro ezo na nke pụtara apụta.
translations.reference: Twentieth century research has shown that there are two pools of genetic variation: hidden and expressed.
translations.hypothesis: Studies conducted over the past twenty years have shown that there are two main types of genetic variation: recessive and dominant.

translations.source: Mgbanwe n'ọdịdị na-agbakwunye ọdịdị kejenetiki ọhụrụ, ma nhọpụta na-ewepụ ya n'ogwu ọdịdị nke a kọwapụtara.
translations.reference: Mutation adds new genetic variation, and selection removes it from the pool of expressed variation.
translations.hypothesis: Mutations introduce new genetic variations, while selection eliminates them from the existing population.

translations.source: Nkewa na ntughari nkpokorita nkeghari na azu n'etiti ọdọ mmiri abua ahu na ọgbọ o bula.
translations.reference: Segregation and recombination shuffle variation back and forth between the two pools with each generation.
translations.hypothesis: The allocation and distribution of resources are constantly shifting between the two groups and generations.

translations.source: N'ime savanna, ọ bụ ihe siri ike na primate nwere usoro nri dị ka nke mmadụ iji mejupụta amino-acid chọrọ site na ihe ọkụkụ dịnụ.
translations.reference: Out on the savanna, it is hard for a primate with a digestive system like that of humans to satisfy its amino-acid requirements from available plant resources.
translations.hypothesis: Within the savanna environment, it is challenging for primates to obtain a diet that provides all the necessary amino acids required for their bodily functions, given the available food sources.

translations.source: Ọzọ dịka ibe ya, ị jụ ime ihe a nwere nnukwu ntaramahụhụ: nnukwu ndamụmbà, ọtịtaahụ, nakwa ọnwụ n'ikpeazụ.
translations.reference: Moreover, failure to do so has serious consequences: growth depression, malnutrition, and ultimately death.
translations.hypothesis: Like its counterpart, this condition can have serious consequences: severe pain, disability, and even death in extreme cases.

translations.source: Ihe akụrụngwa a na-enweta ngwa ngwa ga-abụrịrị protein ndị dị na akwụkwọ na legume gasị, mana ihe ndị a siri ike maka ndị nyiri mmadụ ndịọzọ bị n’ọhịa dịka anyị iji gbazèe ma anyị sie ya n’ọkụ.
translations.reference: The most readily accessible plant resources would have been the proteins accessible in leaves and legumes, but these are hard for primates like us to digest unless they are cooked.
translations.hypothesis: This readily available ingredient should be a source of protein from grains and legumes, but these items are often difficult for those of us who live in rural areas to access and afford.

translations.source: N’aka ọzọ, nri anụmanụ arụrụ, ntanta, akwa) abughi naani di nfe, kama ha na-enye oke protein nke nwere amino acid nile di nma.
translations.reference: In contrast, animal foods (ants, termites, eggs) not only are easily digestible, but they provide high-quantity proteins that contain all the essential amino acids.
translations.hypothesis: On the other hand, animal products (meat, fish, eggs) are not necessarily bad; rather, they provide a high amount of protein, which contains all the essential amino acids.

translations.source: Eleghị anya, ya atụla anyị n'anya ma ọbụrụ na ndị nna nna anyi ji aka ha gboo "mkpa protin" ha n'usoro dị ka nke enwe bi n'ọhịa si eme taa.
translations.reference: All things considered, we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.
translations.hypothesis: It's easy to take things for granted, and we might overlook the importance of protein if our ancestors had to struggle to obtain it, just like animals do in the wild today.

translations.source: Nkwụsịtụ ụra bụ usoro nke ịkpacharanya eteta ụra mgbe oge ị na-ehikarị ụra ma na-ada n’ụra mgbe obere oge gachara (nkeji 10–60).
translations.reference: Sleep interruption is the process of purposefully awakening during your normal sleep period and falling asleep a short time later (10–60 minutes).
translations.hypothesis: Sleep apnea is a condition in which breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep, usually for brief periods (10–60 seconds).

translations.source: Enwere ike ime ka n’uzo mfe site na iweta atanu ogbu-opi uzu ya dikariri nwayo ikpobata gi na uche kama ghara ikpotecha gi na-ozuzuoke.
translations.reference: This can be easily done by using a relatively quiet alarm clock to bring you to consciousness without fully waking you.
translations.hypothesis: It can be achieved more easily by introducing five key principles that will guide you, rather than overwhelming you with a complex system.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ị hụtara onwe gị na-ewubergharị elekere gị n’ime nrọ gị, e nwere ike idobe ya n’akụkụ nke ọzọ nke ime ụlọ ahụ, na-amanye gị isi n’akwa bilie ịgbanyụ ya.
translations.reference: If you find yourself resetting the clock in your sleep, it can be placed on the other side of the room, forcing you to get out of bed to turn it off.
translations.hypothesis: If you find yourself constantly adjusting your clock in your dreams, it might be a sign that something in your waking life is causing you stress or anxiety, prompting you to try and control or fix the situation.

translations.source: Ụzọ biorhythm ndị ọzọ gụnyere ịñụ oke ihe mmiri (karịsịa mmiri maọbụ tii, dayuretik a maara amaara) tupu arahụ ụra, na-amanye mmadụ ibili maka ịnyụ amịrị.
translations.reference: Other biorhythm-based options involve drinking lots of fluid (particularly water or tea, a known diuretic) prior to sleep, forcing one to get up to urinate.
translations.hypothesis: Other sleep-inducing methods include consuming large amounts of fluids (especially water or tea, which have diuretic properties) before bed, which can compel a person to wake up to urinate.

translations.source: Ọ bụ ole udo nke obi mmadụ nwere na-emekọrịta na nchịkọta ihu na ole obimgbalielu nọ n'ime ahụ na mmụọ nke mmadụ.
translations.reference: The amount of inner peace a person possesses correlates oppositely to the amount of tension in one’s body and spirit.
translations.hypothesis: The extent to which a person's inner peace is connected to their physical appearance and the overall well-being of their body and spirit.

translations.source: Ka a na-ewetulata esemokwu ahụ, ka ike ndụ nọ ugbu a na-adịkwuo mma. Mmadu niile nwere ike mmepụta ịchọta udo zuru oke na afọ ojuju.
translations.reference: The lower the tension, the more positive the life force present. Every person has the potential to find absolute peace and contentment.
translations.hypothesis: As we address this issue, the current state of life becomes more promising. Everyone has the potential to find complete peace and fulfillment.

translations.source: Mmadụ nile nwere ike ịma ihe. Sọ ohe nọchiri ụzọ bụ ekweghị ekwe nke anyi na ụjọ.
translations.reference: Everyone can achieve enlightenment. The only thing standing in the way of this goal is our own tension and negativity.
translations.hypothesis: Everyone is capable of learning. The path forward is uncertain, but we must face it with courage.

translations.source: Buddhism ndị Tibet dabere n’ụmụ nkuzi nke Buddha, mana adọtịkwuru ha site n’aka ụzọ nke ihụnanya mahayana ya na site n’aka ọtụtụ usoro si na Yoga Indịa.
translations.reference: The Tibetan Buddhism is based on the teachings of Buddha, but were extended by the mahayana path of love and by a lot of techniques from Indian Yoga.
translations.hypothesis: Tibetan Buddhism is based on the teachings of the Buddha, but it has also been influenced by the Mahayana tradition of compassion and by various practices derived from Indian Yoga.

translations.source: Na ntọala, Buddhism Tibet dị ezigbo mfe. Ọ mejupụtara Yoga Kundalini, ntụgharị uche na ụzọ nke ịhụnanya nnabata-ihe niile.
translations.reference: In principle the Tibetan Buddhism is very simple. It consists of Kundalini Yoga, meditation and the path of all-embracing love.
translations.hypothesis: Essentially, Tibetan Buddhism is quite simple. It combines Kundalini Yoga, mindfulness, and the path of loving-kindness and acceptance.

translations.source: N’iji Yoga Kundalini ike Kundalini (ike mmepe anya) bụ nke etetara site n’ụmụ postchọ yoga, mgbatị ahụ iku ume, ukwe ntụgharị uche na ihe ngosi.
translations.reference: With Kundalini Yoga the Kundalini energy (enlightenment energy) is awakened through yoga postures, breathing exercises, mantras and visualizations.
translations.hypothesis: In Yoga Kundalini, the power of Kundalini (the energy of enlightenment) is awakened through specific yoga postures, breathing techniques, mental exercises, and visualizations.

translations.source: Nke bụ isiokwu ntụgharị uche nke ndị Tibet bụ Deyiti Yoga. Site na ichepụta chi dị iche iche, a na ehichapụta ụkpụrụ ike, kpọghee chakra ma kepụta owuweanya nke amamihe.
translations.reference: The center of Tibetan meditation is the Deity Yoga. Through the visualization of various deities the energy channels are cleaned, the chakras are activated and the enlightenment consciousness is created.
translations.hypothesis: The central theme of Tibetan tantric practices is Deity Yoga. Through the visualization of various deities, practitioners cultivate energy, activate chakras, and generate insights.

translations.source: Jamini bụ ndị iro ọha n'Agha Ụwa nke abụọ, nke mere mba USA na USSR ji nwee mmekọ. Ka agha gwụrụ, esemokwu usoro omume, na omenala mere mba ndị ahụ ji nwee okwu.
translations.reference: Germany was a common enemy in World War 2, leading to cooperation between the USSR and USA. With the end of the war the clashes of system, process and culture led to the countries falling out.
translations.hypothesis: Jamini were a strong stance against public opinion during World War II, which is why the United States and the USSR were able to cooperate. After the war, disagreements over ideology and culture led to a rift between those two countries.

translations.source: N'etiti afọ abụọ nke nlụcha nke agha ahụ, ndị mba bụbu ndị mmekọrịta bụzi ndị iro ugbu a ma Agha Oyi ahụ bidokwara.
translations.reference: With two years of the end of the war, the former allies were now enemies and the Cold War began.
translations.hypothesis: During the two years of the conflict, former allies and current adversaries alike were drawn into the Cold War.

translations.source: O kwesịrị ịnọru ruo afọ iri anọ na-abịa abịa ma a ga-alụkwa ya n'ezie, site n'aka ụsụụ ndị agha nnọchite, n'ama agha site n'Afrịka ruo Eshia, n'ime Afghanistan, Kiuba na ọtụtụ ebe ndị ọzọ.
translations.reference: It was to last for the next 40 years and would be fought for real, by proxy armies, on battlefields from Africa to Asia, in Afghanistan, Cuba and many other places.
translations.hypothesis: It should last for forty years, and it will truly be a war, fought by soldiers from all over the world, from Africa to Asia, including Afghanistan, Cuba, and many other places.

translations.source: Mgbe Septemba 17, 1939 ruru, a kutuola nchekwa ndị Poland; naanị olileanya ha nwere bụ ịlaghachi tụọ atụmatụ ọzọ n'akụkụ isi briij Romenia.
translations.reference: By September 17, 1939, the Polish defense was already broken, and the only hope was to retreat and reorganise along the Romanian bridgehead.
translations.hypothesis: On September 17, 1939, the Polish defenses were breached; their only hope was to regroup and plan another offensive near the Romanian border.

translations.source: Mana, o gbughi oge ka atụmatụ a niile laa n'efu, mgbe ihe karịrị ndị Sọviet Yunịọn Red Amị 800,000 banyere, kepụta ogige agha ndị Belarụs na Yukren, ka ha wakpochara akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ Poland na nnupu isi nye Nkwekọrịta Udo Riga, Nkwekọrịta Udo Sọviet Yunịọn na Poland, na ọtụtụ nkwekọrịta ndị ọzọ, ma nke dị n'etiti mba abụọ, na nke dị n'etiti ọtụtụ mba.
translations.reference: However, these plans were rendered obsolete nearly overnight, when over 800,000 soldiers from the Soviet's Union Red Army entered and created the Belarussian and Ukrainian fronts after invading the eastern regions of Poland in violation of the Riga Peace Treaty, the Soviet-Polish Non-Aggression Pact, and other international treaties, both bilateral and multilateral.
translations.hypothesis: However, these plans were quickly overtaken by events. When more than 800,000 Soviet troops entered, establishing a military presence in Belarus and Ukraine, they effectively cut off the eastern part of Poland and paved the way for the Riga Peace Treaty, the Soviet-Polish Treaty, and numerous other agreements, both bilateral and multilateral.

translations.source: Iji ụgbọ mmiri ebughari ngwa ahịa bụ ụzọ kachasị mma n'ezie iji buru ọtụtụ ndị na ọtụtụ ngwa gafee oke osimiri.
translations.reference: Using ships to transport goods is by far the most efficient way to move large amounts of people and goods across oceans.
translations.hypothesis: Using a cargo ship is undoubtedly the most efficient way to transport a large number of people and goods across the ocean.

translations.source: Ọrụ nke ndị agha nke mmiri abụrụla kemgbe ịgba mbọ hụ na mba gị jidesiri ike ikikere ibugharị ndị gị na ngwaahịa gị, ma n'otu mgbe ahụ, na-egbochi ikikere onye iro gị ibugharị ndị ya na ngwaahịa ya.
translations.reference: The job of navies has traditionally been to ensure that your country maintains the ability to move your people and goods, while at the same time, interfering with your enemy's ability to move his people and goods.
translations.hypothesis: The role of the military has long been to ensure the security of your nation, allowing you to freely trade with your allies and partners, while simultaneously preventing your adversaries from doing the same.

translations.source: Otu n’ime ọmụmatụ oge na-etebeghị anya nke a kacha tozuo oke bụbu kampeenụ Ugwu Atlantik nke WWII. Ndị Amerịka nọ na-anwa ibugharị ụmụ nwoke na ngwongwo gafee Oke osimiri Atlantik inyere Britenụ aka.
translations.reference: One of the most noteworthy recent examples of this was the North Atlantic campaign of WWII. The Americans were trying to move men and materials across the Atlantic Ocean to help Britain.
translations.hypothesis: One of the most iconic examples of this era was the Atlantic convoy system of World War II. The Americans were working to transport men and supplies across the Atlantic Ocean to aid Britain.

translations.source: N'otu mgbe ahụ, ndị agha nke mmiri nke Jamanị, n'iji naanị ụgbọokpurummiri, nọ na-agbalị ịkwụsị mkpọchi ụzọ a.
translations.reference: At the same time, the German navy, using mainly U-boats, was trying to stop this traffic.
translations.hypothesis: At one point, German naval forces, using only submarines, attempted to break this blockade.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ndị mba bụbu ndị mmekọrịta dara, Jamanị nwere ike eleghi anya merie Briten dị ka o mere Yurop ndị ọzọ fọdụrụ.
translations.reference: Had the Allies failed, Germany probably would have been able to conquer Britain as it had the rest of Europe.
translations.hypothesis: If the former allies had not been divided, Germany could have easily defeated Britain, just as it did with the other European countries.

translations.source: Ewu yiri ka e buru ụzọ mee ya anụụlọ n’ihe ruru puku afọ iri gara aga n'ugwu Zagros nke Iran.
translations.reference: Goats seem to have been first domesticated roughly 10,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains of Iran.
translations.hypothesis: The sheep appears to have been domesticated as far back as 10,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains of Iran.

translations.source: Omenala ndị mgbe ochie na agbụrụ bidoro iji dobe ha maka inweta ohere dị mfe na mmiri ara, ntutu isi, anụ, na anụahụ gasị.
translations.reference: Ancient cultures and tribes began to keep them for easy access to milk, hair, meat, and skins.
translations.hypothesis: Ancient traditions and customs were established to regulate access to resources like water, hair, meat, and other forms of sustenance.

translations.source: E dobere n'ozuzu ụmụ ehu ụlọ n'ime ìgwè ndị nke pagharịrị n'elu ugwu ma ọ bụ ebe ịta ahịhịa ndị ọzọ, nke ọtụtụ mgbe bụ ndị ọzụzụ ehu na-elekọta ha ndị nke na abụkarị ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ụmụ ntorọbịa, nke yiri onye ọzụzụ atụrụ a ka mara ama. A ka na-eji usoro ọzụzụ ehu ndị a ruo taa.
translations.reference: Domestic goats were generally kept in herds that wandered on hills or other grazing areas, often tended by goatherds who were frequently children or adolescents, similar to the more widely known shepherd. These methods of herding are still used today.
translations.hypothesis: Traditionally, cattle were herded by groups of young men who moved them to higher ground or grazing areas, often accompanied by experienced herders who were usually children or teenagers, much like a shepherd. These herding practices are still used today.

translations.source: E wuru ụzọ ụgbọ ibu gasị n’Ingland dị ka n'oge dị ka narị afọ nke iri na isii ahụ.
translations.reference: Wagonways were built in England as early as the 16th Century.
translations.hypothesis: The development of the trucking industry in England began around the 1960s.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị ụmụ ụzọwagọn nwere naanị ogwe osisi nọ n’akụkụ n’akụkụ, ha nyere ụmụ ịnyịnya na-esere ha òhèrè irute ekwomọsọ ndị karịrị ma sere ibu kara dị ukwuu karịa n’ụmụ ụzọ nke ụbọchị ahụ ndị karịtụrụ dị ike ike.
translations.reference: Although wagonways merely consisted of parallel planks of wood, they allowed horses pulling them to achieve greater speeds and pull larger loads than on the slightly more rough roads of the day.
translations.hypothesis: Despite having only a single row of trees on either side, the runners provided a clear path for the cyclists, allowing them to maintain a faster pace and cover a greater distance than the cyclists who had to navigate around the trees throughout the day.

translations.source: Ebidoro mgbe gboo were krọstaị na-arụ ụzọ ụgbọoloko ka o were gbasie ike. Obere obere a bịa mata na ụzọ ụgbọoloko ga-esikarị ike ma ọ bụrụ na o nweturu obere igwe n’elu ya.
translations.reference: Crossties were introduced fairly early to hold the tracks in place. Gradually, however, it was realised that tracks would be more efficient if they had a stip of iron on the top.
translations.hypothesis: The bridge collapsed while a truck was crossing it, causing significant damage. It has now become clear that the bridge was structurally weak and likely couldn't withstand the weight of a heavy vehicle, especially when combined with adverse weather conditions.

translations.source: Nke mechara bụrụ omume a na-emekarị, mana igwe ahụ kpatakwuru ndọwa n'ụkwụ ụmụ ụgbọ ibu ejiri osisi mee.
translations.reference: This became common practice, but the iron caused more wear on the wooden wheels of the wagons.
translations.hypothesis: Eventually, this became a common practice, but the trees were damaged by the trucks that used wooden wheels.

translations.source: N'ikpeazụ, eji wiil ígwè dochie wiil osisi. N'afọ 1767, e wepụtara wiil nke mbụ ejị igwe rụọ kpam kpam.
translations.reference: Eventually, wooden wheels were replaced by iron wheels. In 1767, the first full-iron rails were introduced.
translations.hypothesis: Finally, iron wheels replaced wooden wheels. In 1767, the first fully iron wheel was produced.

translations.source: Usoro njem e bu ụzọ mara ama bụ ịga ije, ụmụ mmadụ bidoro ịkwụ ọtọ aga ije afọ nde abụọ gara aga site na mpụta nke Homo Erektus (nke pụtara nwoke kwụ ọtọ).
translations.reference: The first known transportation was walking, humans began walking upright two million years ago with the emergence of Homo Erectus (meaning upright man).
translations.hypothesis: Walking is a fundamental form of transportation, and humans have been walking for millions of years, dating back to the emergence of Homo Erectus (which translates to "upright man").

translations.source: Ndị bụ ha ụzọ, Ọstralopitekus ahụ akwụghị ọtọ gaa ije dị ka n'akparamagwa.
translations.reference: Their predecessors, the Australopithecus did not walk upright as habitually.
translations.hypothesis: The Australopithecus, known for its bipedal gait, did not walk upright perfectly, but rather in a somewhat awkward manner.

translations.source: Achoputara ọkachamara bipedal na fosil Australopithecus site na nde nde afọ 4.2-3.9 gara aga, o bu ezie na Sahelanthropus nwere ike ije ije n'ukwu abuo na nde afọ asaa gara aga.
translations.reference: Bipedal specializations are found in Australopithecus fossils from 4.2-3.9 million years ago, although Sahelanthropus may have walked on two legs as early as seven million years ago.
translations.hypothesis: While experts have identified bipedalism (walking on two legs) in the fossil record of Australopithecus dating back 4.2 to 3.9 million years, it is possible that Sahelanthropus was also capable of bipedal locomotion as far back as 7 million years ago.

translations.source: Anyị nwere ike malite ibi n’enyi karịa na gburugburu ebe obibi, anyị nwere ike isonye ije nke gburugburu ebe obibi, ma anyị nwekwara ike ịbụ ndị ọchọ mgbanwe ka e nwee ike belata ntaramahụhụ ọdịnihu ruo ogo ụfọdụ.
translations.reference: We can start living more friendly to the environment, we can join to the environmental movement, and we can even be activists in order to reduce the future suffering in some degree.
translations.hypothesis: We can start living more sustainably and in harmony with our environment. We can participate in environmental initiatives, and we can also be agents of change to mitigate future harm to a certain extent.

translations.source: Nke a dị nnọọ ka ọgwụgwọ kemgbaàmà n’ọtụtụ okwu. Agbanyeghị, ọ bụrụ na anyị achọghị naanị ọsịsa nke nwa oge, ya mere anyị kwesịrị ịchọta isi ihe kpatara nsogbu ndị ahụ, ma anyị kwesịrị iwepụ̀ ike ha.
translations.reference: This is just like symptomatic treatment in many cases. However, if we do not only want a temporary solution, then we should find the root of the problems, and we should deactivate them.
translations.hypothesis: This is very much like a superficial treatment of the issue. However, if we don't just want a temporary fix, we need to identify the root causes of these problems and address them effectively.

translations.source: O doro anya nke ọma n'ụwa agbanweela nnukwu n'ihi ụmụ ọganihu nke sayensị na teknụzụ nke ụmụ mmadụ, ma ụmụ nsogbu adịla nnukwu karịa n'ihi ọnụọgụgụ mmadụ karịrị akarị na ibifụga ndụ ókè nke ụmụ mmadụ.
translations.reference: It is obvious enough that the world has changed much because of humankind's scientific and technological advancements, and problems have become greater because of overpopulation and mankind's extravagant lifestyle.
translations.hypothesis: It is clear that the world has undergone significant changes due to the advancements of science and technology made by humans, but these problems have become even greater due to the ever-increasing population and the widening gap in living standards among people.

translations.source: Mgbe Kọngres nyechara ya nkwekọrịta ha na Julaị 4, e weere ya n'akwụkwọ eji aka dee, nke Jọn Hankọk Onye isi Kọngres na Chals Tọmsin Onye odeakwụkwọ tinyere akara nkwado ha, wega ya n'ụlọ mbipụta Jọn Dunlap nke eteghi aka.
translations.reference: After its adoption by Congress on July 4, a handwritten draft signed by the President of Congress John Hancock and the Secretary Charles Thomson was then sent a few blocks away to the printing shop of John Dunlap.
translations.hypothesis: After the Congress reached an agreement on July 4th, the document was handwritten and signed by John Hancock, the President of the Congress, and Charles Thomson, the Secretary, before being sent to the printer, John Dunlap, for publication.

translations.source: N'ime abali n'etiti mbipụta otu narị na iri ise ya na narị abụọ ka e mere, nke a mara ugbu a dị ka “Dunlap broadsides”.
translations.reference: Through the night between 150 and 200 copies were made, now known as "Dunlap broadsides".
translations.hypothesis: During the century and a half between the publication of its first and second editions, these sheets, now known as "Dunlap broadsides," were produced.

translations.source: Oge mbụ a gụpụtara edemede a n'ọha bụ na Julaị 8, nke John Nixn gụrụ na mbaraezi Ụlọọgbakọ Ndipenda.
translations.reference: The first public reading of the document was by John Nixon in the yard of Independence Hall on July 8.
translations.hypothesis: The first public reading of this piece was on July 8th, delivered by John Nixn at the Independence Hall auditorium.

translations.source: Na Julaị 6, e zigaara George Washington otu kọpị, onye mere ka a gụọrọ ya ndị agha ya na Niu Yọk na Julaị 9. Otu kọpị ruru Lọndọn n'Ọgọstụ 10.
translations.reference: One was sent to George Washington on July 6, who had it read to his troops in New York on July 9. A copy reached London on August 10.
translations.hypothesis: On July 6th, George Washington received a shipment of coffee, which was then distributed to his troops in New York on July 9th. The coffee shipment arrived in London on August 10th.

translations.source: Dunlap brọdsaịd 25 ka nọ taa bụ kọpị edemede izizi ndị kachasị dị ochie. Nke izizi e ji aka dee anọzighi.
translations.reference: The 25 Dunlap broadsides still known to exist are the oldest surviving copies of the document. The original handwritten copy has not survived.
translations.hypothesis: The Dunlap broadside, dated 1704, is the earliest known printed copy of the poem. The original was handwritten.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ndị ọkàchamara ihe banyere fọsịl anụmanụ na osisi taa kwenyere na otu òtù daịnosọọ lanarịrị ma dị ndụ taa. Anyị na-akpọ ha ụmụ nnụnụ.
translations.reference: Many paleontologists today believe that one group of dinosaurs survived and is alive today. We call them birds.
translations.hypothesis: Many modern experts in the fields of paleontology and botany believe that a certain group of dinosaurs did not actually become extinct and still exist today. We call them birds.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ anaghị eche bayere ha dị ka daịnosọọ n'ihi na ha nwere nku ma nwee ike ife efe.
translations.reference: Many people don't think about them as dinosaurs because they have feathers and can fly.
translations.hypothesis: Many people don't consider them dinosaurs because they have feathers and can fly.

translations.source: Mana a ka nwere ọtụtụ ihe gbasara ụmụ nnụnụ ndị yiri nke daịnosọọ.
translations.reference: But there are a lot of things about birds that still look like a dinosaur.
translations.hypothesis: However, there are many things we still don't know about these dinosaur-like creatures.

translations.source: Ha nwere okpa ya na abuba na mbu aka, ha na eyi akwa, ha nakwa aga ije na ukwu oji ha abuo dika T-Rex.
translations.reference: They have feet with scales and claws, they lay eggs, and they walk on their two back legs like a T-Rex.
translations.hypothesis: They wear hats and gloves, and they often wear robes, and they walk on two legs, much like a T-Rex.

translations.source: Ihe dịka igwe kọmputa niile e ji arụ ọrụ taa bụ ihe sitere na mkpụrụokwu ndị a gwakọrọ agwakọ nke e tinyere dịka mkpụrụọnụọgụ.
translations.reference: Virtually all computers in use today are based on the manipulation of information which is coded in the form of binary numbers.
translations.hypothesis: Modern computers, like all the technology we use today, are built from a complex combination of components that function as a system.

translations.source: Otu akara ọnụọgụ abụọ nwere ike inwe naanị otu n’ime mbamuru abụọ, ya bụ 0 ma ọ bụ 1, ma a na-akpọ akara ndị a dị ka ọnụọgụ keọnụọgụ abụọ - ma ọ bụ bits, iji asụsụ mpụiche kọmputa.
translations.reference: A binary number can have only one of two values, i.e. 0 or 1, and these numbers are referred to as binary digits - or bits, to use computer jargon.
translations.hypothesis: A pair of binary digits can only have one of two possible values, either 0 or 1. These digits are called binary digits, or "bits," in computer science terminology.

translations.source: Ọrịa ịtụ nsị nke ime ahụ nwere ike ọ gaghị adị ire ozigbo. Ihe ngosipụta ya, dịka ọgbụgbọ, bụ ihe ndị na-emekwa n'ọtụtụ ọrịa ndị ọzọ. Ya mere na enweghi ike ịchọpụta ọrịa a ozigbo ozigbo.
translations.reference: Internal poisoning may not be immediately apparent. Symptoms, such as vomiting are sufficiently general that an immediate diagnosis cannot be made.
translations.hypothesis: Internal bleeding can be difficult to diagnose directly. Its symptoms, such as fatigue, are often similar to those of many other conditions. Therefore, it can be challenging to identify this specific ailment immediately.

translations.source: Ndosipụta kachasị mma maka inwe ńsí n’ime ahụ nwere ike ịbụ ọnụnọ nke mkpọ ogwụ ghe oghe ma ọ bụ kemikalụ ezinụlọ ndị na-egbu agbu.
translations.reference: The best indication of internal poisoning may be the presence of an open container of medication or toxic household chemicals.
translations.hypothesis: The best way to treat internal bleeding may involve the use of blood transfusions or certain medications that help to stop the bleeding.

translations.source: Lelee nnyeàhà ahụ maka ntụziaka mgbata ọsọ enyemaka mbụ akọwapụtara maka nsi ahụ akọwapụtara.
