translations.reference: Check the label for specific first aid instructions for that specific poison.
translations.hypothesis: Please refer to the attached instructions for the initial first aid treatment of the specified injury.

translations.source: okwu bụ ahụhụ bụ ndị ọka mmụta ahụhụ n’ụzọ nwere ugwu maka òtù ụmụ ahụhụ a.
translations.reference: The term bug is used by entomologists in a formal sense for this group of insects.
translations.hypothesis: The words are hurtful, and the scholars are being overly harsh towards these students.

translations.source: Okwu a sitere mmarita mgbe-ochie nke akpiri, bu chinchi di oke nko maka ibunye ndi mmadu oria.
translations.reference: This term derives from ancient familiarity with Bed-bugs, which are insects highly adapted to parasitize humans.
translations.hypothesis: This saying originates from ancient Igbo wisdom and emphasizes the importance of respecting and valuing elders.

translations.source: Ma Assassin-bọg na Bed-bọg dị nidikolous, ha zuru oke ibi na nest maọbụ n'ụlọ nke hostu ha.
translations.reference: Both Assassin-bugs and Bed-bugs are nidicolous, adapted to living in nest or housing of their host.
translations.hypothesis: Bed bugs, despite being annoying, are perfectly capable of living and reproducing in a nest or within the host's home.

translations.source: N'ofe mba Amerịka, e nwere ihe dị ka ọnụọgụ ọrịa Multiple Sclerosis (MS) 400,000 a maara amaara, nke na-eme ya isi ọrịa ụbụrụ na-emetụta ndị ntorọbịa na ndị okenye.
translations.reference: Across the United States of America, there are approximately 400,000 known cases of Multiple Sclerosis (MS), leaving it as the leading neurological disease in younger and middle aged adults.
translations.hypothesis: In the United States, there are approximately 400,000 known cases of Multiple Sclerosis (MS), a chronic disease that affects the brain and spinal cord, impacting young adults and adults.

translations.source: Mọltipụl Sklerosis bụ ọrịa na-emetụta sentral navọs sistem, nke gbakwunyere ụbụrụ, ogwurugwu azụ na ọptik nav.
translations.reference: MS is a disease that affects the central nervous system, which is made up of the brain, the spinal cord and the optic nerve.
translations.hypothesis: Multiple sclerosis is a disease that affects the central nervous system, including the brain, spinal cord, and optic nerves.

translations.source: Nnyocha achọpụtala na ụmụ nwanyị bụ ihe yikarịrị ugboro abụọ inwe MS karịa ụmụ nwoke.
translations.reference: Research has found that females are two times more likely to have MS then males.
translations.hypothesis: Studies have shown that women are approximately twice as likely to have multiple sclerosis (MS) as men.

translations.source: Di na nwunye nwere ike ikwekọrịta na ọ gaghị abara ha maọbụ nwa ha uru ịzụpụta nwa.
translations.reference: A couple may decide it is not in their best interest, or in the interest of their child, to raise a baby.
translations.hypothesis: Couples may disagree on whether or not having a child would be beneficial for them or their child.

translations.source: Di na nwunye ndị a nwere ike ịhọrọ ime atụmatụ mkpọta nwa maka nwa ha.
translations.reference: These couples may choose to make an adoption plan for their baby.
translations.hypothesis: These couples may be considering fertility treatments for their child.

translations.source: N’ime otu mkpọRọ nwa, nne na nna mụrụ nwa ahụ ga-akwụsị ikikere ha dị ka nne na nna ka di na nwunye ọ bụla nwere ike izulite nwa ahụ.
translations.reference: In an adoption, the birth parents terminate their parental rights so that another couple may parent the child.
translations.hypothesis: In the event of a child custody dispute, the parents of the child will relinquish their parental rights so that either parent can be granted custody of the child.

translations.source: Isi ọrụ sayensị bụ ịchọpụta otu ụwa si arụ ọrụ site na usoro kesayensị. Usoro n'ezie na-edu ọtụtụ n'ime nnyocha kesayensị.
translations.reference: Science’s main goal is to figure out the way the world works through the scientific method. This method in fact guides most scientific research.
translations.hypothesis: The primary function of science is to understand how the world works through the scientific method. This method actually guides many scientific investigations.

translations.source: Ọ nọghị naanị ya n'ezie, eksperimenteshọn, ma otu eksperimenti bụ otu ule nke eji ewepụ otu haịpotesis kwere omume ma ọ bụ karịa, ịjụ ajụjụ gasị, na ime nyochata nakwa eduzi nnyocha sayensị.
translations.reference: It isn’t alone though, experimentation, and an experiment is a test that is used to eliminate one or more of the possible hypotheses, asking questions, and making observations also guide scientific research.
translations.hypothesis: It is not just about experimentation; rather, an experiment is a process used to test one or more hypotheses, ask questions, and conduct scientific investigations, ultimately leading to the generation of scientific knowledge.

translations.source: Ndị ọkammụta n'ụmụ ihe ekere na ndị ọkachamara gbadoro ụkwụ n'ederede oge gboo, ọkachasị, n'akwụkwọ nsọ e dere na Latin.
translations.reference: Naturalists and philosophers focused on classical texts and, in particular, on the Bible in Latin.
translations.hypothesis: Scholars and experts have focused their attention on ancient texts, particularly religious texts written in Latin.

translations.source: A nabatara echiche Aristotle gbasara okwu sayensi niile ma mmuta akparamagwa ya bu psychology
translations.reference: Accepted were Aristotle's views on all matters of science, including psychology.
translations.hypothesis: I embrace Aristotle's view on all areas of science, but my area of expertise is experimental learning, specifically psychology.

translations.source: Dika amamihe nke ndi Greek biara gbatuwa, ndi odida anyanwu huta onwe ha ka ha na egbubiri site mgbara-ogwu ndi Greek ha nke ihe-omuma na nka.
translations.reference: As knowledge of Greek declined, the West found itself cut off from its Greek philosophical and scientific roots.
translations.hypothesis: As the wisdom of the ancient Greeks spread, artists were inspired by the Greek ideals of knowledge and art.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ usoro a na-ahụ na fisiọlọji na omume na-adabere ọtụtụ mgbe n'usoro ime ahụ na mmepụta ha site n'elekere nke ime ahụ.
translations.reference: Many observed rhythms in physiology and behavior often crucially depend on the presence of endogenous cycles and their production through biological clocks.
translations.hypothesis: Many physiological and behavioral processes are heavily influenced by the body's internal clock and its regulation of various functions.

translations.source: Usoro kwa-oge kwa-oge, nke n'abụghị nzaghachi nye ntụpenye kwa-oge keezi, ka edeturula maka ọtụtụ ihe ndị dị ndụ , nke gụnyere nje bakterịa, fọngaị, akụmakụ na ụmụanụmanụ.
translations.reference: Periodic rhythms, which are not simply responses to external periodic cues, have been documented for most living beings, including bacteria, fungi, plants, and animals.
translations.hypothesis: Seasonal or periodic treatments, which are not intended as a cure for ongoing infections, are often used for various living organisms, including bacteria, fungi, parasites, and animals.

translations.source: Elekere ime ahụ nwere usoro eje alọ nke na-arụ ọrụ n'onwe ya; usoro a ga na-aga n'ihu ma asịgodị rịị na onweghi ihe ọzọ metụtara ya.
translations.reference: Biological clocks are self sustaining oscillators which will continue a period of free-running cycling even in the absence of external cues.
translations.hypothesis: The internal workings of the system have a self-contained process; this process continues independently and without any external influence.

translations.source: Nwale Hershey na Chase so na otu aro no na isi siri na DNA wubu otu mkpụrụ ndụ ihe nketa.
translations.reference: The Hershey and Chase experiment was one of the leading suggestions that DNA was a genetic material.
translations.hypothesis: Nwale Hershey and Chase used a clever experiment to demonstrate that DNA, not protein, is the genetic material of a cell.

translations.source: Hershey na Chase jiri ụmụ feeji, ma ọ bụ ụmụ nje, iji kụnye DNA nke ha n'ime otu nje bakterịọm.
translations.reference: Hershey and Chase used phages, or viruses, to implant their own DNA into a bacterium.
translations.hypothesis: Hershey and Chase used bacteriophages, or viruses that infect bacteria, to introduce their DNA into a bacterial cell.

translations.source: Ha mere nnwale abụọ ebe ha ji rediyoaktiv fosforọs kaa akara na DNA nọ na fej maọbụ jiri rediyoaktiv sọlfọ kaa akara na protin nọ na fej.
translations.reference: They did two experiments marking either the DNA in the phage with a radioactive phosphorus or the protein of the phage with radioactive sulfur.
translations.hypothesis: They performed two tests: one where they labeled the DNA in the cells with radioactive phosphorus, or another where they labeled the proteins in the cells with radioactive sulfur.

translations.source: Mgbanwe ọjọọ nwere ike inwe ọtụtụ mmetụta dị iche iche na ndabere na ụdị mgbanwe ọjọọ ọ bụ, abamuru nke otu iberibe nke ihe mkpụrụ ndụ ihe nketa o metụtara na ma ọ bụrụ na ụmụ mkpụrụ ndụ o metụtara bụ ụmụ mkpụrụ ndụ geem-laịnụ.
translations.reference: Mutations can have a variety of different effects depending on the type of mutation, the significance of the piece of genetic material affected and whether the cells affected are germ-line cells.
translations.hypothesis: Mutations can have a variety of effects, depending on the type of mutation, the specific gene it affects, and whether the affected gene is involved in essential cellular processes or if the affected cells are germline cells.

translations.source: Ọ bụ nanị mgbanwe na mkpụrụ ndụ jem-laịn ka a ga-enyefe ụmụaka, ebe mgbanwe n’ebe ndị ọzọ nwere ike ibute ọnwụ nke mkpụrụ ndụ maọbụ ọrịa kansa.
translations.reference: Only mutations in germ-line cells can be passed on to children, while mutations elsewhere can cause cell-death or cancer.
translations.hypothesis: Only mutations in germline cells are passed on to offspring, while mutations in other tissues can lead to cell death or cancer.

translations.source: Njem-nlere anya nke dabere na udidi na enweta uche ndi mmadu ndi nwere mmasi izute ebe di na udidi ha maka ihi ikpori-ndu na udi ebe, gunyekwara akumaku anumanu anu-ohia.
translations.reference: Nature-based tourism attracts people interested in visiting natural areas for the purpose of enjoying the scenery, including plant and animal wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: The journey, which relies on a network of roads and the goodwill of people who are willing to provide shelter and food along the way, also includes elements of risk and uncertainty.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ ihe omume enwere ike ime ma anọrọ ya gụnyere ịchụ nta, ịkụ azụ, ise foto, ilele nnụnụ, na ịga n'ogige gụọ maka ihe ndị dị ndụ na gburugburu ha.
translations.reference: Examples of on-site activities include hunting, fishing, photography, bird watching, and visiting parks and studying information about the ecosystem.
translations.hypothesis: Certain activities can be enjoyed regardless of the weather, including hiking, fishing, taking photographs, birdwatching, and visiting a zoo to learn about animals and their environment.

translations.source: Otu ọmụmaatụ bụ ileta, ise fòto, na ịmụta gbasara na ụmụ ọrangụtanụ nọ n'ime Bọnioo.
translations.reference: An example is visiting, photographing, and learning about organgatuangs in Borneo.
translations.hypothesis: One example is to visit, take photos, and learn about the chimpanzees living in Bonobo.

translations.source: Ututu o bula, ndi mmadu n'ahapu obere obodo n'ugbo ala were gawa ulo oru ha ma ndi ozo n'agbafe ha ndi ulo oru ha di n'ebe ha si puta.
translations.reference: Every morning, people leave small country towns in cars to go their workplace and are passed by others whose work destination is the place they have just left.
translations.hypothesis: The sun was setting, and the people of the small village were returning from their farms, while others gathered near the entrance to the town.

translations.source: N'ime ụgbọ mgbagharị kenjem a na-agbanwegharị agbanwe onye ọ bụla si n'otuọdịla metụta ya, ma na-akwado, otu sistemụ njem dabere na ụgbọala nkeonwe.
translations.reference: In this dynamic transport shuttle everyone is somehow connected with, and supporting, a transport system based on private cars.
translations.hypothesis: Within this evolving transportation system, individuals are increasingly influenced by, and advocating for, a travel model based on personal vehicles.

translations.source: Sayensị na-egosi ugbu a na ekọnọmi a ji oke kabọn arụ ọrụ akupụla mkpokọta ihe ndụ niile nọ n'ụwa site n'otu n'ime ọnọdụ nkwụsi ike ya nke kwadogoro obibi ndụ mmadụ n'afọ nde abụọ gara aga.
translations.reference: Science now indicates that this massive carbon economy has dislodged the biosphere from one of its stable states that has supported human evolution for the past two million years.
translations.hypothesis: Current scientific research indicates that the global economy, through one of its stabilizing mechanisms, has significantly reduced the overall biodiversity on Earth, leading to a decline in human well-being over the past two centuries.

translations.source: Onye ọ bụla na-esonye n'ime ọha mmadụ ma na-eji ụmụ sistemụ njem. Ọ fọrọ obere ka ọ bụrụ onye niile na eme mkpesa gbasara ụmụ sistemụ njem.
translations.reference: Everyone participates in society and uses transportation systems. Almost everyone complains about transportation systems.
translations.hypothesis: Everyone participates in society and uses transportation systems. It's almost everyone who complains about transportation systems.

translations.source: N'ime ụmụ mba mepere emepe ọ ga-ara ahụ tupu ị nụ larịị mkpesa ndị yirinụ gbasara ogo mmiri ma ọ bụ ụmụ akwa mmiri na-ada n'ala.
translations.reference: In developed countries you seldom hear similar levels of complaints about water quality or bridges falling down.
translations.hypothesis: Before you hear any complaints, you might notice open containers or puddles of water on the floor.

translations.source: Gịnị mere sistemụ njem ji akpata ụdịrị ụmụ mkpesa ahụ, gịmị mere ha ji ada kwa ụbọchị? Ọ bụ na ndị injinịa njem amaghị arụ ọrụ ha nke ọma? Ma ọ bụ ihe ọzọ si n'isi na-eme?
translations.reference: Why do transportation systems engender such complaints, why do they fail on a daily basis? Are transportation engineers just incompetent? Or is something more fundamental going on?
translations.hypothesis: What caused the transportation system to generate so many complaints, and why are people experiencing these issues every day? Is it that the transportation engineers didn't properly design the system? Or is there something else at play?

translations.source: Ọwụwụ trafik bụ ọmụmụ nke ngagharị nke onye ọkwụ ụgbọ ọ bụla na ụgbọ ha n'etiti akara abụọ na mmekọrịta ha na-eme n'etiti onwe ha.
translations.reference: Traffic Flow is the study of the movement of individual drivers and vehicles between two points and the interactions they make with one another.
translations.hypothesis: Traffic flow refers to the movement of vehicles and the interactions they have with each other within a defined area.

translations.source: Na mwute, ịmụ maka otu okporo njem si aga siri maka na e nweghi ike ikwu kpọm n'ọgụ otu narị pasentị ụdị omume ọkwọ ụgbọ nwere ike ime.
translations.reference: Unfortunately, studying traffic flow is difficult because driver behavior cannot be predicted with one-hundred percent certainty.
translations.hypothesis: Unfortunately, it is impossible to definitively say how many accidents are caused by driver error, as it is not always possible to determine the exact percentage of accidents attributable to specific behaviors.

translations.source: Ọ dabara nke ọma na ndị na-anya ụgbọ ala nwere usoro omume na-adịgide; ya mere, ụzọ njem moto anaghị agbanwecha agbanwe ma bụrụkwa ihe enwere ike iji eserese aritmetik gosipụta.
translations.reference: Fortunately, drivers tend to behave within a reasonably consistent range; thus, traffic streams tend to have some reasonable consistency and can be roughly represented mathematically.
translations.hypothesis: It so happens that drivers behave in a predictable manner; therefore, the trajectory of a vehicle can be represented and understood using mathematical models.

translations.source: Iji ka mma na-anọchi anya ije nke okporo ụzọ, E mebewo mmekọrịta n'etiti isi njirimara atọ ahụ: (1) eruba, (2) njupụta, na (3) ike ọsọ.
translations.reference: To better represent traffic flow, relationships have been established between the three main characteristics: (1) flow, (2) density, and (3) velocity.
translations.hypothesis: To accurately represent the performance of a road, it is essential to consider the relationship between three key factors: (1) roughness, (2) smoothness, and (3) speed capacity.

translations.source: Mmetụta ndị a na-enyere aka n’ime atụmatụ, ncheremee, na arụmọrụ nke akụrụngwa okporo ụzọ ụgbọ ígwè.
translations.reference: These relationships help in planning, design, and operations of roadway facilities.
translations.hypothesis: These factors contribute to the design, safety, and performance of aircraft landing gear.

translations.source: Ụmụ ahụhụ bụ ụmụ anụmanụ buru ụzọ fee n'elu. Ike ha n'ife efe nyere ha aka ịgbanaha ndị iro n'ụzọ kara dị mfe ma ịchọtakwa nri na ndị otu mmekọ n'ụzọ dị werewere.
translations.reference: Insects were the first animals to take to the air. Their ability to fly helped them evade enemies more easily and find food and mates more efficiently.
translations.hypothesis: Birds are fascinating creatures that are capable of flight. Their ability to fly allows them to escape predators more easily and also to find food and mates more efficiently.

translations.source: Ihe karịrị ọtụtụ n’ime ụmụ ahụhụ nwere uru nke inwe ike ịpịa nku ha gaa n’ahụ ha.
translations.reference: Most insects have the advantage of being able to fold their wings back along the body.
translations.hypothesis: For many people who suffer from it, one of the benefits of having eczema is the ability to scratch their skin.

translations.source: Nke a na-eme ka ha nwee ọtụtụ ebe izonarị ndị na-eri ha.
translations.reference: This gives them a wider range of small places to hide from predators.
translations.hypothesis: This makes them vulnerable to various forms of exploitation.

translations.source: Ubochi taa, nani ogugu nwere ike ikpalaga nku ya azu bu ogugu drago na ogugu may.
translations.reference: Today, the only insects that cannot fold back their wings are dragon flies and mayflies.
translations.hypothesis: Today, the only numbers that can be divided by both 3 and 5 are multiples of 15.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ puku afọ gara aga, otu nwoke a kpọrọ Aristarchus kwuru si na Usoro Mbara Igwe nọ na-agagharị gburugburu Anyanwụ.
translations.reference: Thousands of years ago, a man called Aristarchus said that the Solar System moved around the Sun.
translations.hypothesis: Thousands of years ago, a man named Aristarchus proposed that the celestial bodies revolve around the Sun.

translations.source: Ufodu ndi mmadu chere na ihe o na-ekwu bu eziokwu mana ufodu ekweghi; na mbara igwe na-agba uwa okirikiri ma anyanwu(ma kwa kpakpando ndi ozo)
translations.reference: Some people thought he was right but many people believed the opposite; that the Solar System moved around the Earth, including the Sun (and even the other stars).
translations.hypothesis: Many people believe that what they are told is the truth, but this is not always the case; the sky appears blue, but it is actually a mixture of gases and the sun (and other celestial bodies) reflect light.

translations.source: Nke a yiri ezi uche, n’ihi na ọ naghị emetụta ka ụwa ọ na-agagharị agagharị, ọ na-emetụta?
translations.reference: This seems sensible, because the Earth doesn't feel as if it's moving, does it?
translations.hypothesis: This seems reasonable, because if it doesn't affect the world it operates in, does it really matter?

translations.source: Osimiri Amazọn ahụ bụ nke abụọ kachasị ogologo na osimiri kachasị n’ibu n’ụwa. Ọ na-ebu ihe karịrị nha mmiri ugboro asatọ dị ka osimiri nke abụọ kachasị ibu.
translations.reference: The Amazon River is the second longest and the biggest river on Earth. It carries more than 8 times as much water as the second biggest river.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon River is the second longest river in the world and the most voluminous. It carries more than nine times the amount of water than the second most voluminous river.

translations.source: Amazọn bụkwa osimiri kachasị saa mbara n'ụwa, mgbe ụfọdụ ọ na-eru maịlụ isii.
translations.reference: The Amazon is also the widest river on Earth, at times six miles wide.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon is also the largest river in the world, and it can sometimes reach a width of six miles.

translations.source: Pasentị mmmiri 20 zuru oke nke na-awụpụta site na osimiri ụwa ga na-abanye n'ime oke osimiri ga si n'Amazọn abịa.
translations.reference: A full 20 percent of the water that pours out of the planet's rivers into the oceans comes from the Amazon.
translations.hypothesis: Twenty fully equipped research vessels will enter the coastal waters, arriving from the Amazon region.

translations.source: Isi osimiri Amazọnụ dị km 6,387 (maịlị 3,980). Ọ na-ewetaju mmiri site n’ọtụtụ puku osimiri ndị kara di obere.
translations.reference: The main Amazon River is 6,387 km (3,980 miles). It collects water from thousands of smaller rivers.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon River is 6,387 kilometers (3,980 miles) long. It receives water from tens of thousands of smaller rivers.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị na ọrụrụ-piramidi n’okwute gara n’ihu ruo na njedebe nke Alaeze Ochie, ụmụ piramidi nke Giza bụ ndị agafeghị ma ọlị na nha ha na ima mma nka na ụzụ nke ọrụrụ ha.
translations.reference: Although pyramid-building in stone continued until the end of the Old Kingdom, the pyramids of Giza were never surpassed in their size and the technical excellence of their construction.
translations.hypothesis: Despite the decline of pyramid construction towards the end of the Old Kingdom, the pyramids of Giza remain unparalleled in their size, artistic beauty, and engineering prowess.

translations.source: O juru ndị Niu Kịngdọm Ijipt mgbe ochie anya ihe ncheta ndị bu ha ụzọ, nke gaferela otu puku afọ mgbe ahụ.
translations.reference: New Kingdom ancient Egyptians marvelled at their predecessors monuments, which were then well over a thousand year old.
translations.hypothesis: The ancient monuments of the Kingdom of Egypt, which guided them, had stood for over a thousand years.

translations.source: Onu ogugu ndi mmadu obodo Vatican di nari 800. O bu obodo kacha nta n’uwa n’uwa n’uwa na obodo n’ogbe ndi kacha pere mpe.
translations.reference: Vatican City's population is around 800. It is the smallest independent country in the world and the country with the lowest population.
translations.hypothesis: The Vatican City has a population of approximately 800 people. It is the smallest country in the world, both in terms of land area and population.

translations.source: Obodo Vatican na-eji asụsụ Italian na iwu na ukara nkwukọrịta ya.
translations.reference: Vatican City uses Italian in its legislation and official communications.
translations.hypothesis: The Vatican City State uses the Italian language for its official communications and legal proceedings.

translations.source: Asụsụ Itali ka ọtụtụ ndị na-arụ ọrụ na steeti na-asụkwa kwa ụbọchị ebe a na-asụkarị Latin n’emume ndị ụka ga.
translations.reference: Italian is also the everyday language used by most of those who work in the state while Latin is often used in religious ceremonies.
translations.hypothesis: Italian is the language spoken by many workers in the state, and it is also commonly used in formal events where Latin was traditionally spoken.

translations.source: Ndị obodo niile nke Obodo Vatican bụ Roman Katọlik.
translations.reference: All citizens of Vatican City are Roman Catholic.
translations.hypothesis: All the cities within the Vatican City are Roman Catholic.

translations.source: Ndị mmadụ amarala maka isi kemịkalụ njìmebe ndị dị ka ọlaedo, ọlaọcha, ọla kọpa sitere na oge ochie, dị ka enwere ike ịchọpụta ihe ndị a n’ụwa n’ụdị mbupụtaụwa ma dịrị mfe igwupụta n’iji ngwaọrụ ndị mgbe ochie.
translations.reference: People have known about basic chemical elements such as gold, silver, and copper from antiquity, as these can all be discovered in nature in native form and are relatively simple to mine with primitive tools.
translations.hypothesis: People have long been aware of valuable chemical elements like gold, silver, and copper, which can be found in nature in their pure form and are relatively easy to extract using ancient tools.

translations.source: Aristotle, bụ onye ọka ihe ọmụma, ekwuola na tiori na ihe niile bụ mgwọkọta njimebe otu ma ọ bụ karịa mejupụtara ya. Ha wụbụ aja, mmiri, ikuku, na ọkụ.
translations.reference: Aristotle, a philosopher, theorised that everything is made up of a mixture of one or more of four elements. They were earth, water, air, and fire.
translations.hypothesis: Aristotle, a renowned philosopher, stated that all matter is composed of one or more fundamental elements. These elements are earth, water, air, and fire.

translations.source: Nke a dị kara yiri ọnọdụ anọ nke mata (n’usoro ahụ kwa): nsiriike, mmiri mmiri, ikuku, na plasma, agbanyeghị na o nyere tiori na ha na-agbanwe ghụọ umi ọhụrụ iji mepụta ihe anyị na-ahụ anya.
translations.reference: This was more like the four states of matter (in the same order): solid, liquid, gas, and plasma, though he also theorised that they change into new substances to form what we see.
translations.hypothesis: This is similar to the four states of matter (in order): solid, liquid, gas, and plasma; however, it proposes that they transform into a new state to create what we perceive.

translations.source: Ụmụ alọị bụgodu mwurikọta ígwè abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa. Echefula na e nwere ọtụtụ njìmebe nọ na tebụlụ pirịọdik.
translations.reference: Alloys are basically a mixture of two or more metals. Don't forget that there are many elements on the periodic table.
translations.hypothesis: Umụ alọị (students) are often grouped into pairs or larger teams. Keep in mind that there are often several variations or versions of the periodic table available.

translations.source: Ihe ndị dị ka kalsium na potassium bụ igwe. Ee, enwekwara igwe ndị ọzọ dịka ọla ọcha na ọla edo.
translations.reference: Elements like calcium and potassium are considered metals. Of course, there are also metals like silver and gold.
translations.hypothesis: Elements like calcium and potassium are metals. Yes, there are also other metals, such as silver and gold.

translations.source: I nwekwara ike nwee allọyi nke gụnyere nwa-obere njieme gasị nke enweghị metalik dịka cabọn.
translations.reference: You can also have alloys that include small amounts of non-metallic elements like carbon.
translations.hypothesis: It is also possible to have a type of alloy that includes a small amount of non-metallic material, such as carbon.

translations.source: Ihe niile dị na elu ụwa a nwere mata. Mata niile bụ njikọ ọtụtụ obere ihe a na-akpọ atọm.
translations.reference: Everything in the Universe is made of matter. All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms.
translations.hypothesis: Everything in this world is made of matter. Matter is composed of countless tiny particles called atoms.

translations.source: Atọm pere nnọọ mpe ruo na puku ijeri ga-abali n'ime akara kpọm nọ na ngwụcha okwu a.
translations.reference: Atoms are so incredibly tiny that trillions of them could fit into the period at the end of this sentence.
translations.hypothesis: The number of characters remaining in this message is between zero and one hundred million.

translations.source: Ya mere, pensụl ahụ wụbụ ezigbo enyị nye ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ mgbe ọ pụtara.
translations.reference: Thus, the pencil was a good friend to many people when it came out.
translations.hypothesis: Therefore, the pencil became a valuable tool for many people when it was introduced.

translations.source: Ọ bụ ihe mwute na ka ụzọ ọhụrụ e si ede ihe na-apụta, 'ọkwa', mkpịsịodee ọkpọọ bụzi ihe a tụlagara n'akụkụ anaghịzikwa eji ya ede ihe mgbe niile.
translations.reference: Sadly, as newer methods of writing have emerged, the pencil has been relegated to lesser status and uses.
translations.hypothesis: It is unfortunate that as new writing technologies emerge, the "quill," fountain pen, or even a simple pen, are often overlooked and not always used for writing anymore.

translations.source: Ndị mmadụ na-edezi ozi na ihuenyo kọmputa gasị, o nweghị mgbe ha na-enwe ịbịaru nso na otu ọmụ nkọ.
translations.reference: People now write messages on computer screens, never having to come close to a sharpener.
translations.hypothesis: People who communicate through computer screens often lack the personal connection that comes from face-to-face interaction.

translations.source: Mmadụ ga na-atụ naanị n’uche ihe kiibọọdụ ga-abụzi mgbe ihe kara dị ọhụrụ bịaziri.
translations.reference: One can only wonder what the keyboard will become when something newer comes along.
translations.hypothesis: People often only think about keyboards when something goes wrong with them, or when a new technology emerges.

translations.source: Bọmbụ fishọn ahụ na-arụ ọrụ n’iwu na ọ na ewere ike ijikọta otu nuclus ya na ọtụtụ protọnụ na nutrọnụ.
translations.reference: The fission bomb works on the principle that it takes energy to put together a nucleus with many protons and neutrons.
translations.hypothesis: The atomic bomb works by releasing energy through nuclear fission, a process where the nucleus of an atom splits into multiple protons and neutrons.

translations.source: Dika ibinggasi ugbo-ala nke di elu.Nkewa dị na etiti na elụ wee wepụta ike ụfọdụ.
translations.reference: Sort of like rolling a heavy cart up a hill. Splitting the nucleus up again then releases some of that energy.
translations.hypothesis: Like a high-yielding farmland, the arrangement is central and efficient, maximizing productivity.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ atọm nwere nukei na-anọsighị ike nke pụtara na ha na-agbajikarị n'iji obere ma ọ bụ n'enweghị akwamaka.
translations.reference: Some atoms have unstable nuclei which means that they tend to break apart with little or no nudging.
translations.hypothesis: Some atoms have unstable nuclei, which means they are prone to decay, often emitting small amounts of energy or particles.

translations.source: Elu ọnwa bụ ụmụ okwute na ájá mejupụtara ya. Mkpuchi mpụga ọnwa ka a na-akpọ krọstụ.
translations.reference: The surface of the Moon is made of rocks and dust. The outer layer of the Moon is called the crust.
translations.hypothesis: Moon rocks are rocks and minerals that have been collected from the Moon. The outer layer of the Moon is often referred to as the crust.

translations.source: Crọstụ ahụ dị ihe dị ka km70 n'ịgba agba n'akụkụ ya dị nso na km100 n'ịgba ịgba n'akụkụ ya tere anya.
translations.reference: The crust is about 70 km thick on the near side and 100 km thick on the far side.
translations.hypothesis: The road is approximately 70 kilometers long and stretches for about 100 kilometers along the coastline.

translations.source: Ọ kara taa ahụ n'okpuru marịa ma kara gbaa agba n'okpuru ụmụ ala ugwu ugwu ahụ.
translations.reference: It is thinner under the maria and thicker under the highlands.
translations.hypothesis: The sun shone brightly today, warming the ground beneath the tall trees.

translations.source: E nwere ike nwekwuo marịa ọzọ n'akụkụ ya dị nso n'ihi na krọstụ ya kara taa ahụ. Ọ kara dịrị mfe maka lava ịrịgote n'elu ya ahụ.
translations.reference: There may be more maria on the near side because the crust is thinner. It was easier for lava to rise up to the surface.
translations.hypothesis: It might be possible to see more activity nearby because the cross-section reveals a higher concentration of material. This makes it easier for lava to flow over the surface.

translations.source: Tiori ndịnà bụ ndị a gbadoro anya ha ịchọta ihe na-eme ndị mmadụ kpaa agwa ha na-akpa ma ọ bụ ihe na-amasị ha.
translations.reference: Content theories are centered on finding what makes people tick or appeals to them.
translations.hypothesis: Theorists are people who dedicate their time to understanding the reasons behind human behavior and motivations.

translations.source: Tiori ndị a na-ekwu na ndị mmadụ nwere mkpa ụfọdụ na/ma ọ bụ ọchịchọ nke ndị e chechala ma tinye n'uche dị ka ha na-etozuru ntorọbịa.
translations.reference: These theories suggest that people have certain needs and/or desires which have been internalized as they mature to adulthood.
translations.hypothesis: These theories suggest that people have certain needs and/or desires that are triggered or become more prominent when they face challenges.

translations.source: Tiori ndị a na-eleba anya n'ihe gbasara ụfọdụ ndị mmadụ nke kpatara ha ji achọ ihe ndị ha chọrọ na kedu ụmụ ihe nọ na gburugburu ebe obibi ha ga-eme ha mee ma ọ bụ emela ụfọdụ ihe.
translations.reference: These theories look at what it is about certain people that make them want the things that they do and what things in their environment will make them do or not do certain things.
translations.hypothesis: These theories examine the factors that influence people's desires and the ways in which their environment shapes their behavior or has already shaped their experiences.

translations.source: Uzo-echiche ihe-di_n’ime abuo ama ama bu uzo-echiche ogogo nke mkpa nke Maslow na uzo-echiche ihe abuo kpatara nke Hertzberg.
translations.reference: Two popular content theories are Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs Theory and Hertzberg's Two Factor Theory.
translations.hypothesis: Two prominent theories of motivation are Maslow's hierarchy of needs and Herzberg's two-factor theory.

translations.source: Ikwu n'izugbe, akparamaagwa abụọ nwere ike ịpụta dịka ndị  nlekọta na-amalite idu ndị ọgbọ ha ochie. Otu mpaghara n'echiche ahụ bụ "ịgbalị ịnọrọ dịka otu n'ime ụmụokorọbịa" (maọbụ ụmụagbọghọbịa).
translations.reference: Generally speaking, two behaviors can emerge as managers begin to lead their former peers. One end of the spectrum is trying to remain “one of the guys” (or gals).
translations.hypothesis: In many communities, two contrasting trends can emerge as younger generations begin to distance themselves from their elders. One prominent aspect of this is the desire to "fit in" with their peers (or, in the case of young women, their female counterparts).

translations.reference: The modern city of Casablanca was founded by Berber fishermen in the 10th century BCE, and was used by the Phoenicians, Romans, and the Merenids as a strategic port called Anfa.
translations.hypothesis: The city of Casablanca, as it exists today, was founded by Berber fishermen in the 10th century BCE. However, the Phoenicians, Romans, and Merenids used it as a vital port and called it Anfa.

translations.source: Ndị Pọtụgaalụ bibiri ya ma rụgharịa ya n’okpuru aha Casa Branca, naanị ịgbahapụ ya mgbe otu ala ọma jijiji mechara n’ime 1755.
translations.reference: The Portuguese destroyed it and rebuilt it under the name Casa Branca, only to abandon it after an earthquake in 1755.
translations.hypothesis: The Portuguese built it and initially called it Casa Branca, but it was later destroyed in the earthquake of 1755.

translations.source: Sọltan Ndị Moroko ahụ rụgharịrị obodo ahụ dị ka Darụ-I-Badya ma e nyere ya aha Casablanka site n'aka Ndị Spen na-azụ ahịa ndị wubere isi ebe ndị a na-ere ahịa ebe ahụ.
translations.reference: The Moroccan sultan rebuilt the city as Daru l-Badya and it was given the name Casablanca by Spanish traders who established trading bases there.
translations.hypothesis: The Moroccan Sultan transformed the city of Dar-el-Badya and renamed it Casablanca, a name given to it by Spanish merchants who frequented the markets there.

translations.source: Casablanca bụ otu n'ime opekata mpe ebe na-adọrọ mmasị ịzụ ahịa na Morocco niile.
translations.reference: Casablanca is one of the least interesting places to shop in all of Morocco.
translations.hypothesis: Casablanca is one of the most interesting places to shop in all of Morocco.

translations.source: Gburugburu Medina ochie ahụ ọ dị mfe ịchọta ebe ndị na-ere ụmụ ngwaahịa ọdịnala Ndị Moroko, dị ka ụmụ tagịnị, ite akpụrụ akpụ, ngwaahịa ejiri akpụkpọ anụ mee, huuka, na giigawụ nke ụdịdị dị iche iche zuru ezu, mana ha nille bụ maka ndị nleta.
translations.reference: Around the old Medina it's easy to find places selling traditional Moroccan goods, such as tagines, pottery, leather goods, hookahs, and a whole spectrum of geegaws, but it's all for the tourists.
translations.hypothesis: The old Medina area makes it easy to find shops selling traditional Moroccan products, such as tagines, pottery, leather goods, hookahs, and various types of musical instruments, but these are primarily aimed at tourists.

translations.source: Goma bụ obodo nleta nke Democratic Replublic nke Kongo n'ime akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ kachasị anya na nso Rwanda.
translations.reference: Goma is a tourist city of the Democratic Republic of Congo in the extreme east near Rwanda.
translations.hypothesis: Goma is a city in the Democratic Republic of Congo, located in the far eastern part of the country, near the border with Rwanda.

translations.source: N'afọ 2002, ebibiri Goma site n’aka lava si na ugwu ọkụ Nyiragongo nke liri ọtụtụ n'okporoama obodo, ọ kachasị etiti obodo.
translations.reference: In 2002 Goma was destroyed by lava from the Nyiragongo volcano which buried most of the town’s streets, particularly the town centre.
translations.hypothesis: In 2002, Goma was attacked by lava flowing from the Nyiragongo volcano, which is located near the city and poses a significant threat to its inhabitants.

translations.source: Dịka Goma nwetụrụ nchekwa n’ụdị dịtụ mma, nleta ọ bụla na mpụga Goma bụ nke ekwesịrị inyocha iji ghọta ọnọdụ nke ọgụ ka nogidesiri ike n’Ugwu ngalaba ọchịchị kizu.
translations.reference: While Goma is reasonably safe, any visits outside of Goma should be researched to understand the state of the fighting that persists in the North Kivu province.
translations.hypothesis: As Goma remains under a fragile peace, any external visit to Goma should be carefully considered to understand the ongoing situation and the challenges of maintaining stability in the conflict-ridden eastern region.

translations.source: Obodo ahụ bụkwa ntọala ịrị ugwu mgbawa Nyiragongo tinyere ụfọdụ nsochi Ọzọdimgba Ugwu dịchasị ọnụ ala n'Afrịka.
translations.reference: The city is also the base to climb the Nyiragongo volcano along with some of the cheapest Mountain Gorilla tracking in Africa.
translations.hypothesis: The city is also located near the Nyiragongo volcano, along with other significant geographical features that define the landscape of East Africa.

translations.source: Ị nwere ike iji boda-boda (tagzi ọgba tum tum) ịga gburugburu Goma. Ọnụahịa nkịtị (ebeụlọ) bụ Francs Ndị Congo ~500 maka ọkwụkwọ dị mkpirikpi.
translations.reference: You can use boda-boda (motorcycle taxi) to get around Goma. The normal (local) price is ~500 Congolese Francs for the short ride.
translations.hypothesis: You can use a motorcycle taxi (often called a "moto") to get around Goma. The standard (local) price is approximately 500 Congolese Francs for a short trip.

translations.source: Tinyere na ira-ahu na nweta ya karia ibe ya, "Timbuktu" aburula ihe eji ama-atu maka ala ndi di anya, di oke-onu.
translations.reference: Combined with its relative inaccessibility, "Timbuktu" has come to be used as a metaphor for exotic, distant lands.
translations.hypothesis: While the name might suggest a more modest origin, "Timbuktu" has become a symbol of luxury and exclusivity, surpassing its competitors.

translations.source: Taa, Timbuktu obodo agụọ na-egbu, agbanyeghị n'ugwu ya na-eme ya otu ndọta ndị nleta, na o nwere otu ọdụ ụgbọelu.
translations.reference: Today, Timbuktu is an impoverished town, although its reputation makes it a tourist attraction, and it has an airport.
translations.hypothesis: Today, Timbuktu is a bustling city, despite its remote location and the fact that it only has one airport.

translations.source: N'afọ 1990, e debanyere ya n'etiti ebe ọpụrụiche n'ụwa ndị nọ na nsogbu mkpochapụ, maka nsogbu aja si n'ọzara.
translations.reference: In 1990, it was added to the list of world heritage sites in danger, due to the threat of desert sands.
translations.hypothesis: In 1990, he was inducted into the Hall of Fame for troubled youths, due to his struggles with addiction.

translations.source: Ọ bụ otu isi nkwụsịtụ n'oge Henry Louis Gates Ihe-ebube pụrụ iche PBS nke Ụwa Afrịka.
translations.reference: It was one of the major stops during Henry Louis Gates' PBS special Wonders of the African World.
translations.hypothesis: It is a highlight of the Henry Louis Gates Jr. documentary series "Finding Your Roots" on PBS, which focuses on African American history.

translations.source: Obodo ahụ dị n'ọdịiche kachasị ya n'ụmụ obodo nke mba ahụ fọdụrụnụ, n'ihi na o nwere karịa mmasị nke Arabik karịa otu Onye Afrịka.
translations.reference: The city is in stark contrast to the rest of the country's cities, because it has more of an Arabic flair than of an African.
translations.hypothesis: The city stands out among the citizens of the divided nation because it shows a greater preference for Arabic culture than for African culture.

translations.source: Obianụọhịa Kemba Kruger (KNP) nọ n'ebe ugwu-ọwụwa anyanwu nke South Afrịka ma nọrọ ogologo ókè ahụ nke Mozambik n'ime ọwụwa anyanwụ, Zimbabwe n'ime ebe ugwu, na ókè ebe ndịda ahụ bụ Osimmiri Agụiyi.
translations.reference: The Kruger National Park (KNP) lies in the north-east of South Africa and runs along the border of Mozambique in the east, Zimbabwe in the north, and the southern border is the Crocodile River.
translations.hypothesis: The Kruger National Park (KNP) is located in the northeastern part of South Africa and extends along a long stretch of the Mozambican border to the east, with Zimbabwe to the north, and the Indian Ocean to the southeast.

translations.source: Ogige a ruru 19,500 km² nakwa ekewara ya n'ụzọ mpaghara ecozone 14, ebe nke ọbụla na-akwado ụdịrị anụ ọhịa dị iche.
translations.reference: The park covers 19,500 km² and is divided in 14 different ecozones, each supporting different wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: This area covers 19,500 square kilometers and is divided into 14 distinct ecological zones, each supporting a unique variety of wildlife.

translations.source: Ọ bụ otu n’ime nke isi ihe ndọta nke Ndịda Afrịka ma a na-ewe ya dị ka nke kacha mma nke Ebennọkọta Nkeobodo (SANParks) Ndịda Afrịka.
translations.reference: It is one of the main attractions of South Africa and it is considered the flagship of South African National Parks (SANParks).
translations.hypothesis: It is one of the most important conservation areas in Southern Africa and is considered a flagship reserve of South African National Parks (SANParks).

translations.source: Dịka o si adị n'ogige mba niile nọ na Sawụtụ Afrịka, e nwere ụgwọ nchekwa n mbanye a na-akwụ kwa ụbọchị n'ogige a.
translations.reference: As with all South African National Parks, there are daily conservation and entry fees for the park.
translations.hypothesis: As with many national parks in Southern Africa, this reserve has a daily conservation fee that visitors must pay.

translations.source: O nwekwara ike iba uru ka mmadu gote Kaadi Ohia nke ga-enye gi ikikere iji banye na ogige ahoputagoro na South Africa ma o bu na Ogige Kemba South Africa niile.
translations.reference: It may also be beneficial for one to buy a Wild Card, which provides entry to either selections of parks in South Africa or all of the South African National Parks.
translations.hypothesis: It is also possible to benefit from purchasing a Wild Card, which will give you access to all the national parks in South Africa, including all the Kruger National Park locations.

translations.source: Ọ bụ site na Agwaetiti Họng Kọng ka mpaghara Họng Kọng nwetara aha ya; Ọ bụkwa ebe a ka ndị njem nlereanya na-ahụta dịka ebe kachasị mkpa.
translations.reference: Hong Kong Island gives the territory of Hong Kong its name and is the place that many tourists regard as the main focus.
translations.hypothesis: The Hong Kong region derives its name from Hong Kong Island; it is also considered the most important destination for tourists and visitors.

translations.source: E jirila ụmụ ogologo ụlọ elu na-achọ igwe Họng Kọng mma maa atụ na ha yiri eserese baa chat, nke mmiri Viktoria Habọ mere ka ọ pụta ihe.
translations.reference: The parade of buildings that make the Hong Kong skyline has been likened to a glittering bar chart that is made apparent by the presence of the waters of Victoria Harbour.
translations.hypothesis: The residents of the high-rise building were captivated by the beautiful rainbow that appeared, resembling a chat bubble, after a rain shower caused by Victoria Habo.

translations.source: Ịhụta Họng Kọng n'ụzọ kachasị mma, pụọ n'agwaetiti gawa na Kowloon, mpaghara akụkụ mmiri, nke chere gị ihu.
translations.reference: To get the best views of Hong Kong, leave the island and head for the Kowloon waterfront opposite.
translations.hypothesis: To experience Hong Kong in the best way, leave the mainland and head to Kowloon, the coastal district that awaits you.

translations.source: Oke ihe ka n'ọnụ ọgụgụ n'ime mmepe obodo nke Agwaetiti Hong Kong jupụtara n'ọnụ na ala a napụtara na mmiri dị n'ogologo ụzọ nke ugwu akụkụ oke osimiri.
translations.reference: The great majority of Hong Kong Island's urban development is densely packed on reclaimed land along the northern shore.
translations.hypothesis: The numerous buildings in the urban development of Hong Kong Island are situated on a narrow strip of land along the coastline of the eastern part of the island.

translations.source: Ebe a bụ ebe ndị nchịkwa mba si Britenụ were dịka nke ha ya mere ọ bụrụ na ị na-achọ maka akaebe nke nchịkwa ókèala ahụ gara aga, ebe a bụ ebe dị mma ịmalite.
translations.reference: This is the place the British colonisers took as their own and so if you are looking for evidence of the territory's colonial past, this is a good place to start.
translations.hypothesis: This is where the administrators of the country, Britain, used to be located, so if you are looking for a glimpse into the past of colonial administration, this is a good place to start.

translations.source: Ebe Sundarbans bụ ebe ala nwere ọhịa mmiri nọ n'akụkụ mmiri kachasị ukwuu n'ụwa dum, na-agbatị ruo kilomita 80 (50 mi) n'ime n'ala Bangladesh na India ahụ nke amaghị ama site n'ụsọ osimiri.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans are the largest littoral mangrove belt in the world, stretching 80 km (50 mi) into the Bangladeshi and Indian hinterland from the coast.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans is a vast mangrove forest located in the delta region of the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers, stretching for approximately 80 kilometers (50 miles) inland into the territories of Bangladesh and India, bordering the Bay of Bengal.

translations.source: E kwupụtawo na Sundarbans bụ otu Ebe Nketa Keụwa UNESCO. Akụkụ nke oke ọhịa n'ime ókèala nke Indịa ka a na-akpọ Obianụọhịa Kemba Sundarbans.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The part of the forest within Indian territory is called Sundarbans National Park.
translations.hypothesis: It has been declared that the Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A portion of the mangrove forest within the Indian border is also known as the Kempa Sundarbans wildlife sanctuary.

translations.source: Ọhịa ndị a abụghịkwa sọọsọ apịtị mangrov dị na ha – ha gụnyekwara ihe ndị ka fọrọ site n'oke ọhịa ndị juburu Ala nọ na mpaghara Ganjiz.
translations.reference: The forests aren't just mangrove swamps though — they include some of the last remaining stands of the mighty jungles which once covered the Gangetic plain.
translations.hypothesis: These diseases are not just limited to mangrove forests; they also include other plant diseases that affect vegetation found in the Ganjiz region.

translations.source: Sundabans kpuchiri ohere km² 3850, nke mmiri maọbụ ala apịtị kpuchiri otu ụzọ n'ụzọ atọ ya.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans cover an area of 3,850 km², of which about one-third is covered in water/marsh areas.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans covers an area of 3,850 square kilometers, with about one-third of it being covered by water.

translations.source: Ka mgbe 1966, ka Sundarbans ji buru ebe obibi nso anu ohia ana asi na aga enwe ihe dika 400 Royal Bengal tiger na ihe dika 30,000 mgbada nwere ntupo na mpaghara ebe ahu.
translations.reference: Since 1966 the Sundarbans have been a wildlife sanctuary, and it is estimated that there are now 400 Royal Bengal tigers and about 30,000 spotted deer in the area.
translations.hypothesis: Before 1966, the Sundarbans, a vast mangrove forest bordering India and Bangladesh, was estimated to be home to around 400 Royal Bengal tigers and approximately 30,000 spotted deer within its boundaries.

translations.source: Bọọsụ na-esi n'ọdụ ụgbọala njikọ-mpaghara apụ (n'ofe osimiri ahụ) mgbe niile n'ụbọchị, agbanyeghị na nke kacha, tụmadị ndị ahụ na-aga n'ebe ọwụwaanyanwụ na Jakar/Bumthang na-apụ n'etiti 06:30 na 07:30.
translations.reference: Buses depart the inter-district bus station (across the river) throughout the day, though most, especially those heading to the east and Jakar/Bumthang leave between 06:30 and 07:30.
translations.hypothesis: Buses regularly depart from the regional bus station (on the other side of the river) throughout the day. However, the most frequent departures for those traveling to Jakar/Bumthang occur between 6:30 AM and 7:30 AM.

translations.source: Dị ka ụmụ bọọsụ njikọ-mpaghara na-ejukarị eju, ọ bụ ezi ndụmọdụ ịzụta otu tiketi ụbọchị ole na ole n'ọdịnihu.
translations.reference: As the inter-district buses are often full, it is advisable to purchase a ticket a few days in advance.
translations.hypothesis: As regional transportation companies often increase fares, it's a good idea to purchase a multi-day ticket in advance.

translations.source: A na-ejere imirikiti mpaghara ozi site n'ụmụ Nnukwu Bọọsụ nke ndị Japan, nke dị mma ma sie ike.
translations.reference: Most districts are served by small Japanese Coaster Buses, which are comfortable and sturdy.
translations.hypothesis: Japanese companies, particularly large corporations, are known for their rigorous and demanding work environments.

translations.source: Tagzi ekere eke bụ ụzọ dị ọsịsọ ma maa mma iji gaa ebe dị nso, dịka Paro (Nu 150) na Punakha (Nu 200).
translations.reference: Shared taxis are a quick and comfortable means to travel to nearby places, such as Paro (Nu 150) and Punakha (Nu 200).
translations.hypothesis: The scenic mountain roads are a beautiful way to travel to nearby places, such as Paro (approximately 150 kilometers) and Punakha (approximately 200 kilometers).

translations.source: Akwammiri Osimiri Oyapock bụ otu akwa mmiri ejiri kebùl runye ya. Ọ gbara gburugburu Osimiri Oyapock iji jikọọ ụmụ obodo nke Oiapoque n'ime Brazịl na Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock n'ime French Guiana.
translations.reference: The Oyapock River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge. It spans the Oyapock River to link the cities of Oiapoque in Brazil and Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock in French Guiana.
translations.hypothesis: The Oyapock River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge that spans the Oyapock River. It connects the town of Oiapoque in Brazil with Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock in French Guiana.

translations.source: Towa abuo ahu rigoro 83 meters, ogologo o bu 378 meters n’ogologo ma o nwekwara obodobo uzo abuo di 3.50m.
translations.reference: The two towers rise to a height of 83 meters, it's 378 meters long and it has two lanes of 3.50 m wide.
translations.hypothesis: The bridge has a height of 83 meters, a length of 378 meters, and also features two traffic lanes, each 3.50 meters wide.

translations.source: Ogologo ahụ ya kwụ-ọtọ nke akwa mmiri ahụ bụ mita 15. A rụchara ọrụrụ ya n'Ọgọọst 2011, e mepeghị ya nye ụgbọala ruo Maachị 2017.
translations.reference: The vertical clearance under the bridge is 15 meters. Construction was completed in August 2011, it didn't open to traffic until March 2017.
translations.hypothesis: The length of the tunnel is 15 meters. It was completed in August 2011, but it was not opened to traffic until March 2017.

translations.source: E hiwere na akwa ahụ ga-ebido rụwa ọrụ n'uju na Septemba 2017, mgbe a na-ele anya ịrụcha ebe nnyocha nke ụlọọrụ na-ahụ maka ọpụpụ na mbata nke ndị Brazili.
translations.reference: The bridge is scheduled to be fully operational in September 2017, when the Brazilian customs checkpoints are expected to be finished.
translations.hypothesis: It is expected that the system will begin operating fully in September 2017, following the completion of the inspection of the facility responsible for the entry and exit of Brazilian citizens.

translations.source: Ndị Guaraní bụ otu amaala kachasị gbaa ọkpụrụkpụrụ bi n'eba a na-akpọ ugbua Ọwụwaanyanwụ Paragụwa, ha na-ebi ka ndị dinta na-awagharị awagharị ma na-arụkwa ọrụ ugbo mmepụta nri nke onwe.
translations.reference: The Guaraní were the most significant indigenous group inhabiting what is now Eastern Paraguay, living as semi-nomadic hunters who also practised subsistence agriculture.
translations.hypothesis: The Guarani people are an indigenous group living in the Gran Chaco region, primarily in Paraguay. They traditionally live a nomadic lifestyle, but also engage in subsistence agriculture.

translations.source: Mpaghara Chako bụ ụlọ nye ụfọdụ agbụrụ amaala ndị ọzọ dịka Guaykuru na Payagua, ndị ji nta, ntụtụkọ, na ịkụ azụ wee zụọ onwe ha nri.
translations.reference: The Chaco region was home to other groups of indigenous tribes such as the Guaycurú and Payaguá, who survived by hunting, gathering and fishing.
translations.hypothesis: The Chaco region is home to several indigenous groups, such as the Guaykuru and Payagua, who traditionally relied on hunting, gathering, and fishing to sustain themselves.

translations.source: N'ime narị afọ nke iri na isii Paragwei, a kpọbụrụ "Nnukwu Ngalaba Ọchịchị nke Ndị Indii", bụ nke a mụrụ n'ihi mbịakwute nke ndị mmeri Ndị Spen ya na ụmụ òtù nwaafọ amaala.
translations.reference: In the 16th century Paraguay, formerly called "The Giant Province of the Indies", was born as a result of the encounter of Spanish conquerors with the native indigenous groups.
translations.hypothesis: During the sixteenth century in Paraguay, a group known as the "Great Paraguayan Province" emerged, formed as a result of conflicts between the Spanish conquistadors and the indigenous population.

translations.source: Ndị Spen bidoro oge ọchịchị ike nke digidere ruo narị afọ atọ.
translations.reference: The Spaniards started the colonization period which lasted for three centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The Spanish ruled for a period of three centuries.

translations.source: Kemgbe ntọala Asunción n’ime 1537, Paraguay agbalịala idobe ọtụtụ n’ime omume na njirimara amaala ya.
translations.reference: Since the foundation of Asunción in 1537, Paraguay has managed to keep a lot of its indigenous character and identity.
translations.hypothesis: Since the founding of Asunción in 1537, Paraguay has strived to maintain many of its traditions and cultural characteristics.

translations.source: Amaara mba Ajentịna dịka obodo nwere ndị egwuregwu na otu egwuregwu polo kachasị mma n'ụwa dum.
translations.reference: Argentina is well known for having one of the best polo teams and players in the world.
translations.hypothesis: Argentina is known as a country with passionate sports fans and boasts one of the best polo teams in the world.

translations.source: Ndọrọndọrọ kachasị ukwu nke afọ ahụ na-eme na Disemba na fịịldị polo n’ime Las Cañitas.
translations.reference: The largest tournament of the year takes place in December at the polo fields in Las Cañitas.
translations.hypothesis: The most important event of the year takes place in December at the polo field in Las Cañitas.

translations.source: Obere asọmpi ga na egwuregwu bọlụ ga ka e nwere ike ịhụ ebe a n'oge ụfọdụ n'afọ.
translations.reference: Smaller tournaments and matches can also be seen here at other times of the year.
translations.hypothesis: Occasionally, during a football game, you might witness a moment of intense competition.

translations.source: Maka akụkọ gbasara ụmụ ndorondoro na ebe a na-azụ tiketi maka egwuregwu polo, lelee Asociacion Argentina de Polo.
translations.reference: For news on tournaments and where to buy tickets for polo matches, check Asociacion Argentina de Polo.
translations.hypothesis: For information about polo players and where to buy tickets for polo matches, please visit the Asociacion Argentina de Polo website.

translations.source: Ego azụmahịa mba Fọlkụlandị bụ pam Fọlkụlandị (FKP) nke ọnụ ya na otu pam ndị Britenị (GBP) ha.
translations.reference: The official Falklands currency is the Falkland pound (FKP) whose value is set equivalent to that of one British pound (GBP).
translations.hypothesis: The official currency of the Falkland Islands is the Falkland Pound (FKP), which is equivalent in value to the British Pound (GBP).

translations.source: E nere ike ime mgbanwe ego na naanị otu ụlọ akụ nọ n’agwaetiti ndị ahụ nke a ga-achọtali n’ime Stanley n’ofe site n’ụlọ ahịa FIC West.
translations.reference: Money can be exchanged at the only bank in the islands which is located in Stanley across from the FIC West store.
translations.hypothesis: It is important to note that currency exchange services are only available at one bank branch on those islands, which can be found within the Stanley area, accessible through the FIC West store.

translations.source: A ga-anabata n’izugbe pam ndị Britenụ ebe ọbụla n’ime agwaetiti ndị ahụ ma na gburugburu ụmụ kaadị mbiri ego Stanley na dọla mba Amerịka sokwa na ndị a na-anabata.
translations.reference: British pounds will generally be accepted anywhere in the islands and within Stanley credit cards and United States dollars are also often accepted.
translations.hypothesis: British pounds are widely accepted throughout the islands, as are credit cards, particularly Visa and Mastercard, and US dollars are also commonly accepted.

translations.source: N’agwaetiti ndị nọ na mpụga ebe ahụ ụmụ kaadị akwụmụgwọ nwere ike a gaghị anabata ya, n’agbanyeghị na enwere ike iwe ego Britenụ na United States; leru anya na ndị nwe ya n’ọdịnihu iji chọpụta ihe bụ ụzọ nkwụmụgwọ a na-anabata.
translations.reference: On the outlying islands credit cards will probably not be accepted, although British and United States currency may be taken; check with the owners in advance to determine what is an acceptable payment method.
translations.hypothesis: For those living abroad, it may be difficult to obtain a birth certificate, even if they can provide British or American currency; therefore, it is important for future parents to research and determine the accepted methods of payment.

translations.source: Ọ na-ara ezigbote ahụ ịgbanwe ego Falklands ma e si n'agwaetiti a pụọ, ya mere gbanwee ego gi tupu i si na ya pụọ.
translations.reference: It is nearly impossible to exchange Falklands currency outside of the islands, so exchange money prior to leaving the islands.
translations.hypothesis: It's important to exchange currency before leaving the Falkland Islands, so be sure to do so before you depart.

translations.source: Ebe Montevideo dị na ndịda Iquetọ, ọ bụ oge ọkọchị ebe ahụ mgbe oge oyi dị na Ebe ugwu Emisfee ma n'otu aka ahụ.
translations.reference: Since Montevideo is south of the Equator, it is summer there when it's winter in the Northern Hemisphere and vice versa.
translations.hypothesis: Montevideo, located in the Southern Hemisphere, experiences summer during the winter months in the Northern Hemisphere, including in the region of Emisfee.

translations.source: Montevideo nọ n'ime ebe na-ekpọ ọkụ ma jụọkwa oyi; n'ime ụmụ ọnwa ọkọchị, okpomọkụ gafere +30°C bụ ihe nkịtị.
translations.reference: Montevideo is in the subtropics; in the summer months, temperatures above +30°C are common.
translations.hypothesis: Montevideo experiences both hot summers and cold winters; during the summer months, temperatures often exceed +30°C.

translations.source: Oge oyi nwere ike ịjụ ezigbo oyi n'aghụghọ: okpomọkụ na-ara ahụ tupu ya gaa n'okpuru ịghọ okwute mmiri, mana ikuku na oruru mmiri na-abịakọta ọnụ ime ka o nwee mmetụta kara jụọ oyi karịa ihe temometa kwuru.
translations.reference: The winter can be deceptively chilly: temperatures rarely go below freezing, but the wind and humidity combine to make it feel colder than what the thermometer says.
translations.hypothesis: Cold weather can sometimes feel much colder than the thermometer indicates: the temperature might be relatively mild before it drops below freezing, but the combination of wind and humidity creates a situation where the perceived cold is significantly greater than what the thermometer reads.

translations.source: Enweghị ihe dị ka "udu mmiri" na "ọkọchị": ogo mmiri ozuzo na-anọkarị otu ebe ogologo afọ niile.
translations.reference: There are no particular "rainy" and "dry" seasons: the amount of rain stays roughly the same throughout the year.
translations.hypothesis: There's no such thing as a "water well" or a "bicycle": rainfall patterns tend to remain consistent in a particular location over many years.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị na ọ maala ahụ ọtụtụ n'ime ụmụ anụmanụ nọ n'obianụmanụ ịhụ ndị mmadụ, ka o sina dị anụ ọhịa bụ nke azụghịazụ ma e kwesịghị inye ha nri ma ọ bụ nye ha nsogbu.
translations.reference: Though many of the animals in the park are used to seeing humans, the wildlife is nonetheless wild and should not be fed or disturbed.
translations.hypothesis: While many of the animals in the sanctuary are accustomed to seeing people, the wild animals are still skittish and should not be fed or approached.

translations.source: Site n'aka ndị na-ahụ maka ogige anụmanụ, nọtee aka opekata mpe yadị maọbụ mita 100 n'ebe anụ ọhịa bea na wulfu nọ na yadị maọbụ mita 25 n'ebe anụ ọhịa ndị ọzọ niile nọ!
translations.reference: According to park authorities, stay at least 100 yards/meters away from bears and wolves and 25 yards/meters from all other wild animals!
translations.hypothesis: According to animal welfare guidelines, keep a minimum distance of at least 100 yards (approximately 90 meters) from wild animals like deer and wolves, and a distance of at least 25 yards (approximately 23 meters) from all other wild animals!

translations.source: Agbanyeghị etu ha siri dị nwayọọ, bison, elk, muuz, bea, na anụmanụ ukwu niile nwere ike iluso ọgụ.
translations.reference: No matter how docile they may look, bison, elk, moose, bears, and nearly all large animals can attack.
translations.hypothesis: Despite their size, bison, elk, moose, bears, and other large animals are all capable of fighting.

translations.source: Afọ ọ bụla, a na-emerụ ọtụtụ ndị nleta ahụ n'ihi na ha enyeghị ezigbo ohere. Ụmụ anụmanụ ndị a buru ibu, azụghịazụ, ma nweekkwa ike ịbụ ihe ize ndụ, ya mere nye ha ohere.
translations.reference: Each year, dozens of visitors are injured because they didn't keep a proper distance. These animals are large, wild, and potentially dangerous, so give them their space.
translations.hypothesis: Every year, many visitors are injured because they do not give way to others. These large, slow-moving vehicles can be dangerous, so please yield to them.

translations.source: Na mgbakwunye, mara amara na usi na adọta ụmụ bea na anụ ọhịa ndị ọzọ, ya mere zere ibu ma ọ bụ isi ụmụ nri na-esi usi ma debe kampụ dị ọcha.
translations.reference: In addition, be aware that odors attract bears and other wildlife, so avoid carrying or cooking odorous foods and keep a clean camp.
translations.hypothesis: In addition, be aware that some types of fish and wild game can carry parasites, so avoid consuming raw or undercooked meat and ensure that all food is properly cooked.

translations.source: Apia bụ isi obodo Samoa. Obodo ahụ nọ n'agwaetiti Upolu ma ma nwee ngụpụta mmadụ nke ji obere ihe ghara eru 40,000.
translations.reference: Apia is the capital of Samoa. The town is on the island of Upolu and has a population of just under 40,000.
translations.hypothesis: Apia is the capital city of Samoa. The city is located on the island of Upolu and has a population of just under 40,000.

translations.source: E kepụtara Apịa n'afọ ndị 1850; kemgbe 1959, ọ bụ isi obodo Samoa.
translations.reference: Apia was founded in the 1850s and has been the official capital of Samoa since 1959.
translations.hypothesis: Apia was established in the 1850s; since 1959, it has been the capital of Samoa.

translations.source: Ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ahụ bụ ebe nguzosike nke ndị agha mmiri wuru ewu na 1889 mgbe nnukwu ụgbọ mmiri asaa si Jamani, US, na Briten jụrụ ịhapụ ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ahụ.
translations.reference: The harbor was the site of an infamous naval standoff in 1889 when seven ships from Germany, the US, and Britain refused to leave the harbor.
translations.hypothesis: The pier is a historic site where warships were built in 1889, after seven large warships from Germany, the United States, and Britain refused to leave the pier.

translations.source: Nnukwu ụgbọ mmiri niile ndị ahụ miri, ewezụga otu ụgbọ agha Ndị Briten. Ọ fọrọ obere ka o ruo Ndị Amerịka na Ndị Jamani 200 nwụrụnụ.
translations.reference: All the ships were sunk, except for one British cruiser. Nearly 200 American and German lives were lost.
translations.hypothesis: All those large ships that were present, including a British warship, caused significant damage. It took a relatively short time for 200 Americans and Germans to perish.

translations.source: N'oge mgba maka nnwereonwe nke a haziri site n'aka ngagharị Mau, otu nzukọ keudo n'ime obodo rụpụtara n'ogbugbu nke ezigbo onyeisi Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.reference: During the struggle for independence organised by the Mau movement, a peaceful gathering in the town resulted in the killing of the paramount chief Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.hypothesis: During this period of political turmoil, orchestrated by the Mau movement, a coalition of groups within the city rose up in defiance of the legitimate leader, Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.

translations.source: E nwere ọtụtụ ọnụ mmiri, n’ihi nnọnetiti nke Ọklandị nke ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri abụọ. Ndị nke kacha ewu ewu nọ n’ebe atọ.
translations.reference: There are many beaches, due to Auckland's straddling of two harbours. The most popular ones are in three areas.
translations.hypothesis: There are many fountains, due to the presence of two large ports in Oakland. The most famous one is located in three places.

translations.source: Akụkụ mmiri Ọnụmmiri Ugwu (nọ na mpaghara Ugwu Ebe ndote ụgbọ mmiri) nọ n’oke osimiri Pacifik ma dọtịa site na Long Bay nọ n’ugwu ruo Devonport nọ na ndịda.
translations.reference: North Shore beaches (in North Harbour district) are on the Pacific Ocean and stretch from Long Bay in the north to Devonport in the south.
translations.hypothesis: The Auckland Harbour Bridge (located in the Auckland region, near the waterfront) spans the Waitematā Harbour and connects the North Shore with the city center, stretching from Long Bay in the north to Devonport in the south.

translations.source: Ha niile fọrọ obere ka ha bụrụchaa akụkụ mmiri aja aja ya na igwu mmiri echedoro echedo, ma ọtụtụ n'ime ha nwere ndo enyere site n'aka ụmụ osisi pohutukawa.
translations.reference: They are almost all sandy beaches with safe swimming, and most have shade provided by pohutukawa trees.
translations.hypothesis: They were all small, nestled amongst the silvery-grey leaves of the protected water garden, but many of them were sheltered by the branches of the pohutukawa trees.

translations.source: Ụmụ akụkụ mmiri Tamaki Drive nọ n’Ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri Waitemata ahụ, n’ime ahịa ndị bara ụba nọ mpaghara ebe obibi nke Mission Bay na St Heliers n’ime Central Auckland.
translations.reference: Tamaki Drive beaches are on the Waitemata Harbour, in the upmarket suburbs of Mission Bay and St Heliers in Central Auckland.
translations.hypothesis: The Tamaki Drive apartments are located at the Waitemata Harbour, within a vibrant area that includes the residential neighborhoods of Mission Bay and St Heliers, in central Auckland.

translations.source: Ebe ndị a bụ mgbe ụfọdụ akụkụ mmiri ezinụlọ ndị mmadụ juru ya n’ọtụtụ ụdị ụlọ ahịa nọ n’ogologo ọnụ mmiri ahụ. Igwu mmiri dị mma.
translations.reference: These are sometimes-crowded family beaches with a good range of shops lining the shore. Swimming is safe.
translations.hypothesis: These are some of the water features that families can enjoy in various shops along the waterfront. The fountains are beautiful.

translations.source: Isi biya imeobodo ahụ bụ 'Number One', ọ bụghị biya na-agbagwoju anya, mana dị mma n'ahụ ma na-edo ahụ nke ọma. Biya imeobodo nke ọzọ bụ nke a na-akpọ "Manta".
translations.reference: The main local beer is 'Number One', it is not a complex beer, but pleasant and refreshing. The other local beer is called "Manta".
translations.hypothesis: The primary type of traditional Igbo clothing is called "Number One," which isn't a confusing name, but rather a term that signifies its high quality and comfortable fit. Another popular type of traditional Igbo clothing is called "Manta."

translations.source: Enwere ọtụtụ mmanya si Frans mmadụ ga-aṅụ, mana mmanya Niu Ziland na Ọstrelia ga-aka mma maka njem.
translations.reference: There are many French wines to be had, but the New Zealand and Australian wines might travel better.
translations.hypothesis: There are many types of alcoholic beverages that people can drink, but New Zealand and Australian wines are particularly well-suited for travel.

translations.source: Mmiri mgbata ebeụlọ dị mma nke ọma ịn̄ụ, mana mmiri bọtụlụ dị mfe ịchọta ma ọ bụrụ na ụjọ na-atụ gị.
translations.reference: The local tap water is perfectly safe to drink, but bottled water is easy to find if you are fearful.
translations.hypothesis: The tap water in this area is generally safe to drink, but bottled water is readily available and a good option if you are concerned.

translations.source: Maka ndị Australia, kọfị 'flat white' bụ ihe ala ọzọ. Shọt blak bụ 'espresso', cappuccino na-ebu nnukwu krim abịa (ọ bụghị froth), ha na-añụ tii na-etinyeghị mmiri ara ehi.
translations.reference: For Australians, the idea of 'flat white' coffee is foreign. A short black is 'espresso', cappuccino comes heaped high with cream (not froth), and tea is served without milk.
translations.hypothesis: For Australians, a "flat white" coffee is a common beverage. A "short black" is an espresso, a cappuccino has a generous amount of milk foam (not just froth), and they typically drink tea without milk.

translations.source: Chokoleeti ọkụ a ruru ogo nke Beljiọm. Mmanya mkpụrụ osisi dị ọnụ mana ha amaka.
translations.reference: The hot chocolate is up to Belgian standards. Fruit juices are pricey but excellent.
translations.hypothesis: This hot chocolate is of Belgian quality. The ingredients are expensive, but the taste is exquisite.

translations.source: A na-eme ọtụtụ njem ịga na ime ala osimiri gburugburu afọ niile, ma mmerụ ahụ n'ihi otu n'ime ihe mkpata ndị a n'ime ala osimiri ahụ na-ara ahụ inweta.
translations.reference: Many trips to the reef are made all year around, and injuries due to any of these causes on the reef are rare.
translations.hypothesis: Throughout the year, numerous expeditions are conducted to explore the seabed, but injuries resulting from one of these underwater hazards are unfortunately common.

translations.source: N’agbanyeghị, were ndụmọdụ si n'aka ndị nọ n’ọchịchị, rube isi n’ihe ntụaka niile, ma gee ntị nke ọma maka ịdọ aka na ntị nke nchekwa.
translations.reference: Still, take advice from authorities, obey all signs, and pay close attention to safety warnings.
translations.hypothesis: Despite everything, heed the advice of those in authority, be cautious in all your endeavors, and pay close attention to any warnings regarding safety.

translations.source: Azụjelii igbe na-apụta n'akụkụ ọnụ osimiri ma n'ụso ụmụ njekọta osimiri site n'Ọktoba ruo Eprel ugwu nke 1770. E nwekwara ike ịhụ ha mgbe ụfọdụ n'oge ndị ọzọ n'abụghị oge ndị a.
translations.reference: Box jellyfish occur near beaches and near river estuaries from October to April north of 1770. They can occasionally be found outside these times.
translations.hypothesis: These fish appear near the coast and are caught by fishermen from October to the middle of April, starting in 1770. They can also sometimes be found during other times of the year, although not as frequently.

translations.source: Shaakị gasị dị adị, otú ọ dị, ha adịkarịghị awakpo ụmụ mmadụ. Imirikiti shaakị na-atụ ụmụ mmadụ egwu yana ga-egwu mmiri pụọ.
translations.reference: Sharks do exist, however they rarely attack humans. Most sharks are scared of humans and would swim away.
translations.hypothesis: While snakes are often feared, they rarely pose a threat to humans. Most snakes are shy and will try to avoid contact.

translations.source: Agụiyi mmiri nnu anaghị ebikewe n'ime oke osimiri, ebe ha na-ebikarị bụ na ngwọkọta osimiri na mmiri nnu dị n'ugwu sitere na Rọkhamptịn.
translations.reference: Saltwater Crocodiles do not actively live in the ocean, their primary habitat is in river estuaries north from Rockhampton.
translations.hypothesis: Oil slicks are not typically found within the ocean itself; instead, they usually appear in coastal areas or where rivers and streams, carrying oil from upstream sources like Rockhampton, flow into the sea.

translations.source: Itinye akwụkwọ n’ọdịnihu na-enye onye njem ahụ obi udo na ha nwere ebe ha ga-arahụ ụra ozugbo ha rutere ebe ha na-aga.
translations.reference: Booking in advance gives the traveller peace of mind that they will have somewhere to sleep once they arrive at their destination.
translations.hypothesis: Booking accommodation in advance gives the traveler peace of mind, knowing they have a place to stay as soon as they arrive at their destination.

translations.source: Ndị nnọchi anya ndị njem na-enwekarị nkwekọ azụmahịa ha na kpọmkwem ụmụ họteelụ, agbanyeghị na ị nwere ike ịhụ na o kwere omume itinye akwụkwọ maka ụdị nnabata ndị ọzọ, dị ka ala ebe a na-ama ụlọikwu, sitere n'otu onye nnọchite anya njem.
translations.reference: Travel agents often have deals with specific hotels, although you may find it possible to book other forms of accommodation, like camping grounds, through a travel agent.
translations.hypothesis: Travel agents often have agreements with specific hotels, but it is still possible to request different types of accommodations, such as rooms with specific views, through a travel agent.

translations.source: Ndị nnọchi anya ndị njem na-enyekarị ụmụ ngwungwu na-agụnye nri ụtụtụ, nhazi ụzọ esi eje njem ịga na/site na ọdụ ụgbọelu ma ọ bụ njem ụgbọelu etikọrọ ọnụ ya na ụmụ ngwungwu họteelụ.
translations.reference: Travel agents usually offer packages that include breakfast, transportation arrangements to/from the airport or even combined flight and hotel packages.
translations.hypothesis: Travel agents often provide luggage storage services for travelers, including options for storing luggage overnight, arranging transportation to and from the airport or train station, and coordinating luggage transfers with hotels.

translations.source: Ha nwekwara ike idobere gị ohere a ma ọ bụrụ na ị ka chọrọ oge ịtụgharị uche na ya maọbụ ịnweta akwụkwọ ndị ọzọ maka ebe ị na-aga (ọmụmaatụ: visa).
translations.reference: They can also hold the reservation for you if you need time to think about the offer or procure other documents for your destination (e.g. visa).
translations.hypothesis: They may also be able to grant you this extension if you still need more time to process the application or obtain other documents required for your travel (for example, a visa).

translations.source: Ihe ọbụla a chọrọ ịgbanwe maọbụ ịna, ọ bụ onye ejenti njem ka a ga-ebu ụzọ gakwuru; ọ bụghị họteelụ n'onwe ya.
translations.reference: Any amendments or requests though should be coursed through the travel agent first and not directly with the hotel.
translations.hypothesis: This property is not a hotel; it is a travel agency that will arrange your trip. It is not a hotel itself.

translations.source: Maka ụfọdụ mmemme, nnukwu ọtụtụ n’ime ndị bịara na mmemme egwu ahụ kpebiri ịnọ na kampụ n’ebe ahụ, ma ọtụtụ n’ime ndị bịara na-ewe ya otu akụkụ dị oke mkpa nke ahụmihe ahụ.
translations.reference: For some festivals, the vast majority of the attendants to music festivals decide to camp on site, and most attendants consider it a vital part of the experience.
translations.hypothesis: For some attendees, a significant number of whom chose to stay in the nearby campground, the experience of being there was a crucial part of the event.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ị chọrọ ịnọ nso na emereme ahụ ị ga-ekwesị ịbanye ọsịịsọ iji nweta otu ebe a na-ama ụlọikwu nọ nso n'egwu ahụ.
translations.reference: If you want to be close to the action you're going to have to get in early to get a camping site close to the music.
translations.hypothesis: If you want to be close to the stage, you should enter through the side entrance to access a seating area that is near the performance.

translations.source: Cheta na obu ezie na egwu ogbo-egwu nwere ike gwula, enwere ike inwe mpaghara mmeme ahu gana aku egwu ruo ime abali.
translations.reference: Remember that even though music on the main stages may have finished, there may be sections of the festival that will keep playing music until late into the night.
translations.hypothesis: While traditional Igbo music can be lively and energetic, it's also possible to have more subdued and gentle musical performances that can last for hours.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ ememme nwere ebe ndị a na-ama ụlọikwuu pụrụ iche maka ezinụlọ nke nwere ụmụ na-eto eto.
translations.reference: Some festivals have special camping areas for families with young children.
translations.hypothesis: Some events have special areas designed for families with teenagers.

translations.source: Mgbe ị na-agafe Ebe ugwu Baltic n’oge oyi, lelee ebe kabịn ahụ, dị ka ịgafe okwute mmiri na-akpata mkpọtụ dị nnọọ egwu maka ndị ọ kacha metụta.
translations.reference: If crossing the Northern Baltic in winter, check the cabin location, as going through ice causes quite horrible noise for those most affected.
translations.hypothesis: When traveling through the Baltic region during the winter, be mindful of the ice, as crossing frozen bodies of water can be extremely dangerous, especially for those most vulnerable.

translations.source: Njem nnyagharị nke Senti Piitasbọg gụnyere oge n'ime obodo. Ndị njem nke njem nnyagharị bụ ndị ewezụgara site n'ụmụ ihe ndị achọrọ maka visa (lelee usoro ahụ).
